meta.title: Have rules in the agent instructions to auto document decisions

before.body:
## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Make decision documentation a routine part of the agent protocol so consequential project choices and their reasoning are retained beyond the originating ticket.

### Scope and approach

Update tool-neutral agent guidance, generated context, and MCP onboarding to instruct agents to look up existing decisions and create/update decision records when choosing a meaningful architecture, product behavior, UI convention, dependency strategy, or workflow policy. Keep routine implementation trivia out of the decision log.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Instructions state when to record a decision, with examples of consequential choices versus minor implementation details.
- [ ] A decision records the choice, context, rationale, alternatives considered, tradeoffs, scope, attribution, and links to relevant tickets/references.
- [ ] Agents search existing decisions before creating another, link tickets to the applicable decision, and supersede earlier decisions explicitly rather than rewriting away the old rationale.
- [ ] Unresolved proposals and assumptions are labeled as such; an agent does not invent human agreement or treat an unresolved question as an accepted choice.
- [ ] Agents may record decisions within approved work, but decision records do not grant implementation scope approval or bypass human acceptance of tickets.
- [ ] Review handoffs identify decisions made or changed, and agents can retrieve those records after the originating ticket is archived.
- [ ] The instructions ship consistently in AGENT_GUIDE.md, generated context, and MCP guidance; users can see the rule in the playbook from #26.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with AGENT_GUIDE.md, src/store.ts contextMarkdown and decision validation, src/mcp.ts onboarding/list_knowledge, and existing record create/update APIs. Reuse durable decision records and predecessor links. This is protocol-driven behavior, not automatic inference from arbitrary file changes.

### Human review / verification

Run a disposable agent workflow that makes a meaningful design choice, records its alternatives/rationale, links it to the ticket, and later supersedes it. Confirm the guidance is available through CLI/MCP context and that archived work does not hide its decisions.

meta.handoff: Hardened the screenshot connection-failure path shown in image-9019d4a9b5090ca7. Read-only API requests retry transient connection failures up to twice, including interrupted response bodies. Permission messages remain distinct, metadata fetches recover without refreshing, and beginning another image upload clears an old upload error.

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Break down a parent ticket into real child tickets directly inside its detail dialog, using a title field and Enter for each child. Keep the parent open and the input ready for the next title.

### Scope and approach

Add a Children section with quick entry and links to existing children. Use the project’s configured intake/backlog default and show the destination. For a new unsaved parent, save it successfully before persisting children; retain pending titles if that save fails. Checklist items are handled separately in #20.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Entering a nonblank title and pressing Enter creates one numbered ticket with the current ticket as its parent; no questionnaire is required.
- [ ] Repeated entry retains focus and supports several children without closing the parent; whitespace and repeated submission while saving do not create duplicates.
- [ ] The child appears immediately in the Children section and under its parent on a parent-grouped board.
- [ ] Creation failures retain the title and give a retryable error. Closing the parent follows existing save behavior.
- [ ] Child creation preserves agent scope rules, and completing children never automatically completes the parent.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with web/RecordDetail.tsx (existing child list), web/QuickTicket.tsx, and src/store.ts create/relationship validation. Reuse quick entry; coordinate the parent chooser with #15.

### Human review / verification

Create several children from an existing parent and from a newly drafted parent. Open a child, reload, and confirm its title, number, parent, and stage. Exercise a failed save and keyboard-only entry.

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

When a human opens a ticket in Review, make Accept into Done and Request changes immediately available without changing a status dropdown.

### Scope and approach

Add prominent, distinct review outcome buttons in ticket detail, alongside the review summary and conversation. Request changes should target the configured Failed Review column when available; otherwise use an explicit project setting or visible choice of an appropriate progress column. Keep naming aligned with the board actions in #16.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] For a Review ticket, a human sees Accept into Done and Request changes with the destination clearly indicated; these do not appear as active agent acceptance actions.
- [ ] Accept into Done saves any pending ticket edits and moves to the configured Done destination using current revision checks.
- [ ] Request changes allows a concise review comment, saves it as human Review feedback, and moves the ticket to the configured return stage; submitting does not require a long questionnaire.
- [ ] If a save or transition fails, the ticket remains open with the draft/feedback retained and a clear error; retry does not duplicate feedback.
- [ ] A successful action closes the dialog consistently with Save and updates the board immediately, retaining previous handoff and verification history.
- [ ] Multiple custom Review/Done/progress columns are handled by explicit deterministic destination rules, and accepting a parent never silently accepts its children.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with web/RecordDetail.tsx save/close/review actions, src/store.ts authority/history, and project column configuration. Related: #16 provides quick actions outside the dialog; #18 handles status customization. Share action logic to avoid divergent validation.

### Human review / verification

Open a reviewed ticket, accept it and observe the board; repeat with Request changes and a comment. Test pending edits, a stale save, renamed columns, and missing Failed Review configuration. Check attribution and preservation of the review conversation.

## Choice

Name the local authentication cookie with the stable project ID. Each project keeps its existing token and loopback service.

## Context and rationale

Browser cookies are shared across ports on the same host. The previous common cookie name let opening a second Control Room project overwrite the first project’s session. Both Control Room Dev and JuiceLab run on 127.0.0.1.

## Alternatives and tradeoffs

Separate hostnames require more local setup; storing a bearer token in browser JavaScript would change the security model. Project-specific HttpOnly cookies preserve the existing model and allow concurrent projects. A refresh establishes the new cookie after an upgrade. Tokens are still checked by each service; attribution labels do not become a security boundary.

## Attribution and scope

Codex fixes, implementation decision within approved ticket #39. Applies to local browser session isolation. No separate human agreement is claimed, and this record grants no scope approval or Done authority.

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started. Proposed behavior below remains subject to human scope review.

### Intended outcome

Clear completed tickets from the active board quickly, while keeping their history easy to browse and restore.

### Scope and approach

Add an Archive completed tickets action to a Done-status column header. Proposed first-release behavior: archive only unarchived tickets in that column that match the current view/search filters, across its visible groups. Before applying, show the exact count and scope, with a way to inspect the affected tickets. Provide an obvious Archived tickets view with search and an Unarchive action.

Unarchiving returns a ticket to the active board in its existing workflow stage (usually Done); moving it back into development remains a separate explicit action. Archiving a parent does not implicitly archive its children. This is a focused implementation follow-up to #23; it need not wait for every clutter-management recommendation.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A Done-role column offers the archive action, including renamed/custom Done columns; non-Done columns do not silently offer the same completed-work operation.
- [ ] The preview names the column, filter scope and affected ticket count. Empty sets are harmless; cancel changes nothing. Tickets outside the preview are never archived.
- [ ] Each write uses the previewed ticket revision. Concurrent changes are rejected for that ticket, with clear success/failure counts and a refresh/review path; no stale record is overwritten.
- [ ] Archived tickets disappear from ordinary active views and remain searchable in an explicitly labeled archive view.
- [ ] A ticket can be opened and unarchived from the archive view. Its status, number, prose, comments, attachments, decisions and parent/child links survive the round trip.
- [ ] Archiving preserves decision/rule discovery and does not delete local screenshots or implicitly archive linked records.
- [ ] The action and archive navigation work with keyboard input, and the chosen scope stays explicit when filters or column visibility change.

Reuse the existing archived metadata and is:archived filtering in web/model.ts and the detail Unarchive action. ## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started. Proposed behavior below remains subject to human scope review.

### Intended outcome

Opening a ticket from Needs you immediately shows the question to answer or the review action to take, without searching a long conversation. Put manual test/feedback instructions beside Accept/Reject.

### Scope and approach

Add a prominent action area near the top of ticket details and conversation views, aligned with the existing review controls. Surface all unresolved questions with their author and original context, with an answer action and a link to the original thread entry. Render this from the existing question records rather than creating duplicate comments. Show the same action area when opening the ticket directly so the need for attention does not depend on the entry route.

For Review tickets, display the current submission's human review instructions, relevant handoff and verification summary beside Accept/Reject. If the submission explicitly requires no manual checks and recorded verification supports it, say the test suite passed and offer the evidence. Never infer a pass or invent manual checks from missing instructions; missing/failed/unrun verification must be clearly labeled.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Opening a question-bearing ticket from Needs you shows the unresolved question text near the top, regardless of conversation sort order or length.
- [ ] Multiple unresolved questions remain individually identifiable with attribution, links to their original entries and a straightforward answer path. Long content can expand without concealing the existence of other questions.
- [ ] Posting an answer uses the existing durable conversation and retains the draft on failure; resolving a question is explicit and affects only that question. Merely opening a ticket never resolves it.
- [ ] Resolving/reopening a question updates the top area and Needs you after refresh; review instructions remain visible if the ticket also awaits review.
- [ ] Review instructions and requested feedback appear beside the existing Accept/Reject controls, with accessible Markdown and useful links. Acceptance feedback continues to work as implemented in #30.
- [ ] The summary reflects the latest review submission and distinguishes manual checks, successful automated verification, failures, exceptions and missing evidence. An old passing result is not presented as proof of a newer unverified submission.
- [ ] When no manual checks are explicitly required and the current submission has passing verification, concise text says the test suite passed, with access to its recorded command/result. Otherwise the UI states what is requested or unknown truthfully.
- [ ] Needs you remains actionable until all applicable attention reasons are addressed; resolving one question does not hide another question or a pending review.
- [ ] Keyboard and compact-screen users can reach the question/answer and review controls without losing unsaved ticket or reply drafts.

### Implementation notes and related work

Inspect web/Pages.tsx AttentionPage, web/model.ts attention reasons, web/RecordDetail.tsx question comments and review data, and web/ReviewActions.tsx. Use existing handoff, review instructions and verification records; clarify current-submission evidence association during implementation if needed. Related: #30 optional review feedback, #32 conversation ordering, #27 future structured questionnaires. This ticket does not require implementing the full questionnaire system.

### Human review / verification

Open a ticket with two unanswered questions deep in a long conversation; answer and resolve one, then verify the other remains prominent. Test a Review ticket with manual steps, one explicitly requiring only recorded automated checks, and one with missing/failed verification. Check that a fresh review submission cannot inherit a misleading old pass summary.

## Visual feedback

[![Screenshot](/api/images/image-ba7623ff65d116a9/base)](#image=image-ba7623ff65d116a9)

- [ ] A1 (note-d0faa9fc-2c69-47fb-961e-0cb7aaaba320): Clicking the button should popup a prompt for name for ticket and then open up the new ticket as a popup so I can add any details. 

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started. Proposed behavior remains subject to human scope review.

### Intended outcome

Click Save to ticket, enter a short ticket title in a focused prompt, and immediately open the created ticket in the centered detail popup to add further details. Preserve the screenshot and annotations throughout. Source: screenshot annotation A1 (note-d0faa9fc-2c69-47fb-961e-0cb7aaaba320).

### Scope and approach

For the single-new-ticket path, make Save to ticket open a small in-app title dialog instead of silently creating a generically named ticket. Prefill from any title already entered, select/focus the text for quick replacement, and support Enter to create and Escape/Cancel to return to the annotation editor. Require a nonblank trimmed title; no additional questionnaire.

After saving the annotations and creating the ticket successfully, use the returned ticket ID to open its normal detail dialog. The title prompt is the single authoritative title entry; remove or synchronize the existing inline title field to avoid competing values. Keep attachment-to-existing-ticket and split-annotation workflows distinct, without introducing a single-title prompt into those paths. New tickets use the project's normal initial stage, currently Concept.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Save to ticket in new-ticket mode opens an accessible, focused title prompt before creating a ticket. Typing a title and pressing Enter creates it; whitespace-only input is rejected inline.
- [ ] Cancel/Escape creates no ticket, returns focus to the editor, and preserves the screenshot and unsaved annotation draft.
- [ ] On success, the editor/title prompt hands off to the centered detail popup for the exact newly created ticket. Its heading matches the entered title and the ticket URL identifies it.
- [ ] The description contains the screenshot preview and written annotation instructions with stable annotation references. Base image, editable geometry and attachment links remain intact and available to agent context.
- [ ] The user can add description/details immediately. Save or clicking outside uses existing save-and-close behavior; a failed save retains the draft and explains the error.
- [ ] While submission is pending, repeated clicks/Enter cannot create multiple tickets. Annotation-save or creation failures retain the title and annotations, show a useful error, and do not claim success.
- [ ] Once creation succeeds, a later refresh/navigation failure offers reopening the returned ticket rather than creating another. Uncertain write results are not automatically replayed.
- [ ] Saving a standalone screenshot still creates no ticket. Attaching to an existing ticket and splitting annotations retain their current explicitly selected destinations and behavior.
- [ ] Keyboard focus transfers correctly between editor, title prompt and ticket detail, including on narrow screens; there is no inaccessible stack of active modal dialogs.

### Implementation notes and related work

Inspect attach() in web/AnnotationEditor.tsx: the new-ticket branch currently posts a record, reloads, then closes without using the created record to open details. Coordinate the transition with web/App.tsx, web/RecordDetail.tsx and web/ticketNavigation.ts. Retain revision checks when saving annotations; use the existing imageMarkdown and annotation content rather than inventing a second attachment format. Related: #35 screenshot conversations, #39 description thumbnails and #42 ticket URLs. No new native capture or batch-split redesign is needed.

### Human review / verification

Capture or open a screenshot, add annotations, click Save to ticket, enter a title and confirm. Verify the resulting ticket opens with the correct title, preview and instructions; add details, close and reopen to check persistence. Also try cancel, blank title, repeated submission and a simulated save failure, then check standalone save and existing-ticket attachment still work.

meta.handoff: Fixed a reproduced cross-project authentication bug: browser cookies share a host across ports, so the old common cookie name caused projects to overwrite each other’s sessions. Cookies now use the stable project ID. State reads coalesce concurrent refresh triggers, have bounded timeouts/retries, retain displayed work during outages, and retry on returning to the tab or Reconnect now. No mutation requests are automatically replayed. Screenshot-created tickets embed their screenshot in description Markdown; existing attachment-only descriptions show a thumbnail without rewriting their prose. Refreshed both Control Room Dev and JuiceLab installations and verified simultaneous authenticated reads with both cookies present. Decision: DEC-5d6d97f61404555b — Isolate local browser sessions by project.
meta.evidence: Production build/typecheck and 56 core/model/integration tests passed. All 50 browser workflows passed across the full regression run and focused reruns after fixing test timing/selector/legacy-opening assumptions. New coverage is in tests/browser/latest-feedback.spec.ts and tests/project-sessions.test.ts. Expanded dialog visually inspected; desktop/mobile geometry and footer accessibility verified. Live session check passed with both Control Room Dev (4173) and JuiceLab (4280) cookies present. JuiceLab upgrade preserved record hashes and its custom launcher. Details in VALIDATION.md. Changes remain uncommitted.
meta.reviewInstructions:
1. Refresh both http://127.0.0.1:4173 and http://127.0.0.1:4280. Switch between them and open/edit tickets: opening one project should no longer invalidate the other session.

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Break down a parent ticket into real child tickets directly inside its detail dialog, using a title field and Enter for each child. Keep the parent open and the input ready for the next title.

### Scope and approach

Add a Children section with quick entry and links to existing children. Use the project’s configured intake/backlog default and show the destination. For a new unsaved parent, save it successfully before persisting children; retain pending titles if that save fails. Checklist items are handled separately in #20.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Entering a nonblank title and pressing Enter creates one numbered ticket with the current ticket as its parent; no questionnaire is required.
- [ ] Repeated entry retains focus and supports several children without closing the parent; whitespace and repeated submission while saving do not create duplicates.
- [ ] The child appears immediately in the Children section and under its parent on a parent-grouped board.
- [ ] Creation failures retain the title and give a retryable error. Closing the parent follows existing save behavior.
- [ ] Child creation preserves agent scope rules, and completing children never automatically completes the parent.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with web/RecordDetail.tsx (existing child list), web/QuickTicket.tsx, and src/store.ts create/relationship validation. Reuse quick entry; coordinate the parent chooser with #15.

### Human review / verification

Create several children from an existing parent and from a newly drafted parent. Open a child, reload, and confirm its title, number, parent, and stage. Exercise a failed save and keyboard-only entry.

Ability to add microtasks to a ticket

before.body:
These are just small tasks that are tracked inside the ticket and don't show up as separate full tickets. Sort of like a checklist of things that need to be done for that ticket. 

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Track small steps inside a ticket with a checklist, without creating separate numbered tickets or cluttering the board.

### Scope and approach

Provide an editable Microtasks section with add, rename, reorder, complete, and remove actions. Keep it readable/editable in Markdown and include it in agent context. Reuse Markdown task-list syntax in a clearly owned section where practical; preserve other prose and existing acceptance criteria.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Enter adds a nonblank checklist item and keeps focus ready for the next; items can be checked, edited, reordered, and removed with keyboard alternatives.
- [ ] Items persist across save/reopen and direct Markdown edits; concurrent changes use revision protection.
- [ ] Agents can read and update checklist state through the supported record interfaces without creating ticket IDs for checklist items.
- [ ] The ticket displays completed/total counts, including the all-complete state; cards may show a compact count without listing every item.
- [ ] Completing the checklist does not automatically move the ticket to Done or claim its acceptance criteria are satisfied.
- [ ] Unrelated Markdown, attachments, and comments survive checklist edits.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with web/RecordDetail.tsx, web/RecordMarkdown.tsx (GFM rendering already exists), src/files.ts Markdown preservation and src/store.ts context. Related: #14 for work large enough to need child tickets; #23 for reducing board clutter.

### Human review / verification

Create/reorder/toggle items, reopen, edit a task in Markdown, and retrieve agent context. Verify a stale toggle cannot overwrite a newer edit and all-complete leaves ticket status unchanged.

meta.title: Add questionaires to tickets for human review

before.body:
If the LLM has questions about a ticket, they can add a questionaire with multiple choice questions or text questions to a ticket and mark it as needing human feedback. 

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Let an agent attach a structured questionnaire to a ticket and request human input, keeping questions and answers in the ticket’s conversation.

### Scope and approach

Support one or more multiple-choice or free-text questions, an explicit needs-feedback state, and answering at the human’s pace. Store structured data durably in Markdown records/metadata and expose it through CLI/MCP context. Keep this distinct from mandatory ticket creation forms.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An agent can submit a questionnaire with stable question IDs, clear prompts, answer types, and optional recommended choices; users can provide custom text where choices are offered.
- [ ] The ticket appears in Needs you with a direct route to its unanswered questionnaire; a separate flag does not silently change its workflow stage.
- [ ] Questions never time out or disappear because the user pauses. Draft answers persist across closing/reopening and refresh, and can be submitted explicitly.
- [ ] No recommended/preselected option counts as an answer until the human submits; required unanswered questions remain visible.
- [ ] Submitted answers retain human attribution, question wording, and timestamps in the conversation, and are readable by agent context and wait-for-update workflows.
- [ ] Question edits/replacements and amended answers retain history; stale submissions do not overwrite a newer questionnaire, and resolving one request does not clear unrelated open questions.

### Implementation notes and related work

Extend src/types.ts, src/store.ts comments/context, src/server.ts, src/cli.ts/src/mcp.ts, web/RecordDetail.tsx and web/model.ts attention handling. Reuse the existing question/resolve flow where possible. Related: #26.

### Human review / verification

Submit a mixed questionnaire, leave it unanswered beyond ordinary UI timers, save a partial draft, reload, and finish later. Confirm that an agent receives the explicit answers and that a concurrent question edit triggers reconciliation.

meta.title: More themes

before.body:
We have themes now for System, Light, and Dark. I like current theme but it would be cool to have more:
- Win95
- Win 3.1
- Commodore 64
- Classic Mac System 7
- AmigaOS
- NES
- SNES
- Synthwave
- Elektron
- Gameboy



## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Offer the requested retro and music-hardware-inspired themes while retaining the current Control Room appearance and readable, usable controls.

### Scope and approach

Treat this as an umbrella for a reusable theme structure and all requested presets: Win95, Win 3.1, Commodore 64, Classic Mac System 7, AmigaOS, NES, SNES, Synthwave, Elektron, and Gameboy. Keep System, Light, and Dark available. Develop representative previews first, then deliver presets in reviewable batches; this ticket is complete only when the agreed full set is available.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A theme picker presents clear names and previews and persists the selected theme with the existing preference model.
- [ ] Each requested preset has a coherent palette, typography, surfaces, borders, focus treatment, and semantic state colors; presets need more than a background-color swap.
- [ ] Board, table, ticket dialogs, conversation, knowledge views, menus, settings, and screenshot tools remain legible and usable in every preset.
- [ ] Keyboard focus, contrast, validation states, blocked/review states, and responsive layouts remain distinguishable without relying solely on color.
- [ ] Theme switching preserves application state and annotation geometry; System continues to follow the operating system appearance.
- [ ] Shared tokens and reusable overrides avoid duplicating application layout or behavior for each theme.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with web/styles.css tokens, web/project.css, web/TopNav.tsx themes, and web/App.tsx preference handling. Use original styling/assets inspired by the references. Create child implementation tickets when this umbrella is selected for development.

### Human review / verification

Review a consistent set of desktop/mobile screenshots for every preset and exercise keyboard focus, long content, error states, and reload persistence. Obtain visual review of representative presets before extending the full set.

meta.title: Quick Filter out swimlane

before.body:
I would like a way to click a swimlane and turn on/off the tickets in that swimline from being visible. For example backlog can be large and I want to turn off backlog and just view the other swimlanes. Maybe a little human eye icon that is in the swimlane header you can click and quickly turn on/off visibility.

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started. Proposed behavior below remains subject to human scope review.

### Intended outcome

Temporarily hide tickets in a busy status column such as Backlog with one click, then restore them just as easily.

### Scope and approach

The Backlog example refers to workflow/status columns (called swimlanes in the request). Add an eye-style visibility toggle to each column header. Hide that column's ticket content across all parent/label groups, retaining a compact labeled header or equivalent visible restore control. This is a visibility preference, not an archive or ticket-status change.

Proposed default: remember hidden column IDs per project and saved view in personal UI preferences, without rewriting the shared view's search query. Keep visibility independent of existing horizontal group collapse. Provide Show all columns and a clear indication of hidden columns.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] One click hides Backlog's cards across all groups and leaves other columns usable. A visible control restores Backlog with one click.
- [ ] Header controls expose an accessible name and pressed/expanded state, work by keyboard, and clearly distinguish hidden from empty columns.
- [ ] No ticket, claim, stage, archive flag or parent relationship changes when toggling visibility.
- [ ] Search/filter changes compose with visibility without losing the user's query. Hidden columns remain identifiable, and Show all recovers from every column being hidden.
- [ ] Visibility is remembered for that project/view after refresh without leaking to another project/view; custom column rename/reorder preserves it by stable ID, and deleted IDs are safely ignored.
- [ ] Board keyboard navigation skips hidden cards, focus stays recoverable after hiding a focused column, and hidden content cannot receive invisible drag/drop or quick-create interactions.
- [ ] Counts and any bulk-action preview make their scope clear; hidden tickets are not silently selected for operations on visible tickets.
- [ ] Table/list views retain their existing behavior; switching back to the board restores its column visibility preferences.

### Implementation notes and related work

Inspect web/BoardView.tsx column rendering and keyboard navigation, web/ProjectPage.tsx view preferences and web/model.ts filters. Related: #44 quick archive, #23 ticket clutter, #18 status customization. Do not conflate this with existing parent-group collapse or automatically create a new shared saved view.

### Human review / verification

Hide Backlog on a populated parent-grouped board, filter the remaining tickets, restore Backlog and refresh. Switch views/projects and rename a custom column. Check keyboard recovery and the all-hidden state.

Follow the setup and review recipes against a disposable project using current CLI commands. Copy a ticket-specific prompt and verify correct number/context, no secrets, and no automatic execution.

meta.title: Screenshot Save to Ticket

before.body:
## Visual feedback

[![Screenshot](/api/images/image-ba7623ff65d116a9/base)](#image=image-ba7623ff65d116a9)

- [ ] A1 (note-d0faa9fc-2c69-47fb-961e-0cb7aaaba320): Clicking the button should popup a prompt for name for ticket and then open up the new ticket as a popup so I can add any details. 

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started. Proposed behavior remains subject to human scope review.

### Intended outcome

Click Save to ticket, enter a short ticket title in a focused prompt, and immediately open the created ticket in the centered detail popup to add further details. Preserve the screenshot and annotations throughout. Source: screenshot annotation A1 (note-d0faa9fc-2c69-47fb-961e-0cb7aaaba320).

### Scope and approach

For the single-new-ticket path, make Save to ticket open a small in-app title dialog instead of silently creating a generically named ticket. Prefill from any title already entered, select/focus the text for quick replacement, and support Enter to create and Escape/Cancel to return to the annotation editor. Require a nonblank trimmed title; no additional questionnaire.

After saving the annotations and creating the ticket successfully, use the returned ticket ID to open its normal detail dialog. The title prompt is the single authoritative title entry; remove or synchronize the existing inline title field to avoid competing values. Keep attachment-to-existing-ticket and split-annotation workflows distinct, without introducing a single-title prompt into those paths. New tickets use the project's normal initial stage, currently Concept.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Save to ticket in new-ticket mode opens an accessible, focused title prompt before creating a ticket. Typing a title and pressing Enter creates it; whitespace-only input is rejected inline.
- [ ] Cancel/Escape creates no ticket, returns focus to the editor, and preserves the screenshot and unsaved annotation draft.
- [ ] On success, the editor/title prompt hands off to the centered detail popup for the exact newly created ticket. Its heading matches the entered title and the ticket URL identifies it.
- [ ] The description contains the screenshot preview and written annotation instructions with stable annotation references. Base image, editable geometry and attachment links remain intact and available to agent context.
- [ ] The user can add description/details immediately. Save or clicking outside uses existing save-and-close behavior; a failed save retains the draft and explains the error.
- [ ] While submission is pending, repeated clicks/Enter cannot create multiple tickets. Annotation-save or creation failures retain the title and annotations, show a useful error, and do not claim success.
- [ ] Once creation succeeds, a later refresh/navigation failure offers reopening the returned ticket rather than creating another. Uncertain write results are not automatically replayed.
- [ ] Saving a standalone screenshot still creates no ticket. Attaching to an existing ticket and splitting annotations retain their current explicitly selected destinations and behavior.
- [ ] Keyboard focus transfers correctly between editor, title prompt and ticket detail, including on narrow screens; there is no inaccessible stack of active modal dialogs.

### Implementation notes and related work

Inspect attach() in web/AnnotationEditor.tsx: the new-ticket branch currently posts a record, reloads, then closes without using the created record to open details. Coordinate the transition with web/App.tsx, web/RecordDetail.tsx and web/ticketNavigation.ts. Retain revision checks when saving annotations; use the existing imageMarkdown and annotation content rather than inventing a second attachment format. Related: #35 screenshot conversations, #39 description thumbnails and #42 ticket URLs. No new native capture or batch-split redesign is needed.

### Human review / verification

Capture or open a screenshot, add annotations, click Save to ticket, enter a title and confirm. Verify the resulting ticket opens with the correct title, preview and instructions; add details, close and reopen to check persistence. Also try cancel, blank title, repeated submission and a simulated save failure, then check standalone save and existing-ticket attachment still work.

meta.title: Quick Archive Swimlane

before.body:
Already experiencing effects, maybe have a way to quick archive the "Done" swimlane and also a way to go back and view past archived done tickets and unarchive return to active if possible

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started. Proposed behavior below remains subject to human scope review.

### Intended outcome

Clear completed tickets from the active board quickly, while keeping their history easy to browse and restore.

### Scope and approach

Add an Archive completed tickets action to a Done-status column header. Proposed first-release behavior: archive only unarchived tickets in that column that match the current view/search filters, across its visible groups. Before applying, show the exact count and scope, with a way to inspect the affected tickets. Provide an obvious Archived tickets view with search and an Unarchive action.

Unarchiving returns a ticket to the active board in its existing workflow stage (usually Done); moving it back into development remains a separate explicit action. Archiving a parent does not implicitly archive its children. This is a focused implementation follow-up to #23; it need not wait for every clutter-management recommendation.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A Done-role column offers the archive action, including renamed/custom Done columns; non-Done columns do not silently offer the same completed-work operation.
- [ ] The preview names the column, filter scope and affected ticket count. Empty sets are harmless; cancel changes nothing. Tickets outside the preview are never archived.
- [ ] Each write uses the previewed ticket revision. Concurrent changes are rejected for that ticket, with clear success/failure counts and a refresh/review path; no stale record is overwritten.
- [ ] Archived tickets disappear from ordinary active views and remain searchable in an explicitly labeled archive view.
- [ ] A ticket can be opened and unarchived from the archive view. Its status, number, prose, comments, attachments, decisions and parent/child links survive the round trip.
- [ ] Archiving preserves decision/rule discovery and does not delete local screenshots or implicitly archive linked records.
- [ ] The action and archive navigation work with keyboard input, and the chosen scope stays explicit when filters or column visibility change.

### Implementation notes and related work

Reuse the existing archived metadata and is:archived filtering in web/model.ts and the detail Unarchive action. Inspect web/BoardView.tsx, web/ProjectPage.tsx and revision-checked record updates in src/store.ts. Related: parent #23, #17 bulk actions, #46 column visibility. Scheduled/automatic archiving and deletion are outside this ticket.

### Human review / verification

On a fixture with completed parent/child tickets and active work, archive a filtered Done subset, find it through Archived tickets, then restore one ticket. Verify unrelated tickets and linked project knowledge remain intact. Exercise a concurrent edit during the preview to confirm it is reported rather than overwritten.

meta.title: Tickets in progress should animate and track the agents progress

before.body:
If in progress would be nice to see how long llm has worked on ticket as well as estimated progress. 

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Make in-progress work easier to monitor with restrained animation, elapsed time, and agent-reported progress that clearly communicates uncertainty.

### Scope and approach

Show current owner/claim, last reported update, elapsed time since entering In Progress, and an optional agent-reported percentage or checklist progress. Elapsed wall-clock time is not measured active work. Running-agent supervision remains outside the initial product; animation must not imply a verified live process.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Cards/rows and ticket details show last reported activity and elapsed time with explicit labels; reload reconstructs elapsed time from durable timestamps.
- [ ] Agents can report a short progress note and optional bounded percentage through CLI/MCP; percentages are labeled estimates, and missing values display as unknown rather than invented.
- [ ] Checklist completion, if shown from #20, is labeled separately from overall completion; 100% never automatically moves a ticket to Done.
- [ ] Expired claims, stale reports, and blockers are visibly distinct from recent reported activity; the UI never treats a claim alone as proof an agent is running.
- [ ] Subtle in-progress animation respects reduced-motion preferences and stops or changes appropriately for blocked/stale/review/done states.
- [ ] Repeated work sessions retain useful history; displayed elapsed duration uses a documented rule for leaving and re-entering In Progress, without double-counting or inventing active hours.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with web/TicketCard.tsx, web/TableView.tsx, src/types.ts, src/store.ts claims/history and CLI/MCP update interfaces. Prefer explicit reported data and disposable derived timers over writing a record every second. Related: #20 and #25.

### Human review / verification

Exercise a fresh report, missing estimate, stale/expired claim, blocker, and re-entry into In Progress with controlled timestamps. Reload and enable reduced motion; verify the labels never claim measured agent runtime.

before.body:
## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Offer a newest-first project activity feed so a human can quickly see what changed across tickets and project knowledge.

### Scope and approach

Add a Feed view combining meaningful ticket transitions/edits, comments, review submissions, and decision/rule changes. Reuse durable history and comments with stable event identities; keep Needs you focused on actionable items rather than replacing it.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Entries show actor, time, event type, ticket number/title or knowledge title, and a concise change summary; clicking opens the relevant record/conversation.
- [ ] New activity appears at the top while the user is at the top; when reading older items, offer a new-updates indicator without yanking scroll position.
- [ ] Refresh/reconnect does not duplicate entries; ordering is deterministic for equal timestamps and older history can be loaded incrementally.
- [ ] Filter by actor, event type, and related ticket; group noisy edits without hiding review requests or human questions.
- [ ] Durable comments and record history remain the source of truth; the feed is reconstructible and retains attribution.
- [ ] Archived-ticket events stay traceable, malformed/missing references degrade gracefully, and unrelated routine heartbeats do not flood the feed.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with src/store.ts historyFor/state/index, src/server.ts state updates, web/useProjectState.ts, web/Pages.tsx and web/TopNav.tsx. Account for current JSONL history and supported legacy events. Related: #23 and #28.

### Human review / verification

Create comments, submit review, change a rule, and update a ticket; verify newest-first attribution and deep links after reload. Test scrolling while new events arrive and loading older events without duplication.

meta.title: Need a way to merge or relate tickets in case of duplicates

before.body:
## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Connect overlapping tickets and consolidate genuine duplicates without losing their discussion, images, decisions, or history.

### Scope and approach

Support a lightweight Related tickets relationship and a separate explicit merge action that chooses a surviving ticket. Show a reviewable merge preview. Retain the source ticket as an archived duplicate pointing to the survivor rather than deleting its record; preserve original attribution and links.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Find related tickets by number/title, add or remove a relationship, and see reciprocal links in both details and agent context without treating related work as a blocking dependency.
- [ ] A merge preview identifies the survivor and source, content to preserve, and conflicts in parent, status, owner, priority, or acceptance criteria; conflicting metadata is not silently overwritten.
- [ ] The survivor retains access to source descriptions, comments, attachments/annotations, and decision/rule references with their original provenance. Existing links to the source still resolve and show the survivor.
- [ ] Source tickets are explicitly marked as duplicates and excluded from ordinary active views after merge; this does not claim the work was completed or accepted into Done.
- [ ] Incoming parent/dependency links are handled deliberately, with cycle/self-link validation, and both records retain an audit trail.
- [ ] Merge uses revision checks on every affected record and reports partial failure/recovery clearly; repeated requests must not duplicate content. Related links remain independently editable.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with src/types.ts, src/store.ts relationship/context/archive behavior, and web/RecordDetail.tsx. Add CLI/MCP support so agents can identify duplicates and retrieve related context. Coordinate with #23; related, duplicate, parent, and dependency are distinct relationships.

### Human review / verification

Relate two tickets, then preview and merge duplicates containing different comments/images and conflicting metadata. Follow old links, retrieve agent context, and simulate stale input. Confirm that no content or attribution disappears and no ticket is falsely accepted as Done.

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Make workflow status customization easy to discover from the board and safe to use as the project evolves.

### Acceptance criteria

before.body:
## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Provide a dedicated vertical planning view where dragging tickets changes the order in which work should be considered.

### Scope and approach

Build on the saved table view and existing manual/priority sorting. Offer an obvious Priority planning preset, rank tickets within priority groups, and allow explicit movement into another priority group. Ordering must not silently change workflow status or parent. Explain that priority is the urgency bucket and rank is the order within it.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The planning view shows a vertical list with priority groups and visible drag handles, including the start/end of each group.
- [ ] Dragging within a group changes persistent relative rank; dragging to another priority group updates priority and rank visibly.
- [ ] Reordering across tickets with different statuses does not move either ticket to the other status or change its parent.
- [ ] Move up/down and move-to-priority controls provide keyboard alternatives, including first/last positions.
- [ ] Reloading or returning to the saved view retains the order; concurrent reorder failures reconcile without losing tickets.
- [ ] Filtered reordering uses defined visible anchors and preserves the relative order of hidden tickets; saved sort modes clearly indicate whether manual reordering is active.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with web/ProjectPage.tsx place/peersOf, web/TableView.tsx and web/model.ts sortTickets. Current place also copies the target status, so reuse needs care. Coordinate drag preview with #22; prefer existing order metadata over a second competing ranking field.

### Human review / verification

Rank tickets across several stages and priorities, move to first/last, refresh, and repeat with a filter and keyboard controls. Confirm that status/parent stay unchanged and priority changes only when crossing an explicit priority group.

meta.title: Bulk edit feature for tickets

before.body:
## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Select multiple tickets and change shared fields in one operation, with predictable selection and a clear result for every ticket.

### Scope and approach

Extend the existing table checkbox/bulk-status UI to status, priority, owner, labels, and parent; expose selection on the board as well. Labels need separate add/remove actions so existing labels are not accidentally replaced. Approval actions are specified in #16; deletion is outside this ticket.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Board and table support explicit multi-selection, select visible items, clear selection, and a persistent count while the action is being prepared.
- [ ] Only selected visible tickets are affected; filtering or changing view reconciles selection and never silently includes hidden items.
- [ ] Mixed values display as Mixed. Fields left unchanged retain their original values; label addition/removal preserves all other labels.
- [ ] Each change uses the ticket’s revision and normal validation, including parent cycles, scope, and review evidence requirements.
- [ ] The result identifies succeeded, failed, and unchanged tickets; failed items remain available for correction/retry without reapplying successful writes.
- [ ] Selection and operations are keyboard accessible and survive ordinary live refresh without jumping to different tickets.

### Implementation notes and related work

web/TableView.tsx currently loops onMove for bulk status changes. Start there and in web/ProjectPage.tsx; coordinate shared selection/results rather than creating a second independent bulk model. Related: #16 and #23.

### Human review / verification

Bulk-edit a mixed selection, add/remove labels, and simulate a stale revision plus a validation failure. Verify exact affected IDs, preservation of untouched fields, and per-item feedback.

meta.title: Ability to quickly approve tickets without needing to click enter each one

before.body:
## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Approve work from the board or table without opening each ticket. Make scope approval and acceptance of completed work separate, clearly named actions.

### Scope and approach

Provide Approve scope for unapproved planned work, and Accept into Done for tickets in Review. Show the result inline. Batch actions share the selection model from #17. Scope approval alone should not silently select, start, or complete a ticket.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A human can approve a ticket’s scope from its card/row; approved and inherited-scope states are visually distinguishable.
- [ ] A human can accept a Review ticket into Done directly; its summary and evidence remain accessible before accepting.
- [ ] Selected tickets can receive the same eligible approval action with a visible selection count; ineligible items are identified rather than silently changed.
- [ ] Agent requests cannot approve scope or accept work into Done, including through the new bulk path.
- [ ] Stale revisions and partial failures are shown per ticket; successful changes retain human attribution and do not overwrite unrelated fields.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with web/TicketCard.tsx, web/TableView.tsx, web/ProjectPage.tsx and src/store.ts authority/history. Related: #17. Keep the two meanings of approval explicit in copy and action availability.

### Human review / verification

Approve scope on a single item and selected items, then accept a reviewed item. Check that status is unchanged by scope approval, agent calls remain rejected, and a stale item produces a clear result.

meta.title: Need a way inside a ticket to navigate to parent ticket

before.body:
## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started. Proposed behavior below remains subject to human scope review.

### Intended outcome

Navigate directly from a child ticket to its parent without searching the board or using the parent-selection editor.

### Scope and approach

Show a clearly labeled parent link with the parent's ticket number and short title near the top of ticket details. Keep this navigation separate from changing the parent relationship. Follow existing ticket-link behavior, including middle-click and modifier-click opening a separate tab.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A child ticket shows a keyboard-accessible Parent: #number title link; clicking it opens the correct parent's detail dialog.
- [ ] Same-tab navigation saves pending edits first using the existing autosave/conflict behavior. A failed save keeps the child draft open and explains the failure.
- [ ] Middle-click/modifier-click opens the parent in a separate tab while leaving the current ticket and its draft intact; the resulting URL survives refresh.
- [ ] An archived parent remains navigable and is clearly marked Archived; navigation does not unarchive or reparent anything.
- [ ] A ticket without a parent has no misleading navigation target. A missing parent shows an unavailable state without crashing or silently discarding the stored relationship.
- [ ] Changing the parent updates the navigation target consistently after saving. The parent picker continues to edit the relationship independently.
- [ ] Long titles remain usable at compact/mobile widths, with accessible link names that include the ticket number and title.

### Implementation notes and related work

Reuse web/ticketNavigation.ts from #42 and RecordDetail's save-before-child-navigation pattern. Inspect web/RecordDetail.tsx and web/ParentInput.tsx. Related: #14 child management, #15 parent selection, #42 new-tab navigation. Breadcrumb navigation across the full ancestry and a new navigation-history system are outside this scope.

### Human review / verification

Open a child, edit its description and navigate to its parent, then reopen the child to verify persistence. Try keyboard, middle-click, an archived parent, a long title and a failed/conflicting save.

meta.title: Ability to add microtasks to a ticket

before.body:
These are just small tasks that are tracked inside the ticket and don't show up as separate full tickets. Sort of like a checklist of things that need to be done for that ticket. 

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Track small steps inside a ticket with a checklist, without creating separate numbered tickets or cluttering the board.

### Scope and approach

Provide an editable Microtasks section with add, rename, reorder, complete, and remove actions. Keep it readable/editable in Markdown and include it in agent context. Reuse Markdown task-list syntax in a clearly owned section where practical; preserve other prose and existing acceptance criteria.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Enter adds a nonblank checklist item and keeps focus ready for the next; items can be checked, edited, reordered, and removed with keyboard alternatives.
- [ ] Items persist across save/reopen and direct Markdown edits; concurrent changes use revision protection.
- [ ] Agents can read and update checklist state through the supported record interfaces without creating ticket IDs for checklist items.
- [ ] The ticket displays completed/total counts, including the all-complete state; cards may show a compact count without listing every item.
- [ ] Completing the checklist does not automatically move the ticket to Done or claim its acceptance criteria are satisfied.
- [ ] Unrelated Markdown, attachments, and comments survive checklist edits.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with web/RecordDetail.tsx, web/RecordMarkdown.tsx (GFM rendering already exists), src/files.ts Markdown preservation and src/store.ts context. Related: #14 for work large enough to need child tickets; #23 for reducing board clutter.

### Human review / verification

Create/reorder/toggle items, reopen, edit a task in Markdown, and retrieve agent context. Verify a stale toggle cannot overwrite a newer edit and all-complete leaves ticket status unchanged.

meta.title: In needs you show open questions at top of ticket

before.body:
It can be difficult to find what I need to answer in conversation chain. Put the question I need to answer right at top similar to the accept/reject buttons. Also if it's ready to accept or reject and you want me the manually test or give feedback put it in text with accept/reject. If I don't need to check out something, just say it passed the test suite.

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started. Proposed behavior below remains subject to human scope review.

### Intended outcome

Opening a ticket from Needs you immediately shows the question to answer or the review action to take, without searching a long conversation. Put manual test/feedback instructions beside Accept/Reject.

### Scope and approach

Add a prominent action area near the top of ticket details and conversation views, aligned with the existing review controls. Surface all unresolved questions with their author and original context, with an answer action and a link to the original thread entry. Render this from the existing question records rather than creating duplicate comments. Show the same action area when opening the ticket directly so the need for attention does not depend on the entry route.

For Review tickets, display the current submission's human review instructions, relevant handoff and verification summary beside Accept/Reject. If the submission explicitly requires no manual checks and recorded verification supports it, say the test suite passed and offer the evidence. Never infer a pass or invent manual checks from missing instructions; missing/failed/unrun verification must be clearly labeled.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Opening a question-bearing ticket from Needs you shows the unresolved question text near the top, regardless of conversation sort order or length.
- [ ] Multiple unresolved questions remain individually identifiable with attribution, links to their original entries and a straightforward answer path. Long content can expand without concealing the existence of other questions.
- [ ] Posting an answer uses the existing durable conversation and retains the draft on failure; resolving a question is explicit and affects only that question. Merely opening a ticket never resolves it.
- [ ] Resolving/reopening a question updates the top area and Needs you after refresh; review instructions remain visible if the ticket also awaits review.
- [ ] Review instructions and requested feedback appear beside the existing Accept/Reject controls, with accessible Markdown and useful links. Acceptance feedback continues to work as implemented in #30.
- [ ] The summary reflects the latest review submission and distinguishes manual checks, successful automated verification, failures, exceptions and missing evidence. An old passing result is not presented as proof of a newer unverified submission.
- [ ] When no manual checks are explicitly required and the current submission has passing verification, concise text says the test suite passed, with access to its recorded command/result. Otherwise the UI states what is requested or unknown truthfully.
- [ ] Needs you remains actionable until all applicable attention reasons are addressed; resolving one question does not hide another question or a pending review.
- [ ] Keyboard and compact-screen users can reach the question/answer and review controls without losing unsaved ticket or reply drafts.

### Implementation notes and related work

Inspect web/Pages.tsx AttentionPage, web/model.ts attention reasons, web/RecordDetail.tsx question comments and review data, and web/ReviewActions.tsx. Use existing handoff, review instructions and verification records; clarify current-submission evidence association during implementation if needed. Related: #30 optional review feedback, #32 conversation ordering, #27 future structured questionnaires. This ticket does not require implementing the full questionnaire system.

### Human review / verification

Open a ticket with two unanswered questions deep in a long conversation; answer and resolve one, then verify the other remains prominent. Test a Review ticket with manual steps, one explicitly requiring only recorded automated checks, and one with missing/failed verification. Check that a fresh review submission cannot inherit a misleading old pass summary.

Opening a ticket from Needs you immediately shows the question to answer or the review action to take, without searching a long conversation. Put manual test/feedback instructions beside Accept/Reject.

### Scope and approach

Add a prominent action area near the top of ticket details and conversation views, aligned with the existing review controls. Surface all unresolved questions with their author and original context, with an answer action and a link to the original thread entry. Render this from the existing question records rather than creating duplicate comments. meta.title: Adopt ControlRoom names with explicit legacy-folder migration

after.body:
## Choice

New projects use .controlroom and the controlroom command. Existing .workboard projects remain readable in place until an explicit stopped-service migration renames the folder. Refuse ambiguous dual folders. Keep old command/environment aliases, legacy backup import, and stable record/project identifiers.

## Context and rationale

Approved ticket #43 requests ControlRoom naming across commands, MCP and data storage. Projects already contain durable records and ignored screenshots, and agents may refer to existing paths. A silent upgrade-time move could strand those integrations or split the board.

## Alternatives and tradeoffs

A hard rename without compatibility would break existing agents. Keeping Workboard as the primary name would not fulfill the request. Explicit migration requires one deliberate maintenance step and external-path updates, but keeps the rename reviewable. The service must stop, old installed runtimes must upgrade first, and backups are documented. The native capture bundle identifier and shared rendezvous directory remain legacy compatibility identifiers so upgraded and older project services coordinate one companion. The helper's display and executable names are ControlRoom Capture; ad-hoc builds may need renewed macOS permission approval.

## Attribution and related work

Codex fixes, implementation choice within human-approved #43. Related #50 cross-project capture coordination. This record grants no additional implementation approval or ticket acceptance.

after.body:
## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started. Proposed behavior remains subject to human scope review.

### Intended outcome

Quickly switch the board between all tickets, tickets explicitly approved for agent work, and tickets still needing explicit approval, without typing filter syntax or opening each ticket.

### Scope and approach

Add a compact, labeled Approval control beside the existing board search/filter field with All, Approved and Not approved options. Reuse the current is:approved and -is:approved filters so the control, typed query and saved view stay in sync. Make the same control available in the project's table view.

Proposed definition: approval means the ticket's own Approve this scope for agent work checkbox, matching the existing filter. This is separate from acceptance into Done. A child may be authorized through an approved parent while lacking its own explicit approval; help text must explain that distinction. Do not change inherited agent permissions or set approval flags as a side effect of filtering.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The Approval control switches between All, Approved and Not approved with a single selection and clearly shows the active choice.
- [ ] Approved matches scopeApproved=true; Not approved includes false or absent values. All removes only the approval constraint, preserving other search text and filters.
- [ ] Typing is:approved or -is:approved updates the control, and using the control updates the query without duplicating or leaving contradictory approval terms.
- [ ] Complex or mixed approval expressions are represented honestly (for example, a Custom state); changing them never silently drops unrelated query constraints.
- [ ] Existing status, label, owner and text filters compose correctly. Board/table counts and empty-state messaging reflect the filtered result. Archived tickets remain excluded unless explicitly requested.
- [ ] The control follows existing saved-view draft/save behavior, survives refresh after saving, and restores each view's own approval filter when switching views.
- [ ] Approval changes made in a ticket or another session update the visible results on refresh/live synchronization without losing the active filter.
- [ ] Keyboard operation and accessible labeling work in both density modes and narrow layouts; the new control does not shift saved-view tab widths.
- [ ] Filtering does not approve, move, claim, archive or accept tickets. Parent-scope authorization continues to behave as before.

### Implementation notes and related work

web/model.ts already supports is:approved and its negation using the explicit scopeApproved flag. Inspect web/ProjectPage.tsx for filter controls and saved-view handling, and src/store.ts approvedScope behavior when explaining inherited permission. Reuse parsed filter behavior rather than fragile string replacement. Related: #16 quick approval actions and #46 column visibility. Bulk approval and changing approval inheritance are outside this ticket.

### Human review / verification

Use a fixture with explicitly approved, unchecked and parent-authorized child tickets. Toggle all three options, combine with a label/text query, save a view and reload. Approve a visible ticket in another session and confirm it enters/leaves the filtered set correctly. Check that changing the filter never modifies any ticket's approval or stage.

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Break down a parent ticket into real child tickets directly inside its detail dialog, using a title field and Enter for each child. Keep the parent open and the input ready for the next title.

### Scope and approach

Add a Children section with quick entry and links to existing children. Use the project’s configured intake/backlog default and show the destination. For a new unsaved parent, save it successfully before persisting children; retain pending titles if that save fails. Checklist items are handled separately in #20.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Entering a nonblank title and pressing Enter creates one numbered ticket with the current ticket as its parent; no questionnaire is required.
- [ ] Repeated entry retains focus and supports several children without closing the parent; whitespace and repeated submission while saving do not create duplicates.
- [ ] The child appears immediately in the Children section and under its parent on a parent-grouped board.
- [ ] Creation failures retain the title and give a retryable error. Closing the parent follows existing save behavior.
- [ ] Child creation preserves agent scope rules, and completing children never automatically completes the parent.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with web/RecordDetail.tsx (existing child list), web/QuickTicket.tsx, and src/store.ts create/relationship validation. Reuse quick entry; coordinate the parent chooser with #15.

### Human review / verification

Create several children from an existing parent and from a newly drafted parent. Open a child, reload, and confirm its title, number, parent, and stage. Exercise a failed save and keyboard-only entry.

before.body:
## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started. Proposed behavior below remains subject to human scope review.

### Intended outcome

Navigate directly from a child ticket to its parent without searching the board or using the parent-selection editor.

### Scope and approach

Show a clearly labeled parent link with the parent's ticket number and short title near the top of ticket details. Keep this navigation separate from changing the parent relationship. Follow existing ticket-link behavior, including middle-click and modifier-click opening a separate tab.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A child ticket shows a keyboard-accessible Parent: #number title link; clicking it opens the correct parent's detail dialog.
- [ ] Same-tab navigation saves pending edits first using the existing autosave/conflict behavior. A failed save keeps the child draft open and explains the failure.
- [ ] Middle-click/modifier-click opens the parent in a separate tab while leaving the current ticket and its draft intact; the resulting URL survives refresh.
- [ ] An archived parent remains navigable and is clearly marked Archived; navigation does not unarchive or reparent anything.
- [ ] A ticket without a parent has no misleading navigation target. A missing parent shows an unavailable state without crashing or silently discarding the stored relationship.
- [ ] Changing the parent updates the navigation target consistently after saving. The parent picker continues to edit the relationship independently.
- [ ] Long titles remain usable at compact/mobile widths, with accessible link names that include the ticket number and title.

### Implementation notes and related work

Reuse web/ticketNavigation.ts from #42 and RecordDetail's save-before-child-navigation pattern. Inspect web/RecordDetail.tsx and web/ParentInput.tsx. Related: #14 child management, #15 parent selection, #42 new-tab navigation. Breadcrumb navigation across the full ancestry and a new navigation-history system are outside this scope.

### Human review / verification

Open a child, edit its description and navigate to its parent, then reopen the child to verify persistence. Try keyboard, middle-click, an archived parent, a long title and a failed/conflicting save.

before.body:
It can be difficult to find what I need to answer in conversation chain. Put the question I need to answer right at top similar to the accept/reject buttons. Also if it's ready to accept or reject and you want me the manually test or give feedback put it in text with accept/reject. If I don't need to check out something, just say it passed the test suite.

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started. Proposed behavior below remains subject to human scope review.

### Intended outcome

Opening a ticket from Needs you immediately shows the question to answer or the review action to take, without searching a long conversation. Put manual test/feedback instructions beside Accept/Reject.

### Scope and approach

Add a prominent action area near the top of ticket details and conversation views, aligned with the existing review controls. Surface all unresolved questions with their author and original context, with an answer action and a link to the original thread entry. Render this from the existing question records rather than creating duplicate comments. Show the same action area when opening the ticket directly so the need for attention does not depend on the entry route.

For Review tickets, display the current submission's human review instructions, relevant handoff and verification summary beside Accept/Reject. If the submission explicitly requires no manual checks and recorded verification supports it, say the test suite passed and offer the evidence. Never infer a pass or invent manual checks from missing instructions; missing/failed/unrun verification must be clearly labeled.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Opening a question-bearing ticket from Needs you shows the unresolved question text near the top, regardless of conversation sort order or length.
- [ ] Multiple unresolved questions remain individually identifiable with attribution, links to their original entries and a straightforward answer path. Long content can expand without concealing the existence of other questions.
- [ ] Posting an answer uses the existing durable conversation and retains the draft on failure; resolving a question is explicit and affects only that question. Merely opening a ticket never resolves it.
- [ ] Resolving/reopening a question updates the top area and Needs you after refresh; review instructions remain visible if the ticket also awaits review.
- [ ] Review instructions and requested feedback appear beside the existing Accept/Reject controls, with accessible Markdown and useful links. Acceptance feedback continues to work as implemented in #30.
- [ ] The summary reflects the latest review submission and distinguishes manual checks, successful automated verification, failures, exceptions and missing evidence. An old passing result is not presented as proof of a newer unverified submission.
- [ ] When no manual checks are explicitly required and the current submission has passing verification, concise text says the test suite passed, with access to its recorded command/result. Otherwise the UI states what is requested or unknown truthfully.
- [ ] Needs you remains actionable until all applicable attention reasons are addressed; resolving one question does not hide another question or a pending review.
- [ ] Keyboard and compact-screen users can reach the question/answer and review controls without losing unsaved ticket or reply drafts.

### Implementation notes and related work

Inspect web/Pages.tsx AttentionPage, web/model.ts attention reasons, web/RecordDetail.tsx question comments and review data, and web/ReviewActions.tsx. Use existing handoff, review instructions and verification records; clarify current-submission evidence association during implementation if needed. Related: #30 optional review feedback, #32 conversation ordering, #27 future structured questionnaires. This ticket does not require implementing the full questionnaire system.

### Human review / verification

Open a ticket with two unanswered questions deep in a long conversation; answer and resolve one, then verify the other remains prominent. Test a Review ticket with manual steps, one explicitly requiring only recorded automated checks, and one with missing/failed verification. Check that a fresh review submission cannot inherit a misleading old pass summary.
