meta.title: Screenshot Save to Ticket

before.body:
## Visual feedback

[![Screenshot](/api/images/image-ba7623ff65d116a9/base)](#image=image-ba7623ff65d116a9)

- [ ] A1 (note-d0faa9fc-2c69-47fb-961e-0cb7aaaba320): Clicking the button should popup a prompt for name for ticket and then open up the new ticket as a popup so I can add any details. 

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started. Proposed behavior remains subject to human scope review.

### Intended outcome

Click Save to ticket, enter a short ticket title in a focused prompt, and immediately open the created ticket in the centered detail popup to add further details. Preserve the screenshot and annotations throughout. Source: screenshot annotation A1 (note-d0faa9fc-2c69-47fb-961e-0cb7aaaba320).

### Scope and approach

For the single-new-ticket path, make Save to ticket open a small in-app title dialog instead of silently creating a generically named ticket. Prefill from any title already entered, select/focus the text for quick replacement, and support Enter to create and Escape/Cancel to return to the annotation editor. Require a nonblank trimmed title; no additional questionnaire.

After saving the annotations and creating the ticket successfully, use the returned ticket ID to open its normal detail dialog. The title prompt is the single authoritative title entry; remove or synchronize the existing inline title field to avoid competing values. Keep attachment-to-existing-ticket and split-annotation workflows distinct, without introducing a single-title prompt into those paths. New tickets use the project's normal initial stage, currently Concept.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Save to ticket in new-ticket mode opens an accessible, focused title prompt before creating a ticket. Typing a title and pressing Enter creates it; whitespace-only input is rejected inline.
- [ ] Cancel/Escape creates no ticket, returns focus to the editor, and preserves the screenshot and unsaved annotation draft.
- [ ] On success, the editor/title prompt hands off to the centered detail popup for the exact newly created ticket. Its heading matches the entered title and the ticket URL identifies it.
- [ ] The description contains the screenshot preview and written annotation instructions with stable annotation references. Base image, editable geometry and attachment links remain intact and available to agent context.
- [ ] The user can add description/details immediately. Save or clicking outside uses existing save-and-close behavior; a failed save retains the draft and explains the error.
- [ ] While submission is pending, repeated clicks/Enter cannot create multiple tickets. Annotation-save or creation failures retain the title and annotations, show a useful error, and do not claim success.
- [ ] Once creation succeeds, a later refresh/navigation failure offers reopening the returned ticket rather than creating another. Uncertain write results are not automatically replayed.
- [ ] Saving a standalone screenshot still creates no ticket. Attaching to an existing ticket and splitting annotations retain their current explicitly selected destinations and behavior.
- [ ] Keyboard focus transfers correctly between editor, title prompt and ticket detail, including on narrow screens; there is no inaccessible stack of active modal dialogs.

### Implementation notes and related work

Inspect attach() in web/AnnotationEditor.tsx: the new-ticket branch currently posts a record, reloads, then closes without using the created record to open details. Coordinate the transition with web/App.tsx, web/RecordDetail.tsx and web/ticketNavigation.ts. Retain revision checks when saving annotations; use the existing imageMarkdown and annotation content rather than inventing a second attachment format. Related: #35 screenshot conversations, #39 description thumbnails and #42 ticket URLs. No new native capture or batch-split redesign is needed.

### Human review / verification

Capture or open a screenshot, add annotations, click Save to ticket, enter a title and confirm. Verify the resulting ticket opens with the correct title, preview and instructions; add details, close and reopen to check persistence. Also try cancel, blank title, repeated submission and a simulated save failure, then check standalone save and existing-ticket attachment still work.

meta.title: Need a way inside a ticket to navigate to parent ticket

before.body:
## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started. Proposed behavior below remains subject to human scope review.

### Intended outcome

Navigate directly from a child ticket to its parent without searching the board or using the parent-selection editor.

### Scope and approach

Show a clearly labeled parent link with the parent's ticket number and short title near the top of ticket details. Keep this navigation separate from changing the parent relationship. Follow existing ticket-link behavior, including middle-click and modifier-click opening a separate tab.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A child ticket shows a keyboard-accessible Parent: #number title link; clicking it opens the correct parent's detail dialog.
- [ ] Same-tab navigation saves pending edits first using the existing autosave/conflict behavior. A failed save keeps the child draft open and explains the failure.
- [ ] Middle-click/modifier-click opens the parent in a separate tab while leaving the current ticket and its draft intact; the resulting URL survives refresh.
- [ ] An archived parent remains navigable and is clearly marked Archived; navigation does not unarchive or reparent anything.
- [ ] A ticket without a parent has no misleading navigation target. A missing parent shows an unavailable state without crashing or silently discarding the stored relationship.
- [ ] Changing the parent updates the navigation target consistently after saving. The parent picker continues to edit the relationship independently.
- [ ] Long titles remain usable at compact/mobile widths, with accessible link names that include the ticket number and title.

### Implementation notes and related work

Reuse web/ticketNavigation.ts from #42 and RecordDetail's save-before-child-navigation pattern. Inspect web/RecordDetail.tsx and web/ParentInput.tsx. Related: #14 child management, #15 parent selection, #42 new-tab navigation. Breadcrumb navigation across the full ancestry and a new navigation-history system are outside this scope.

### Human review / verification

Open a child, edit its description and navigate to its parent, then reopen the child to verify persistence. Try keyboard, middle-click, an archived parent, a long title and a failed/conflicting save.

Opening a ticket from Needs you immediately shows the question to answer or the review action to take, without searching a long conversation. Put manual test/feedback instructions beside Accept/Reject.

### Scope and approach

Add a prominent action area near the top of ticket details and conversation views, aligned with the existing review controls. Surface all unresolved questions with their author and original context, with an answer action and a link to the original thread entry. Render this from the existing question records rather than creating duplicate comments. Show the same action area when opening the ticket directly so the need for attention does not depend on the entry route.

For Review tickets, display the current submission's human review instructions, relevant handoff and verification summary beside Accept/Reject. If the submission explicitly requires no manual checks and recorded verification supports it, say the test suite passed and offer the evidence. Never infer a pass or invent manual checks from missing instructions; missing/failed/unrun verification must be clearly labeled.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Opening a question-bearing ticket from Needs you shows the unresolved question text near the top, regardless of conversation sort order or length.
- [ ] Multiple unresolved questions remain individually identifiable with attribution, links to their original entries and a straightforward answer path. Long content can expand without concealing the existence of other questions.
- [ ] Posting an answer uses the existing durable conversation and retains the draft on failure; resolving a question is explicit and affects only that question. Merely opening a ticket never resolves it.
- [ ] Resolving/reopening a question updates the top area and Needs you after refresh; review instructions remain visible if the ticket also awaits review.
- [ ] Review instructions and requested feedback appear beside the existing Accept/Reject controls, with accessible Markdown and useful links. Acceptance feedback continues to work as implemented in #30.
- [ ] The summary reflects the latest review submission and distinguishes manual checks, successful automated verification, failures, exceptions and missing evidence. An old passing result is not presented as proof of a newer unverified submission.
- [ ] When no manual checks are explicitly required and the current submission has passing verification, concise text says the test suite passed, with access to its recorded command/result. Otherwise the UI states what is requested or unknown truthfully.
- [ ] Needs you remains actionable until all applicable attention reasons are addressed; resolving one question does not hide another question or a pending review.
- [ ] Keyboard and compact-screen users can reach the question/answer and review controls without losing unsaved ticket or reply drafts.

- [ ] A1 (note-d0faa9fc-2c69-47fb-961e-0cb7aaaba320): Clicking the button should popup a prompt for name for ticket and then open up the new ticket as a popup so I can add any details. 

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started. Proposed behavior remains subject to human scope review.

### Intended outcome

Click Save to ticket, enter a short ticket title in a focused prompt, and immediately open the created ticket in the centered detail popup to add further details. Preserve the screenshot and annotations throughout. Source: screenshot annotation A1 (note-d0faa9fc-2c69-47fb-961e-0cb7aaaba320).

### Scope and approach

For the single-new-ticket path, make Save to ticket open a small in-app title dialog instead of silently creating a generically named ticket. Prefill from any title already entered, select/focus the text for quick replacement, and support Enter to create and Escape/Cancel to return to the annotation editor. Require a nonblank trimmed title; no additional questionnaire.

After saving the annotations and creating the ticket successfully, use the returned ticket ID to open its normal detail dialog. The title prompt is the single authoritative title entry; remove or synchronize the existing inline title field to avoid competing values. Keep attachment-to-existing-ticket and split-annotation workflows distinct, without introducing a single-title prompt into those paths. New tickets use the project's normal initial stage, currently Concept.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Save to ticket in new-ticket mode opens an accessible, focused title prompt before creating a ticket. Typing a title and pressing Enter creates it; whitespace-only input is rejected inline.
- [ ] Cancel/Escape creates no ticket, returns focus to the editor, and preserves the screenshot and unsaved annotation draft.
- [ ] On success, the editor/title prompt hands off to the centered detail popup for the exact newly created ticket. Its heading matches the entered title and the ticket URL identifies it.
- [ ] The description contains the screenshot preview and written annotation instructions with stable annotation references. Base image, editable geometry and attachment links remain intact and available to agent context.
- [ ] The user can add description/details immediately. Save or clicking outside uses existing save-and-close behavior; a failed save retains the draft and explains the error.
- [ ] While submission is pending, repeated clicks/Enter cannot create multiple tickets. Annotation-save or creation failures retain the title and annotations, show a useful error, and do not claim success.
- [ ] Once creation succeeds, a later refresh/navigation failure offers reopening the returned ticket rather than creating another. Uncertain write results are not automatically replayed.
- [ ] Saving a standalone screenshot still creates no ticket. Attaching to an existing ticket and splitting annotations retain their current explicitly selected destinations and behavior.
- [ ] Keyboard focus transfers correctly between editor, title prompt and ticket detail, including on narrow screens; there is no inaccessible stack of active modal dialogs.

Coordinate the transition with web/App.tsx, web/RecordDetail.tsx and web/ticketNavigation.ts. Retain revision checks when saving annotations; use the existing imageMarkdown and annotation content rather than inventing a second attachment format. Related: #35 screenshot conversations, #39 description thumbnails and #42 ticket URLs. No new native capture or batch-split redesign is needed.

### Human review / verification

Capture or open a screenshot, add annotations, click Save to ticket, enter a title and confirm. Verify the resulting ticket opens with the correct title, preview and instructions; add details, close and reopen to check persistence. Also try cancel, blank title, repeated submission and a simulated save failure, then check standalone save and existing-ticket attachment still work.

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started. Proposed behavior below remains subject to human scope review.

### Intended outcome

Clear completed tickets from the active board quickly, while keeping their history easy to browse and restore.

### Scope and approach

Add an Archive completed tickets action to a Done-status column header. Proposed first-release behavior: archive only unarchived tickets in that column that match the current view/search filters, across its visible groups. Before applying, show the exact count and scope, with a way to inspect the affected tickets. Provide an obvious Archived tickets view with search and an Unarchive action.

Unarchiving returns a ticket to the active board in its existing workflow stage (usually Done); moving it back into development remains a separate explicit action. Archiving a parent does not implicitly archive its children. This is a focused implementation follow-up to #23; it need not wait for every clutter-management recommendation.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A Done-role column offers the archive action, including renamed/custom Done columns; non-Done columns do not silently offer the same completed-work operation.
- [ ] The preview names the column, filter scope and affected ticket count. Empty sets are harmless; cancel changes nothing. Tickets outside the preview are never archived.
- [ ] Each write uses the previewed ticket revision. Concurrent changes are rejected for that ticket, with clear success/failure counts and a refresh/review path; no stale record is overwritten.
- [ ] Archived tickets disappear from ordinary active views and remain searchable in an explicitly labeled archive view.
- [ ] A ticket can be opened and unarchived from the archive view. Its status, number, prose, comments, attachments, decisions and parent/child links survive the round trip.
- [ ] Archiving preserves decision/rule discovery and does not delete local screenshots or implicitly archive linked records.
- [ ] The action and archive navigation work with keyboard input, and the chosen scope stays explicit when filters or column visibility change.

### Implementation notes and related work

Reuse the existing archived metadata and is:archived filtering in web/model.ts and the detail Unarchive action. Inspect web/BoardView.tsx, web/ProjectPage.tsx and revision-checked record updates in src/store.ts. Related: parent #23, #17 bulk actions, #46 column visibility. Scheduled/automatic archiving and deletion are outside this ticket.

### Human review / verification

On a fixture with completed parent/child tickets and active work, archive a filtered Done subset, find it through Archived tickets, then restore one ticket. Verify unrelated tickets and linked project knowledge remain intact. Exercise a concurrent edit during the preview to confirm it is reported rather than overwritten.

after.body:
I would like a way to click a swimlane and turn on/off the tickets in that swimline from being visible. For example backlog can be large and I want to turn off backlog and just view the other swimlanes. Maybe a little human eye icon that is in the swimlane header you can click and quickly turn on/off visibility.

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started. Proposed behavior below remains subject to human scope review.

### Intended outcome

Temporarily hide tickets in a busy status column such as Backlog with one click, then restore them just as easily.

### Scope and approach

The Backlog example refers to workflow/status columns (called swimlanes in the request). Add an eye-style visibility toggle to each column header. Hide that column's ticket content across all parent/label groups, retaining a compact labeled header or equivalent visible restore control. This is a visibility preference, not an archive or ticket-status change.

Proposed default: remember hidden column IDs per project and saved view in personal UI preferences, without rewriting the shared view's search query. Keep visibility independent of existing horizontal group collapse. Provide Show all columns and a clear indication of hidden columns.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] One click hides Backlog's cards across all groups and leaves other columns usable. A visible control restores Backlog with one click.
- [ ] Header controls expose an accessible name and pressed/expanded state, work by keyboard, and clearly distinguish hidden from empty columns.
- [ ] No ticket, claim, stage, archive flag or parent relationship changes when toggling visibility.
- [ ] Search/filter changes compose with visibility without losing the user's query. Hidden columns remain identifiable, and Show all recovers from every column being hidden.
- [ ] Visibility is remembered for that project/view after refresh without leaking to another project/view; custom column rename/reorder preserves it by stable ID, and deleted IDs are safely ignored.
- [ ] Board keyboard navigation skips hidden cards, focus stays recoverable after hiding a focused column, and hidden content cannot receive invisible drag/drop or quick-create interactions.
- [ ] Counts and any bulk-action preview make their scope clear; hidden tickets are not silently selected for operations on visible tickets.
- [ ] Table/list views retain their existing behavior; switching back to the board restores its column visibility preferences.

### Implementation notes and related work

Inspect web/BoardView.tsx column rendering and keyboard navigation, web/ProjectPage.tsx view preferences and web/model.ts filters. Related: #44 quick archive, #23 ticket clutter, #18 status customization. Do not conflate this with existing parent-group collapse or automatically create a new shared saved view.

### Human review / verification

Hide Backlog on a populated parent-grouped board, filter the remaining tickets, restore Backlog and refresh. Switch views/projects and rename a custom column. Check keyboard recovery and the all-hidden state.

after.body:
I would like a way to click a swimlane and turn on/off the tickets in that swimline from being visible. For example backlog can be large and I want to turn off backlog and just view the other swimlanes. Maybe a little human eye icon that is in the swimlane header you can click and quickly turn on/off visibility.

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started. Proposed behavior below remains subject to human scope review.

### Intended outcome

Temporarily hide tickets in a busy status column such as Backlog with one click, then restore them just as easily.

### Scope and approach

The Backlog example refers to workflow/status columns (called swimlanes in the request). Add an eye-style visibility toggle to each column header. Hide that column's ticket content across all parent/label groups, retaining a compact labeled header or equivalent visible restore control. This is a visibility preference, not an archive or ticket-status change.

Proposed default: remember hidden column IDs per project and saved view in personal UI preferences, without rewriting the shared view's search query. Keep visibility independent of existing horizontal group collapse. Provide Show all columns and a clear indication of hidden columns.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] One click hides Backlog's cards across all groups and leaves other columns usable. A visible control restores Backlog with one click.
- [ ] Header controls expose an accessible name and pressed/expanded state, work by keyboard, and clearly distinguish hidden from empty columns.
- [ ] No ticket, claim, stage, archive flag or parent relationship changes when toggling visibility.
- [ ] Search/filter changes compose with visibility without losing the user's query. Hidden columns remain identifiable, and Show all recovers from every column being hidden.
- [ ] Visibility is remembered for that project/view after refresh without leaking to another project/view; custom column rename/reorder preserves it by stable ID, and deleted IDs are safely ignored.
- [ ] Board keyboard navigation skips hidden cards, focus stays recoverable after hiding a focused column, and hidden content cannot receive invisible drag/drop or quick-create interactions.
- [ ] Counts and any bulk-action preview make their scope clear; hidden tickets are not silently selected for operations on visible tickets.
- [ ] Table/list views retain their existing behavior; switching back to the board restores its column visibility preferences.

### Implementation notes and related work

Inspect web/BoardView.tsx column rendering and keyboard navigation, web/ProjectPage.tsx view preferences and web/model.ts filters. Related: #44 quick archive, #23 ticket clutter, #18 status customization. Do not conflate this with existing parent-group collapse or automatically create a new shared saved view.

### Human review / verification

Hide Backlog on a populated parent-grouped board, filter the remaining tickets, restore Backlog and refresh. Switch views/projects and rename a custom column. Check keyboard recovery and the all-hidden state.

after.body:
I would like a way to click a swimlane and turn on/off the tickets in that swimline from being visible. For example backlog can be large and I want to turn off backlog and just view the other swimlanes. Maybe a little human eye icon that is in the swimlane header you can click and quickly turn on/off visibility.

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started. Proposed behavior below remains subject to human scope review.

### Intended outcome

Temporarily hide tickets in a busy status column such as Backlog with one click, then restore them just as easily.

### Scope and approach

The Backlog example refers to workflow/status columns (called swimlanes in the request). Add an eye-style visibility toggle to each column header. Hide that column's ticket content across all parent/label groups, retaining a compact labeled header or equivalent visible restore control. This is a visibility preference, not an archive or ticket-status change.

Proposed default: remember hidden column IDs per project and saved view in personal UI preferences, without rewriting the shared view's search query. Keep visibility independent of existing horizontal group collapse. Provide Show all columns and a clear indication of hidden columns.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] One click hides Backlog's cards across all groups and leaves other columns usable. A visible control restores Backlog with one click.
- [ ] Header controls expose an accessible name and pressed/expanded state, work by keyboard, and clearly distinguish hidden from empty columns.
- [ ] No ticket, claim, stage, archive flag or parent relationship changes when toggling visibility.
- [ ] Search/filter changes compose with visibility without losing the user's query. Hidden columns remain identifiable, and Show all recovers from every column being hidden.
- [ ] Visibility is remembered for that project/view after refresh without leaking to another project/view; custom column rename/reorder preserves it by stable ID, and deleted IDs are safely ignored.
- [ ] Board keyboard navigation skips hidden cards, focus stays recoverable after hiding a focused column, and hidden content cannot receive invisible drag/drop or quick-create interactions.
- [ ] Counts and any bulk-action preview make their scope clear; hidden tickets are not silently selected for operations on visible tickets.
- [ ] Table/list views retain their existing behavior; switching back to the board restores its column visibility preferences.

### Implementation notes and related work

Inspect web/BoardView.tsx column rendering and keyboard navigation, web/ProjectPage.tsx view preferences and web/model.ts filters. Related: #44 quick archive, #23 ticket clutter, #18 status customization. Do not conflate this with existing parent-group collapse or automatically create a new shared saved view.

### Human review / verification

Hide Backlog on a populated parent-grouped board, filter the remaining tickets, restore Backlog and refresh. Switch views/projects and rename a custom column. Check keyboard recovery and the all-hidden state.

meta.title: Ability to add microtasks to a ticket

before.body:
These are just small tasks that are tracked inside the ticket and don't show up as separate full tickets. Sort of like a checklist of things that need to be done for that ticket. 

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Track small steps inside a ticket with a checklist, without creating separate numbered tickets or cluttering the board.

### Scope and approach

Provide an editable Microtasks section with add, rename, reorder, complete, and remove actions. Keep it readable/editable in Markdown and include it in agent context. Reuse Markdown task-list syntax in a clearly owned section where practical; preserve other prose and existing acceptance criteria.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Enter adds a nonblank checklist item and keeps focus ready for the next; items can be checked, edited, reordered, and removed with keyboard alternatives.
- [ ] Items persist across save/reopen and direct Markdown edits; concurrent changes use revision protection.
- [ ] Agents can read and update checklist state through the supported record interfaces without creating ticket IDs for checklist items.
- [ ] The ticket displays completed/total counts, including the all-complete state; cards may show a compact count without listing every item.
- [ ] Completing the checklist does not automatically move the ticket to Done or claim its acceptance criteria are satisfied.
- [ ] Unrelated Markdown, attachments, and comments survive checklist edits.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with web/RecordDetail.tsx, web/RecordMarkdown.tsx (GFM rendering already exists), src/files.ts Markdown preservation and src/store.ts context. Related: #14 for work large enough to need child tickets; #23 for reducing board clutter.

### Human review / verification

Create/reorder/toggle items, reopen, edit a task in Markdown, and retrieve agent context. Verify a stale toggle cannot overwrite a newer edit and all-complete leaves ticket status unchanged.

meta.title: Add questionaires to tickets for human review

before.body:
If the LLM has questions about a ticket, they can add a questionaire with multiple choice questions or text questions to a ticket and mark it as needing human feedback. 

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Let an agent attach a structured questionnaire to a ticket and request human input, keeping questions and answers in the ticket’s conversation.

### Scope and approach

Support one or more multiple-choice or free-text questions, an explicit needs-feedback state, and answering at the human’s pace. Store structured data durably in Markdown records/metadata and expose it through CLI/MCP context. Keep this distinct from mandatory ticket creation forms.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An agent can submit a questionnaire with stable question IDs, clear prompts, answer types, and optional recommended choices; users can provide custom text where choices are offered.
- [ ] The ticket appears in Needs you with a direct route to its unanswered questionnaire; a separate flag does not silently change its workflow stage.
- [ ] Questions never time out or disappear because the user pauses. Draft answers persist across closing/reopening and refresh, and can be submitted explicitly.
- [ ] No recommended/preselected option counts as an answer until the human submits; required unanswered questions remain visible.
- [ ] Submitted answers retain human attribution, question wording, and timestamps in the conversation, and are readable by agent context and wait-for-update workflows.
- [ ] Question edits/replacements and amended answers retain history; stale submissions do not overwrite a newer questionnaire, and resolving one request does not clear unrelated open questions.

### Implementation notes and related work

Extend src/types.ts, src/store.ts comments/context, src/server.ts, src/cli.ts/src/mcp.ts, web/RecordDetail.tsx and web/model.ts attention handling. Reuse the existing question/resolve flow where possible. Related: #26.

### Human review / verification

Submit a mixed questionnaire, leave it unanswered beyond ordinary UI timers, save a partial draft, reload, and finish later. Confirm that an agent receives the explicit answers and that a concurrent question edit triggers reconciliation.

meta.title: Tickets in progress should animate and track the agents progress

before.body:
If in progress would be nice to see how long llm has worked on ticket as well as estimated progress. 

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Make in-progress work easier to monitor with restrained animation, elapsed time, and agent-reported progress that clearly communicates uncertainty.

### Scope and approach

Show current owner/claim, last reported update, elapsed time since entering In Progress, and an optional agent-reported percentage or checklist progress. Elapsed wall-clock time is not measured active work. Running-agent supervision remains outside the initial product; animation must not imply a verified live process.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Cards/rows and ticket details show last reported activity and elapsed time with explicit labels; reload reconstructs elapsed time from durable timestamps.
- [ ] Agents can report a short progress note and optional bounded percentage through CLI/MCP; percentages are labeled estimates, and missing values display as unknown rather than invented.
- [ ] Checklist completion, if shown from #20, is labeled separately from overall completion; 100% never automatically moves a ticket to Done.
- [ ] Expired claims, stale reports, and blockers are visibly distinct from recent reported activity; the UI never treats a claim alone as proof an agent is running.
- [ ] Subtle in-progress animation respects reduced-motion preferences and stops or changes appropriately for blocked/stale/review/done states.
- [ ] Repeated work sessions retain useful history; displayed elapsed duration uses a documented rule for leaving and re-entering In Progress, without double-counting or inventing active hours.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with web/TicketCard.tsx, web/TableView.tsx, src/types.ts, src/store.ts claims/history and CLI/MCP update interfaces. Prefer explicit reported data and disposable derived timers over writing a record every second. Related: #20 and #25.

### Human review / verification

Exercise a fresh report, missing estimate, stale/expired claim, blocker, and re-entry into In Progress with controlled timestamps. Reload and enable reduced motion; verify the labels never claim measured agent runtime.

meta.title: More themes

before.body:
We have themes now for System, Light, and Dark. I like current theme but it would be cool to have more:
- Win95
- Win 3.1
- Commodore 64
- Classic Mac System 7
- AmigaOS
- NES
- SNES
- Synthwave
- Elektron
- Gameboy



## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Offer the requested retro and music-hardware-inspired themes while retaining the current Control Room appearance and readable, usable controls.

### Scope and approach

Treat this as an umbrella for a reusable theme structure and all requested presets: Win95, Win 3.1, Commodore 64, Classic Mac System 7, AmigaOS, NES, SNES, Synthwave, Elektron, and Gameboy. Keep System, Light, and Dark available. Develop representative previews first, then deliver presets in reviewable batches; this ticket is complete only when the agreed full set is available.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A theme picker presents clear names and previews and persists the selected theme with the existing preference model.
- [ ] Each requested preset has a coherent palette, typography, surfaces, borders, focus treatment, and semantic state colors; presets need more than a background-color swap.
- [ ] Board, table, ticket dialogs, conversation, knowledge views, menus, settings, and screenshot tools remain legible and usable in every preset.
- [ ] Keyboard focus, contrast, validation states, blocked/review states, and responsive layouts remain distinguishable without relying solely on color.
- [ ] Theme switching preserves application state and annotation geometry; System continues to follow the operating system appearance.
- [ ] Shared tokens and reusable overrides avoid duplicating application layout or behavior for each theme.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with web/styles.css tokens, web/project.css, web/TopNav.tsx themes, and web/App.tsx preference handling. Use original styling/assets inspired by the references. Create child implementation tickets when this umbrella is selected for development.

### Human review / verification

Review a consistent set of desktop/mobile screenshots for every preset and exercise keyboard focus, long content, error states, and reload persistence. Obtain visual review of representative presets before extending the full set.

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Show the prospective ticket order while dragging so the user knows where the ticket will land before releasing it.

### Scope and approach

Add a stable insertion preview or displaced-row/card preview to existing board and table reordering. Keep the preview local until drop and share the behavior with the planning view in #21.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] While dragging over reorderable tickets, a clear insertion position updates before mouse release, including above the first and below the last item.
- [ ] Moving between valid positions updates the preview without flicker or repeatedly writing record order.
- [ ] Escape, dropping outside a valid target, and canceled drags restore the original visual order without persisted changes.
- [ ] A successful drop persists the displayed placement; failed/stale saves restore or reconcile the list and show an error.
- [ ] Scrolling during a drag keeps the preview aligned; invalid cross-parent/status operations follow existing explicit rules.
- [ ] Keyboard reorder controls remain available, and reduced-motion settings avoid unnecessary movement.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with web/BoardView.tsx, web/TableView.tsx, web/TicketCard.tsx and web/ProjectPage.tsx drag/drop handlers; style in web/project.css. Related: #21, but this fixes the existing reorder interaction independently.

### Human review / verification

Observe a drag before release, cancel it, reorder at both ends, and repeat in a long scrollable list. Confirm canceled previews produce no record writes and the saved order matches the preview.

meta.title: Keep ticket checklists and questionnaires in readable Markdown records

after.body:
## Choice

Microtasks are ordinary checklist lines under a ticket's dedicated level-two Microtasks heading. Only those checklist lines are edited by the checklist controls. Questionnaires extend question comments with stable question IDs and validated metadata, plus readable prompts and submitted answers in their Markdown body.

## Context and rationale

Both humans and agents must read project knowledge without the application. Reusing ticket revisions for checklist edits and comment revisions for questionnaire edits prevents coordinated clients from silently overwriting each other. Browser-only answer drafts are separate from explicitly submitted, human-attributed answers.

## Alternatives and tradeoffs

Separate ticket IDs for every checkbox would clutter the board. A separate questionnaire database would duplicate durable project knowledge. Comment-based forms keep existing Needs-you and context behavior, but structured form metadata is more verbose than plain questions. Replacements and amendments preserve previous wording, answers and history. Drafts are local to a browser and do not expire; they are not automatically shared across browsers.

## Attribution

Implemented by Codex fixes within approved #20 and #27 scope. This is an implementation decision, not a claim of additional human approval.

## References

src/microtasks.ts, src/questionnaire.ts, src/store.ts, web/Questionnaire.tsx

meta.title: Ability to add microtasks to a ticket

before.body:
These are just small tasks that are tracked inside the ticket and don't show up as separate full tickets. Sort of like a checklist of things that need to be done for that ticket. 

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Track small steps inside a ticket with a checklist, without creating separate numbered tickets or cluttering the board.

### Scope and approach

Provide an editable Microtasks section with add, rename, reorder, complete, and remove actions. Keep it readable/editable in Markdown and include it in agent context. Reuse Markdown task-list syntax in a clearly owned section where practical; preserve other prose and existing acceptance criteria.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Enter adds a nonblank checklist item and keeps focus ready for the next; items can be checked, edited, reordered, and removed with keyboard alternatives.
- [ ] Items persist across save/reopen and direct Markdown edits; concurrent changes use revision protection.
- [ ] Agents can read and update checklist state through the supported record interfaces without creating ticket IDs for checklist items.
- [ ] The ticket displays completed/total counts, including the all-complete state; cards may show a compact count without listing every item.
- [ ] Completing the checklist does not automatically move the ticket to Done or claim its acceptance criteria are satisfied.
- [ ] Unrelated Markdown, attachments, and comments survive checklist edits.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with web/RecordDetail.tsx, web/RecordMarkdown.tsx (GFM rendering already exists), src/files.ts Markdown preservation and src/store.ts context. Related: #14 for work large enough to need child tickets; #23 for reducing board clutter.

### Human review / verification

Create/reorder/toggle items, reopen, edit a task in Markdown, and retrieve agent context. Verify a stale toggle cannot overwrite a newer edit and all-complete leaves ticket status unchanged.

meta.title: Add questionaires to tickets for human review

before.body:
If the LLM has questions about a ticket, they can add a questionaire with multiple choice questions or text questions to a ticket and mark it as needing human feedback. 

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Let an agent attach a structured questionnaire to a ticket and request human input, keeping questions and answers in the ticket’s conversation.

### Scope and approach

Support one or more multiple-choice or free-text questions, an explicit needs-feedback state, and answering at the human’s pace. Store structured data durably in Markdown records/metadata and expose it through CLI/MCP context. Keep this distinct from mandatory ticket creation forms.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An agent can submit a questionnaire with stable question IDs, clear prompts, answer types, and optional recommended choices; users can provide custom text where choices are offered.
- [ ] The ticket appears in Needs you with a direct route to its unanswered questionnaire; a separate flag does not silently change its workflow stage.
- [ ] Questions never time out or disappear because the user pauses. Draft answers persist across closing/reopening and refresh, and can be submitted explicitly.
- [ ] No recommended/preselected option counts as an answer until the human submits; required unanswered questions remain visible.
- [ ] Submitted answers retain human attribution, question wording, and timestamps in the conversation, and are readable by agent context and wait-for-update workflows.
- [ ] Question edits/replacements and amended answers retain history; stale submissions do not overwrite a newer questionnaire, and resolving one request does not clear unrelated open questions.

### Implementation notes and related work

Extend src/types.ts, src/store.ts comments/context, src/server.ts, src/cli.ts/src/mcp.ts, web/RecordDetail.tsx and web/model.ts attention handling. Reuse the existing question/resolve flow where possible. Related: #26.

### Human review / verification

Submit a mixed questionnaire, leave it unanswered beyond ordinary UI timers, save a partial draft, reload, and finish later. Confirm that an agent receives the explicit answers and that a concurrent question edit triggers reconciliation.

meta.title: Report progress as attributed estimates and current-session wall-clock time

after.body:
## Choice

The service stamps progress reports with the acting identity and timestamp. Optional percentages are bounded from 0 to 100 and labeled estimates. Entering an In Progress role from another role starts a new session timestamp; moves between In Progress columns retain the session. Prior sessions remain in record history. Displayed elapsed time is derived in the browser rather than written periodically to disk.

## Context and rationale

The tool coordinates agents but does not supervise their execution. A claim or recent report is not proof that an agent process is running. Expired claims and reports older than 30 minutes are labeled explicitly. A percentage, elapsed timer or completed checklist never moves a ticket to Done.

## Alternatives and tradeoffs

Tracking CPU/process time would require an agent execution supervisor outside this release. A lifetime timer would conflate separate implementation attempts. Existing tickets without a session timestamp show Start unknown until their next entry into In Progress; no start time is invented.

## Attribution

Implemented by Codex fixes within approved #28 scope; no new execution-supervision capability is implied.

## References

src/store.ts, web/ProgressReport.tsx, src/cli.ts, src/mcp.ts

meta.title: Tickets in progress should animate and track the agents progress

before.body:
If in progress would be nice to see how long llm has worked on ticket as well as estimated progress. 

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Make in-progress work easier to monitor with restrained animation, elapsed time, and agent-reported progress that clearly communicates uncertainty.

### Scope and approach

Show current owner/claim, last reported update, elapsed time since entering In Progress, and an optional agent-reported percentage or checklist progress. Elapsed wall-clock time is not measured active work. Running-agent supervision remains outside the initial product; animation must not imply a verified live process.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Cards/rows and ticket details show last reported activity and elapsed time with explicit labels; reload reconstructs elapsed time from durable timestamps.
- [ ] Agents can report a short progress note and optional bounded percentage through CLI/MCP; percentages are labeled estimates, and missing values display as unknown rather than invented.
- [ ] Checklist completion, if shown from #20, is labeled separately from overall completion; 100% never automatically moves a ticket to Done.
- [ ] Expired claims, stale reports, and blockers are visibly distinct from recent reported activity; the UI never treats a claim alone as proof an agent is running.
- [ ] Subtle in-progress animation respects reduced-motion preferences and stops or changes appropriately for blocked/stale/review/done states.
- [ ] Repeated work sessions retain useful history; displayed elapsed duration uses a documented rule for leaving and re-entering In Progress, without double-counting or inventing active hours.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with web/TicketCard.tsx, web/TableView.tsx, src/types.ts, src/store.ts claims/history and CLI/MCP update interfaces. Prefer explicit reported data and disposable derived timers over writing a record every second. Related: #20 and #25.

### Human review / verification

Exercise a fresh report, missing estimate, stale/expired claim, blocker, and re-entry into In Progress with controlled timestamps. Reload and enable reduced motion; verify the labels never claim measured agent runtime.

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Let an agent attach a structured questionnaire to a ticket and request human input, keeping questions and answers in the ticket’s conversation.

### Scope and approach

Support one or more multiple-choice or free-text questions, an explicit needs-feedback state, and answering at the human’s pace. Store structured data durably in Markdown records/metadata and expose it through CLI/MCP context. Keep this distinct from mandatory ticket creation forms.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An agent can submit a questionnaire with stable question IDs, clear prompts, answer types, and optional recommended choices; users can provide custom text where choices are offered.
- [ ] The ticket appears in Needs you with a direct route to its unanswered questionnaire; a separate flag does not silently change its workflow stage.
- [ ] Questions never time out or disappear because the user pauses. Draft answers persist across closing/reopening and refresh, and can be submitted explicitly.
- [ ] No recommended/preselected option counts as an answer until the human submits; required unanswered questions remain visible.
- [ ] Submitted answers retain human attribution, question wording, and timestamps in the conversation, and are readable by agent context and wait-for-update workflows.
- [ ] Question edits/replacements and amended answers retain history; stale submissions do not overwrite a newer questionnaire, and resolving one request does not clear unrelated open questions.

### Implementation notes and related work

Extend src/types.ts, src/store.ts comments/context, src/server.ts, src/cli.ts/src/mcp.ts, web/RecordDetail.tsx and web/model.ts attention handling. Reuse the existing question/resolve flow where possible. Related: #26.

### Human review / verification

Submit a mixed questionnaire, leave it unanswered beyond ordinary UI timers, save a partial draft, reload, and finish later. Confirm that an agent receives the explicit answers and that a concurrent question edit triggers reconciliation.

before.body:
If in progress would be nice to see how long llm has worked on ticket as well as estimated progress. 

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Make in-progress work easier to monitor with restrained animation, elapsed time, and agent-reported progress that clearly communicates uncertainty.

### Scope and approach

Show current owner/claim, last reported update, elapsed time since entering In Progress, and an optional agent-reported percentage or checklist progress. Elapsed wall-clock time is not measured active work. Running-agent supervision remains outside the initial product; animation must not imply a verified live process.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Cards/rows and ticket details show last reported activity and elapsed time with explicit labels; reload reconstructs elapsed time from durable timestamps.
- [ ] Agents can report a short progress note and optional bounded percentage through CLI/MCP; percentages are labeled estimates, and missing values display as unknown rather than invented.
- [ ] Checklist completion, if shown from #20, is labeled separately from overall completion; 100% never automatically moves a ticket to Done.
- [ ] Expired claims, stale reports, and blockers are visibly distinct from recent reported activity; the UI never treats a claim alone as proof an agent is running.
- [ ] Subtle in-progress animation respects reduced-motion preferences and stops or changes appropriately for blocked/stale/review/done states.
- [ ] Repeated work sessions retain useful history; displayed elapsed duration uses a documented rule for leaving and re-entering In Progress, without double-counting or inventing active hours.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with web/TicketCard.tsx, web/TableView.tsx, src/types.ts, src/store.ts claims/history and CLI/MCP update interfaces. Prefer explicit reported data and disposable derived timers over writing a record every second. Related: #20 and #25.

### Human review / verification

Exercise a fresh report, missing estimate, stale/expired claim, blocker, and re-entry into In Progress with controlled timestamps. Reload and enable reduced motion; verify the labels never claim measured agent runtime.

before.body:
## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Show the prospective ticket order while dragging so the user knows where the ticket will land before releasing it.

### Scope and approach

Add a stable insertion preview or displaced-row/card preview to existing board and table reordering. Keep the preview local until drop and share the behavior with the planning view in #21.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] While dragging over reorderable tickets, a clear insertion position updates before mouse release, including above the first and below the last item.
- [ ] Moving between valid positions updates the preview without flicker or repeatedly writing record order.
- [ ] Escape, dropping outside a valid target, and canceled drags restore the original visual order without persisted changes.
- [ ] A successful drop persists the displayed placement; failed/stale saves restore or reconcile the list and show an error.
- [ ] Scrolling during a drag keeps the preview aligned; invalid cross-parent/status operations follow existing explicit rules.
- [ ] Keyboard reorder controls remain available, and reduced-motion settings avoid unnecessary movement.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with web/BoardView.tsx, web/TableView.tsx, web/TicketCard.tsx and web/ProjectPage.tsx drag/drop handlers; style in web/project.css. Related: #21, but this fixes the existing reorder interaction independently.

### Human review / verification

Observe a drag before release, cancel it, reorder at both ends, and repeat in a long scrollable list. Confirm canceled previews produce no record writes and the saved order matches the preview.

before.body:
I would like a way to click a swimlane and turn on/off the tickets in that swimline from being visible. For example backlog can be large and I want to turn off backlog and just view the other swimlanes. Maybe a little human eye icon that is in the swimlane header you can click and quickly turn on/off visibility.

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started. Proposed behavior below remains subject to human scope review.

### Intended outcome

Temporarily hide tickets in a busy status column such as Backlog with one click, then restore them just as easily.

### Scope and approach

The Backlog example refers to workflow/status columns (called swimlanes in the request). Add an eye-style visibility toggle to each column header. Hide that column's ticket content across all parent/label groups, retaining a compact labeled header or equivalent visible restore control. This is a visibility preference, not an archive or ticket-status change.

Proposed default: remember hidden column IDs per project and saved view in personal UI preferences, without rewriting the shared view's search query. Keep visibility independent of existing horizontal group collapse. Provide Show all columns and a clear indication of hidden columns.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] One click hides Backlog's cards across all groups and leaves other columns usable. A visible control restores Backlog with one click.
- [ ] Header controls expose an accessible name and pressed/expanded state, work by keyboard, and clearly distinguish hidden from empty columns.
- [ ] No ticket, claim, stage, archive flag or parent relationship changes when toggling visibility.
- [ ] Search/filter changes compose with visibility without losing the user's query. Hidden columns remain identifiable, and Show all recovers from every column being hidden.
- [ ] Visibility is remembered for that project/view after refresh without leaking to another project/view; custom column rename/reorder preserves it by stable ID, and deleted IDs are safely ignored.
- [ ] Board keyboard navigation skips hidden cards, focus stays recoverable after hiding a focused column, and hidden content cannot receive invisible drag/drop or quick-create interactions.
- [ ] Counts and any bulk-action preview make their scope clear; hidden tickets are not silently selected for operations on visible tickets.
- [ ] Table/list views retain their existing behavior; switching back to the board restores its column visibility preferences.

### Implementation notes and related work

Inspect web/BoardView.tsx column rendering and keyboard navigation, web/ProjectPage.tsx view preferences and web/model.ts filters. Related: #44 quick archive, #23 ticket clutter, #18 status customization. Do not conflate this with existing parent-group collapse or automatically create a new shared saved view.

### Human review / verification

Hide Backlog on a populated parent-grouped board, filter the remaining tickets, restore Backlog and refresh. Switch views/projects and rename a custom column. Check keyboard recovery and the all-hidden state.

meta.title: Opt-in trusted-LAN access uses separate paired browser sessions

after.body:
## Choice

Keep loopback-only as the default. An explicit per-project LAN setting enables IPv4 listening with an allowlist of current private interface addresses. Local agent discovery stays at 127.0.0.1. Host and Origin checks remain active, and socket address—not forwarding headers—determines local access.

Remote browsers pair using a host-generated, single-use random code expiring after ten minutes. Each gets a separate project/port-scoped HttpOnly SameSite=Strict session cookie expiring after eight hours. Persist only session hashes in ignored local state. The host can revoke all remote sessions and disable remote access immediately; existing event streams are closed on revocation. The local project token is never automatically issued to remote page requests.

## Context and rationale

The original local browser bootstrap deliberately trusted loopback page loads. Extending that bootstrap unchanged to the LAN would expose project data. Separate credentials keep local agents and native capture independent of remote sessions and their revocation.

## Alternatives and tradeoffs

No anonymous LAN access and no shared long-lived project token in a URL. Local-only operation remains simplest; SSH/VPN or a separately configured trusted TLS transport remain alternatives. This release uses explicitly labeled HTTP on a trusted LAN, not encrypted or public internet hosting. There is no automatic router/firewall configuration. Changing from a loopback-bound service to LAN binding requires a restart; disabling access immediately rejects remote requests and clears remote credentials.

Remote browsers can use board records, comments, screenshots and authenticated backups. Native capture, service shutdown, network administration, canonical-branch reconciliation, configuration changes, host-document import and backup restore stay local. Identity labels remain attribution, not multiple-user permissions.

## Attribution

Implemented by Codex fixes under approved ticket #63. This does not imply a new human approval of public hosting or multi-user collaboration.

after.body:
## Choice

Retain local-only startup and require pairing by default when LAN access is enabled. The host can turn off Require pairing code in Network access settings. In that explicit mode, devices on the permitted trusted LAN can read and edit the project without a code. Host-only controls and Host/origin checks remain enforced, and local tokens are never issued to remote visitors.

Let the host set paired access duration in hours, from 0.25 (15 minutes) to 8760 (365 days), default 8. The value applies to new pairings; existing sessions retain their original expiry unless revoked. The one-use setup code still expires after ten minutes. Keep authentication preferences in ignored project-local state across restarts and CLI mode changes.

Changing whether a code is required clears existing paired sessions and outstanding codes. Turning the requirement back on immediately closes unauthenticated event streams and requires fresh pairing. Open access lasts while LAN is enabled with pairing disabled; it does not use a per-browser access timer. Disable LAN to stop all remote access.

## Context and rationale

The human confirmed a successful connection from another device, but requested optional codes and configurable access duration in the September 27 review of #63. The previous mandatory pairing/eight-hour policy imposed unnecessary friction for this trusted-LAN use case.

## Alternatives and tradeoffs

Mandatory pairing is still the default. Open mode deliberately permits project-wide access to reachable trusted-LAN devices; Settings makes that consequence explicit beside the option. HTTP remains unencrypted. There is no public hosting, automatic firewall change, or separate user permission model. Duration changes apply prospectively to avoid unexpectedly changing already-granted sessions; Revoke all remote sessions resets existing grants immediately.

## Attribution

Chosen by Codex fixes in response to the human's explicit #63 review feedback. This supersedes mandatory pairing and fixed eight-hour duration in DEC-a50e4388f1a92fca while retaining its transport, local-token isolation and host-control boundaries.

We have themes now for System, Light, and Dark. I like current theme but it would be cool to have more:
- Win95
- Win 3.1
- Commodore 64
- Classic Mac System 7
- AmigaOS
- NES
- SNES
- Synthwave
- Elektron
- Gameboy



## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Offer the requested retro and music-hardware-inspired themes while retaining the current Control Room appearance and readable, usable controls.

### Scope and approach

Treat this as an umbrella for a reusable theme structure and all requested presets: Win95, Win 3.1, Commodore 64, Classic Mac System 7, AmigaOS, NES, SNES, Synthwave, Elektron, and Gameboy. Keep System, Light, and Dark available. Develop representative previews first, then deliver presets in reviewable batches; this ticket is complete only when the agreed full set is available.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A theme picker presents clear names and previews and persists the selected theme with the existing preference model.
- [ ] Each requested preset has a coherent palette, typography, surfaces, borders, focus treatment, and semantic state colors; presets need more than a background-color swap.
- [ ] Board, table, ticket dialogs, conversation, knowledge views, menus, settings, and screenshot tools remain legible and usable in every preset.
- [ ] Keyboard focus, contrast, validation states, blocked/review states, and responsive layouts remain distinguishable without relying solely on color.
- [ ] Theme switching preserves application state and annotation geometry; System continues to follow the operating system appearance.
- [ ] Shared tokens and reusable overrides avoid duplicating application layout or behavior for each theme.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with web/styles.css tokens, web/project.css, web/TopNav.tsx themes, and web/App.tsx preference handling. Use original styling/assets inspired by the references. Create child implementation tickets when this umbrella is selected for development.

### Human review / verification

Review a consistent set of desktop/mobile screenshots for every preset and exercise keyboard focus, long content, error states, and reload persistence. Obtain visual review of representative presets before extending the full set.

before.body:
## Intended outcome

Open and use the same project board from another device on the local network while keeping the existing local browser, CLI, worktree coordination and capture service functional.

## Investigation

The current behavior is deliberate, not a missing firewall rule: src/cli.ts binds the service to 127.0.0.1, and src/server.ts rejects non-loopback Host headers. The current browser bootstrap also grants the project cookie to local page requests. Changing only the listener would still fail the Host check; removing both restrictions without replacing the bootstrap would grant project access to any reachable visitor.

## Proposed implementation scope

Add explicit, project-specific LAN access while retaining local-only operation as the default. Show the usable address and connection instructions in the application. Require pairing by default, with a host setting to allow direct trusted-LAN access without a code and a configurable paired-access duration. Never issue the local project credential to remote page requests. Keep local agent discovery pointed at loopback. This ticket concerns the existing single-user board on a trusted local network, not a hosted service or multi-user permission system.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An explicit LAN option exposes the board on the intended local interface and reports usable addresses/port; existing loopback launchers and CLIs continue working.
- [ ] Local-only remains the default. The application reports which mode is active, and disabling LAN prevents further remote access without deleting records.
- [ ] A second device can authenticate and use tickets, comments, screenshots and live updates. When pairing is required, unauthenticated visitors cannot read project records, images, event streams or backups, or perform mutations. When the host explicitly disables pairing, trusted-LAN visitors can use the board directly; host-only controls remain protected.
- [ ] Remote credentials are not embedded in page HTML, asset URLs, logs or ordinary share links. Pairing/session expiration and revocation have a clear recovery path.
- [ ] Host/origin checks remain explicit and project sessions remain isolated across projects/ports. Cross-origin requests and arbitrary Host headers remain rejected.
- [ ] The chosen transport and its limitations are documented accurately; remote connection setup must not imply encryption that is absent. No router port forwarding or public exposure is configured automatically.
- [ ] Local-machine controls such as native capture, shutdown and filesystem import/restore receive an explicit remote-access policy instead of becoming accidentally available through a listener change.
- [ ] Existing running-service discovery, restarts and project-specific launchers honor the selected mode. Address changes, unavailable interfaces and firewall failures produce actionable connection guidance.
- [ ] Automated tests cover local-only behavior, authenticated/unauthenticated LAN requests, origin/Host rejection, credential isolation and revocation. Verify a real second-device browser connection separately from same-machine HTTP tests.

## Verification and decision notes

Record the concrete authentication, transport and opt-in design as a project decision before implementing it. Existing approved scope is preserved. The September 27 review confirmed a successful second-device connection and amended scope to optional pairing codes and configurable paired-access duration. See linked successor decision DEC-0424c8f99e4f4a31.

meta.title: Bundle pixel typography and reuse real actions in retro window menus

after.body:
## Choice

Use pinned, locally served Pixelify Sans for retro body/control typography and Silkscreen for chunky hardware/console display lettering, including Elektron and Game Boy. Ship the original OFL attribution/licenses with the web assets. Use shared theme tokens and one optional window-menu component; the retro desktop presets show actual Save/Close/View commands wired to existing handlers.

Windows 95 uses a blue caption and beveled close button, Windows 3.1 a centered caption and left system-menu-style close gadget, System 7 horizontal title stripes and a left close box, and AmigaOS a blue Workbench-style frame. All keep keyboard-accessible, labeled close controls. Other themes retain their existing window layout.

## Context and rationale

Human review of #19 requested less modern fonts, chunkier Elektron/Game Boy type and OS-inspired window/menu bars. Installed-font fallbacks vary by device and rendered as modern system fonts on macOS. Bundled fonts give repeatable offline rendering and menu commands stay functional instead of decorative.

## Alternatives and tradeoffs

These are original, period-inspired treatments, not exact replicas or extracted proprietary OS font assets. Modern OS font fallbacks were smaller but inconsistent; remote font CDNs would add a network dependency. Pixel display type is limited to suitable headings/controls with more readable proportional pixel text for prose and unchanged monospace code rendering. Existing interactions, record storage and screenshot geometry are reused.

## Attribution

Codex fixes implementing the human's September 27 #19 review. Fonts: Pixelify Sans Project Authors and Silkscreen Project Authors, SIL Open Font License 1.1. The app bundles unmodified font files from pinned Fontsource 5.3.0 packages.

meta.title: Orchestrator-led delegation, agent review and human escalation

after.body:
## Intended outcome

Let a designated reviewer/orchestrator agent coordinate workers through Control Room, independently review their submissions, accept satisfactory work into Done, and escalate work that needs human judgment or feedback. The human sees a clear account of who is doing what and why work was accepted or escalated.

## Requested workflow

1. Orchestrator decomposes permitted work into tickets, adds acceptance criteria/dependencies/context and assigns a named worker.
2. Worker acknowledges/claims the assignment, works in its checkout, reports progress or blockers, and submits a handoff plus verification evidence to Review.
3. Orchestrator inspects the implementation against the acceptance criteria, applicable decisions and UI rules. It checks the submitted code state and performs independent verification where appropriate.
4. Orchestrator records one of three outcomes: Accept into Done; Request changes with actionable feedback; Needs human with a specific question or review request.
5. Human responses return the ticket to the appropriate worker/reviewer queue without losing the prior review history. Humans can override/reopen outcomes.

## Proposed product rules

- Keep worker, orchestrator and human roles distinct. Agents remain attributed as agents and never impersonate a human to accept work. Human explicitly designates an orchestrator and can revoke its authority. The existing human-review workflow remains the default unless orchestration is enabled.
- Worker submissions do not self-approve. Record assignment, worker identity, reviewer identity, outcome, rationale, acceptance criteria checked, evidence and reviewed code state separately. Flag cases where the reviewer also performed implementation for independent/human review.
- Delegation uses durable assignments separate from expiring execution claims. Assigned does not mean acknowledged, claimed does not prove running, and expired claims do not silently free an active worker's checkout. Reassignment preserves history and handles late submissions explicitly.
- Review decisions take the ticket revision and the submitted code/evidence identity. Changed submissions require fresh review. A green test alone is not proof of the intended outcome. Missing or stale evidence must be resolved or escalated.
- Needs human is explicit routing of a question/review, not an ambiguous blocker string. Explain what the human must decide, show the relevant diff/screenshot/evidence, and preserve any unsent feedback. Human-required tickets cannot be quietly auto-accepted.
- Acceptance is separate from Git operations. Do not implicitly merge, push or deploy when accepting a ticket. Where the project defines integration as part of Done, verify the integrated result before acceptance.
- Parent completion remains a deliberate outcome review, not automatic completion when children close.
- Show the agent roster, assigned/claimed work, review queue, Needs human queue, review outcome badges and acceptance history in the UI. Keep authoritative records readable in Markdown.
- Expose matching CLI/MCP operations and role-specific context/protocols so different models and coding tools can participate.
- Identity labels are workflow attribution for agents sharing the local account; they are not a strong isolation/security boundary.

## Open interview choices

Two questions have been presented in the Codex question interface. Do not treat defaults as answers:

1. Delegation transport: assign to agents the human already has running, or launch/supervise agents from Control Room? Recommended first increment: existing agents consume assignments through CLI/MCP. Native process launch/supervision would be a separate adapter layer if chosen.
2. Scope authority: only human-approved goals/tickets, or autonomous backlog selection? Recommended default: retain human-approved scope and allow decomposition/prioritization inside it.

Further details to settle after those answers: first supported agent harnesses if launching is required; circumstances that must always require human acceptance; integration policy for separate worktrees; bounded retries and escalation behavior.

## Implementation outline (proposal)

A. Role/policy configuration, review routing and durable review receipts; preserve existing human behavior and Markdown compatibility.
B. Assignment/acknowledgment/reassignment, worker queues, dependencies and worktree conflict visibility, CLI/MCP protocol.
C. Orchestrator review context and accept/changes/escalate operations, evidence/code identity checks, human-response continuation and parent review.
D. Human dashboard and history, plus a documented end-to-end trial with at least two workers.
E. Launch/supervision adapters only if selected during the interview.

## Acceptance checks

- Two named workers can receive distinct assignments and cannot silently overwrite claims or review decisions.
- A worker cannot accept its own work or grant itself reviewer/scope authority through ordinary workflow operations.
- A designated orchestrator can accept a permitted current submission with an attributed review receipt, request changes, or escalate it with a specific question.
- Human-required work, changed evidence/code, revoked reviewer authority, stale revisions, expired claims, late submissions and retry exhaustion have explicit outcomes.
- Questions do not expire. Human answers, review history, assignments and acceptance receipts survive service restart and Markdown reload.
- The board distinguishes orchestrator-accepted from human-accepted work and exposes any unverified integration state.
- Existing projects retain their current human-only acceptance behavior until orchestration is explicitly enabled.

## Related work and implementation starting points

Related: #58 (human review queue), #28 (reported progress), #31 (decision protocol), #26 (agent playbook). Reuse these rather than creating competing queues/protocols.

Current enforcement lives in src/store.ts assertAgent/reviewOutcome; Actor only distinguishes human/agent in src/types.ts. CLI/MCP and generated context currently promise human-only Done. Update these together when the interview choices are settled. This ticket records the product proposal; implementation has not started and unanswered choices are not approved defaults.
