before.body:
I would like a way to click a swimlane and turn on/off the tickets in that swimline from being visible. For example backlog can be large and I want to turn off backlog and just view the other swimlanes. Maybe a little human eye icon that is in the swimlane header you can click and quickly turn on/off visibility.

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started. Proposed behavior below remains subject to human scope review.

### Intended outcome

Temporarily hide tickets in a busy status column such as Backlog with one click, then restore them just as easily.

### Scope and approach

The Backlog example refers to workflow/status columns (called swimlanes in the request). Add an eye-style visibility toggle to each column header. Hide that column's ticket content across all parent/label groups, retaining a compact labeled header or equivalent visible restore control. This is a visibility preference, not an archive or ticket-status change.

Proposed default: remember hidden column IDs per project and saved view in personal UI preferences, without rewriting the shared view's search query. Keep visibility independent of existing horizontal group collapse. Provide Show all columns and a clear indication of hidden columns.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] One click hides Backlog's cards across all groups and leaves other columns usable. A visible control restores Backlog with one click.
- [ ] Header controls expose an accessible name and pressed/expanded state, work by keyboard, and clearly distinguish hidden from empty columns.
- [ ] No ticket, claim, stage, archive flag or parent relationship changes when toggling visibility.
- [ ] Search/filter changes compose with visibility without losing the user's query. Hidden columns remain identifiable, and Show all recovers from every column being hidden.
- [ ] Visibility is remembered for that project/view after refresh without leaking to another project/view; custom column rename/reorder preserves it by stable ID, and deleted IDs are safely ignored.
- [ ] Board keyboard navigation skips hidden cards, focus stays recoverable after hiding a focused column, and hidden content cannot receive invisible drag/drop or quick-create interactions.
- [ ] Counts and any bulk-action preview make their scope clear; hidden tickets are not silently selected for operations on visible tickets.
- [ ] Table/list views retain their existing behavior; switching back to the board restores its column visibility preferences.

### Implementation notes and related work

Inspect web/BoardView.tsx column rendering and keyboard navigation, web/ProjectPage.tsx view preferences and web/model.ts filters. Related: #44 quick archive, #23 ticket clutter, #18 status customization. Do not conflate this with existing parent-group collapse or automatically create a new shared saved view.

### Human review / verification

Hide Backlog on a populated parent-grouped board, filter the remaining tickets, restore Backlog and refresh. Switch views/projects and rename a custom column. Check keyboard recovery and the all-hidden state.

after.body:
I would like a way to click a swimlane and turn on/off the tickets in that swimline from being visible. For example backlog can be large and I want to turn off backlog and just view the other swimlanes. Maybe a little human eye icon that is in the swimlane header you can click and quickly turn on/off visibility.

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started. Proposed behavior below remains subject to human scope review.

### Intended outcome

Temporarily hide tickets in a busy status column such as Backlog with one click, then restore them just as easily.

### Scope and approach

The Backlog example refers to workflow/status columns (called swimlanes in the request). Add an eye-style visibility toggle to each column header. Hide that column's ticket content across all parent/label groups, retaining a compact labeled header or equivalent visible restore control. This is a visibility preference, not an archive or ticket-status change.

Proposed default: remember hidden column IDs per project and saved view in personal UI preferences, without rewriting the shared view's search query. Keep visibility independent of existing horizontal group collapse. Provide Show all columns and a clear indication of hidden columns.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] One click hides Backlog's cards across all groups and leaves other columns usable. A visible control restores Backlog with one click.
- [ ] Header controls expose an accessible name and pressed/expanded state, work by keyboard, and clearly distinguish hidden from empty columns.
- [ ] No ticket, claim, stage, archive flag or parent relationship changes when toggling visibility.
- [ ] Search/filter changes compose with visibility without losing the user's query. Hidden columns remain identifiable, and Show all recovers from every column being hidden.
- [ ] Visibility is remembered for that project/view after refresh without leaking to another project/view; custom column rename/reorder preserves it by stable ID, and deleted IDs are safely ignored.
- [ ] Board keyboard navigation skips hidden cards, focus stays recoverable after hiding a focused column, and hidden content cannot receive invisible drag/drop or quick-create interactions.
- [ ] Counts and any bulk-action preview make their scope clear; hidden tickets are not silently selected for operations on visible tickets.
- [ ] Table/list views retain their existing behavior; switching back to the board restores its column visibility preferences.

### Implementation notes and related work

Inspect web/BoardView.tsx column rendering and keyboard navigation, web/ProjectPage.tsx view preferences and web/model.ts filters. Related: #44 quick archive, #23 ticket clutter, #18 status customization. Do not conflate this with existing parent-group collapse or automatically create a new shared saved view.

### Human review / verification

Hide Backlog on a populated parent-grouped board, filter the remaining tickets, restore Backlog and refresh. Switch views/projects and rename a custom column. Check keyboard recovery and the all-hidden state.

before.body:
If the LLM has questions about a ticket, they can add a questionaire with multiple choice questions or text questions to a ticket and mark it as needing human feedback. 

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Let an agent attach a structured questionnaire to a ticket and request human input, keeping questions and answers in the ticket’s conversation.

### Scope and approach

Support one or more multiple-choice or free-text questions, an explicit needs-feedback state, and answering at the human’s pace. Store structured data durably in Markdown records/metadata and expose it through CLI/MCP context. Keep this distinct from mandatory ticket creation forms.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An agent can submit a questionnaire with stable question IDs, clear prompts, answer types, and optional recommended choices; users can provide custom text where choices are offered.
- [ ] The ticket appears in Needs you with a direct route to its unanswered questionnaire; a separate flag does not silently change its workflow stage.
- [ ] Questions never time out or disappear because the user pauses. Draft answers persist across closing/reopening and refresh, and can be submitted explicitly.
- [ ] No recommended/preselected option counts as an answer until the human submits; required unanswered questions remain visible.
- [ ] Submitted answers retain human attribution, question wording, and timestamps in the conversation, and are readable by agent context and wait-for-update workflows.
- [ ] Question edits/replacements and amended answers retain history; stale submissions do not overwrite a newer questionnaire, and resolving one request does not clear unrelated open questions.

### Implementation notes and related work

Extend src/types.ts, src/store.ts comments/context, src/server.ts, src/cli.ts/src/mcp.ts, web/RecordDetail.tsx and web/model.ts attention handling. Reuse the existing question/resolve flow where possible. Related: #26.

### Human review / verification

Submit a mixed questionnaire, leave it unanswered beyond ordinary UI timers, save a partial draft, reload, and finish later. Confirm that an agent receives the explicit answers and that a concurrent question edit triggers reconciliation.

after.body:
If the LLM has questions about a ticket, they can add a questionaire with multiple choice questions or text questions to a ticket and mark it as needing human feedback. 

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Let an agent attach a structured questionnaire to a ticket and request human input, keeping questions and answers in the ticket’s conversation.

### Scope and approach

Support one or more multiple-choice or free-text questions, an explicit needs-feedback state, and answering at the human’s pace. Store structured data durably in Markdown records/metadata and expose it through CLI/MCP context. Keep this distinct from mandatory ticket creation forms.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An agent can submit a questionnaire with stable question IDs, clear prompts, answer types, and optional recommended choices; users can provide custom text where choices are offered.
- [ ] The ticket appears in Needs you with a direct route to its unanswered questionnaire; a separate flag does not silently change its workflow stage.
- [ ] Questions never time out or disappear because the user pauses. Draft answers persist across closing/reopening and refresh, and can be submitted explicitly.
- [ ] No recommended/preselected option counts as an answer until the human submits; required unanswered questions remain visible.
- [ ] Submitted answers retain human attribution, question wording, and timestamps in the conversation, and are readable by agent context and wait-for-update workflows.
- [ ] Question edits/replacements and amended answers retain history; stale submissions do not overwrite a newer questionnaire, and resolving one request does not clear unrelated open questions.

### Implementation notes and related work

Extend src/types.ts, src/store.ts comments/context, src/server.ts, src/cli.ts/src/mcp.ts, web/RecordDetail.tsx and web/model.ts attention handling. Reuse the existing question/resolve flow where possible. Related: #26.

### Human review / verification

Submit a mixed questionnaire, leave it unanswered beyond ordinary UI timers, save a partial draft, reload, and finish later. Confirm that an agent receives the explicit answers and that a concurrent question edit triggers reconciliation.

before.body:
I don't like the look of having the checkboxes on the tickets. 

Need to instead be able to shift + select to select multiple tickets on a kanban board view. 

Also need to be able to shift select edit cells in the table view like you would edit a spreadsheet. I should be able to easily use shortcuts to copy paste, so if I wanted to make a bunch of tickets low priority it would be easy.

I don't like the look of having the checkboxes on the tickets.

I don't like the look of having the checkboxes on the tickets. 

Need to instead be able to shift + select to select multiple tickets on a kanban board view. 

Also need to be able to shift select edit cells in the table view like you would edit a spreadsheet. I should be able to easily use shortcuts to copy paste, so if I wanted to make a bunch of tickets low priority it would be easy.

after.body:
## Outcome
Allow a human-authorized chat orchestrator to take over an interrupted managed worker ticket under its own identity, without impersonating the worker or bypassing record protections.

## Reproduction
On #67 the user explicitly requested direct implementation by the chat. Stopping Sol run run-55ab1dec62f77f03 halted execution but retained the acknowledged service-owned assignment. A claim by Codex chat orchestrator returned HTTP 409: Assigned to Sol. Ordinary record updates and manual review submission remain subject to the same assignment guard. The implementation can be completed safely in the stopped checkout, but the board cannot represent the takeover through its existing API.

## Acceptance criteria
- Provide an explicit authorized release/reassignment operation for the configured orchestrator or a human.
- Verify all owned/original worker processes have exited; refuse takeover of active or uncertain processes.
- Serialize the change with current ticket revision and assignment/run identity checks.
- Preserve prior assignment, run, worktree, logs and attribution in history; release only the obsolete claim.
- Allow the new actor to claim, report progress and submit human review using its own identity.
- Do not grant scope approval, reset attempt limits, self-accept an implementation, or forge human attribution.
- Cover active-process refusal, stale revisions, unauthorized workers, successful stopped-run takeover, and unrelated assignment preservation.

## Implementation references
src/orchestration.ts stop(), src/store.ts claim()/updateNow(), src/server.ts orchestration routes.

## Scope
Backlog finding only; not implemented as part of the #67 scrolling correction.

before.body:
These are just small tasks that are tracked inside the ticket and don't show up as separate full tickets. Sort of like a checklist of things that need to be done for that ticket. 

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Track small steps inside a ticket with a checklist, without creating separate numbered tickets or cluttering the board.

### Scope and approach

Provide an editable Microtasks section with add, rename, reorder, complete, and remove actions. Keep it readable/editable in Markdown and include it in agent context. Reuse Markdown task-list syntax in a clearly owned section where practical; preserve other prose and existing acceptance criteria.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Enter adds a nonblank checklist item and keeps focus ready for the next; items can be checked, edited, reordered, and removed with keyboard alternatives.
- [ ] Items persist across save/reopen and direct Markdown edits; concurrent changes use revision protection.
- [ ] Agents can read and update checklist state through the supported record interfaces without creating ticket IDs for checklist items.
- [ ] The ticket displays completed/total counts, including the all-complete state; cards may show a compact count without listing every item.
- [ ] Completing the checklist does not automatically move the ticket to Done or claim its acceptance criteria are satisfied.
- [ ] Unrelated Markdown, attachments, and comments survive checklist edits.

### Implementation notes and related work

These are just small tasks that are tracked inside the ticket and don't show up as separate full tickets. Sort of like a checklist of things that need to be done for that ticket. 

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Track small steps inside a ticket with a checklist, without creating separate numbered tickets or cluttering the board.

### Scope and approach

Provide an editable Microtasks section with add, rename, reorder, complete, and remove actions. Keep it readable/editable in Markdown and include it in agent context. Reuse Markdown task-list syntax in a clearly owned section where practical; preserve other prose and existing acceptance criteria.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Enter adds a nonblank checklist item and keeps focus ready for the next; items can be checked, edited, reordered, and removed with keyboard alternatives.
- [ ] Items persist across save/reopen and direct Markdown edits; concurrent changes use revision protection.
- [ ] Agents can read and update checklist state through the supported record interfaces without creating ticket IDs for checklist items.
- [ ] The ticket displays completed/total counts, including the all-complete state; cards may show a compact count without listing every item.
- [ ] Completing the checklist does not automatically move the ticket to Done or claim its acceptance criteria are satisfied.
- [ ] Unrelated Markdown, attachments, and comments survive checklist edits.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with web/RecordDetail.tsx, web/RecordMarkdown.tsx (GFM rendering already exists), src/files.ts Markdown preservation and src/store.ts context. Related: #14 for work large enough to need child tickets; #23 for reducing board clutter.

### Human review / verification

Create/reorder/toggle items, reopen, edit a task in Markdown, and retrieve agent context. Verify a stale toggle cannot overwrite a newer edit and all-complete leaves ticket status unchanged.

## Microtasks

- [x] Test microtask

- [x] Second microtask

meta.title: Have a view in which I can sort ticket priority by vertically reordering tickets

before.body:
## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Provide a dedicated vertical planning view where dragging tickets changes the order in which work should be considered.

### Scope and approach

Build on the saved table view and existing manual/priority sorting. Offer an obvious Priority planning preset, rank tickets within priority groups, and allow explicit movement into another priority group. Ordering must not silently change workflow status or parent. Explain that priority is the urgency bucket and rank is the order within it.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The planning view shows a vertical list with priority groups and visible drag handles, including the start/end of each group.
- [ ] Dragging within a group changes persistent relative rank; dragging to another priority group updates priority and rank visibly.
- [ ] Reordering across tickets with different statuses does not move either ticket to the other status or change its parent.
- [ ] Move up/down and move-to-priority controls provide keyboard alternatives, including first/last positions.
- [ ] Reloading or returning to the saved view retains the order; concurrent reorder failures reconcile without losing tickets.
- [ ] Filtered reordering uses defined visible anchors and preserves the relative order of hidden tickets; saved sort modes clearly indicate whether manual reordering is active.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with web/ProjectPage.tsx place/peersOf, web/TableView.tsx and web/model.ts sortTickets. Current place also copies the target status, so reuse needs care. Coordinate drag preview with #22; prefer existing order metadata over a second competing ranking field.

### Human review / verification

Rank tickets across several stages and priorities, move to first/last, refresh, and repeat with a filter and keyboard controls. Confirm that status/parent stay unchanged and priority changes only when crossing an explicit priority group.

before.body:
## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Show the prospective ticket order while dragging so the user knows where the ticket will land before releasing it.

### Scope and approach

Add a stable insertion preview or displaced-row/card preview to existing board and table reordering. Keep the preview local until drop and share the behavior with the planning view in #21.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] While dragging over reorderable tickets, a clear insertion position updates before mouse release, including above the first and below the last item.
- [ ] Moving between valid positions updates the preview without flicker or repeatedly writing record order.
- [ ] Escape, dropping outside a valid target, and canceled drags restore the original visual order without persisted changes.
- [ ] A successful drop persists the displayed placement; failed/stale saves restore or reconcile the list and show an error.
- [ ] Scrolling during a drag keeps the preview aligned; invalid cross-parent/status operations follow existing explicit rules.
- [ ] Keyboard reorder controls remain available, and reduced-motion settings avoid unnecessary movement.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with web/BoardView.tsx, web/TableView.tsx, web/TicketCard.tsx and web/ProjectPage.tsx drag/drop handlers; style in web/project.css. Related: #21, but this fixes the existing reorder interaction independently.

### Human review / verification

Observe a drag before release, cancel it, reorder at both ends, and repeat in a long scrollable list. Confirm canceled previews produce no record writes and the saved order matches the preview.

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Show the prospective ticket order while dragging so the user knows where the ticket will land before releasing it.

### Scope and approach

Add a stable insertion preview or displaced-row/card preview to existing board and table reordering. Keep the preview local until drop and share the behavior with the planning view in #21.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] While dragging over reorderable tickets, a clear insertion position updates before mouse release, including above the first and below the last item.
- [ ] Moving between valid positions updates the preview without flicker or repeatedly writing record order.
- [ ] Escape, dropping outside a valid target, and canceled drags restore the original visual order without persisted changes.
- [ ] A successful drop persists the displayed placement; failed/stale saves restore or reconcile the list and show an error.
- [ ] Scrolling during a drag keeps the preview aligned; invalid cross-parent/status operations follow existing explicit rules.
- [ ] Keyboard reorder controls remain available, and reduced-motion settings avoid unnecessary movement.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with web/BoardView.tsx, web/TableView.tsx, web/TicketCard.tsx and web/ProjectPage.tsx drag/drop handlers; style in web/project.css. Related: #21, but this fixes the existing reorder interaction independently.

### Human review / verification

Observe a drag before release, cancel it, reorder at both ends, and repeat in a long scrollable list. Confirm canceled previews produce no record writes and the saved order matches the preview.

before.body:
If in progress would be nice to see how long llm has worked on ticket as well as estimated progress. 

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Make in-progress work easier to monitor with restrained animation, elapsed time, and agent-reported progress that clearly communicates uncertainty.

### Scope and approach

Show current owner/claim, last reported update, elapsed time since entering In Progress, and an optional agent-reported percentage or checklist progress. Elapsed wall-clock time is not measured active work. Running-agent supervision remains outside the initial product; animation must not imply a verified live process.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Cards/rows and ticket details show last reported activity and elapsed time with explicit labels; reload reconstructs elapsed time from durable timestamps.
- [ ] Agents can report a short progress note and optional bounded percentage through CLI/MCP; percentages are labeled estimates, and missing values display as unknown rather than invented.

If in progress would be nice to see how long llm has worked on ticket as well as estimated progress. 

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Make in-progress work easier to monitor with restrained animation, elapsed time, and agent-reported progress that clearly communicates uncertainty.

### Scope and approach

Show current owner/claim, last reported update, elapsed time since entering In Progress, and an optional agent-reported percentage or checklist progress. Elapsed wall-clock time is not measured active work. Running-agent supervision remains outside the initial product; animation must not imply a verified live process.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Cards/rows and ticket details show last reported activity and elapsed time with explicit labels; reload reconstructs elapsed time from durable timestamps.
- [ ] Agents can report a short progress note and optional bounded percentage through CLI/MCP; percentages are labeled estimates, and missing values display as unknown rather than invented.
- [ ] Checklist completion, if shown from #20, is labeled separately from overall completion; 100% never automatically moves a ticket to Done.
- [ ] Expired claims, stale reports, and blockers are visibly distinct from recent reported activity; the UI never treats a claim alone as proof an agent is running.
- [ ] Subtle in-progress animation respects reduced-motion preferences and stops or changes appropriately for blocked/stale/review/done states.
- [ ] Repeated work sessions retain useful history; displayed elapsed duration uses a documented rule for leaving and re-entering In Progress, without double-counting or inventing active hours.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with web/TicketCard.tsx, web/TableView.tsx, src/types.ts, src/store.ts claims/history and CLI/MCP update interfaces. Prefer explicit reported data and disposable derived timers over writing a record every second. Related: #20 and #25.

### Human review / verification

Exercise a fresh report, missing estimate, stale/expired claim, blocker, and re-entry into In Progress with controlled timestamps. Reload and enable reduced motion; verify the labels never claim measured agent runtime.

before.body:
I would like a way to click a swimlane and turn on/off the tickets in that swimline from being visible. For example backlog can be large and I want to turn off backlog and just view the other swimlanes. Maybe a little human eye icon that is in the swimlane header you can click and quickly turn on/off visibility.

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started. Proposed behavior below remains subject to human scope review.

### Intended outcome

Temporarily hide tickets in a busy status column such as Backlog with one click, then restore them just as easily.

### Scope and approach

The Backlog example refers to workflow/status columns (called swimlanes in the request). Add an eye-style visibility toggle to each column header. Hide that column's ticket content across all parent/label groups, retaining a compact labeled header or equivalent visible restore control. This is a visibility preference, not an archive or ticket-status change.

Proposed default: remember hidden column IDs per project and saved view in personal UI preferences, without rewriting the shared view's search query. Keep visibility independent of existing horizontal group collapse. Provide Show all columns and a clear indication of hidden columns.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] One click hides Backlog's cards across all groups and leaves other columns usable. A visible control restores Backlog with one click.
- [ ] Header controls expose an accessible name and pressed/expanded state, work by keyboard, and clearly distinguish hidden from empty columns.
- [ ] No ticket, claim, stage, archive flag or parent relationship changes when toggling visibility.
- [ ] Search/filter changes compose with visibility without losing the user's query. Hidden columns remain identifiable, and Show all recovers from every column being hidden.
- [ ] Visibility is remembered for that project/view after refresh without leaking to another project/view; custom column rename/reorder preserves it by stable ID, and deleted IDs are safely ignored.

after.body:
I would like a way to click a swimlane and turn on/off the tickets in that swimline from being visible. For example backlog can be large and I want to turn off backlog and just view the other swimlanes. Maybe a little human eye icon that is in the swimlane header you can click and quickly turn on/off visibility.

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started. Proposed behavior below remains subject to human scope review.

### Intended outcome

Temporarily hide tickets in a busy status column such as Backlog with one click, then restore them just as easily.

### Scope and approach

The Backlog example refers to workflow/status columns (called swimlanes in the request). Add an eye-style visibility toggle to each column header. Hide that column's ticket content across all parent/label groups, retaining a compact labeled header or equivalent visible restore control. This is a visibility preference, not an archive or ticket-status change.

Proposed default: remember hidden column IDs per project and saved view in personal UI preferences, without rewriting the shared view's search query. Keep visibility independent of existing horizontal group collapse. Provide Show all columns and a clear indication of hidden columns.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] One click hides Backlog's cards across all groups and leaves other columns usable. A visible control restores Backlog with one click.
- [ ] Header controls expose an accessible name and pressed/expanded state, work by keyboard, and clearly distinguish hidden from empty columns.
- [ ] No ticket, claim, stage, archive flag or parent relationship changes when toggling visibility.
- [ ] Search/filter changes compose with visibility without losing the user's query. Hidden columns remain identifiable, and Show all recovers from every column being hidden.
- [ ] Visibility is remembered for that project/view after refresh without leaking to another project/view; custom column rename/reorder preserves it by stable ID, and deleted IDs are safely ignored.
- [ ] Board keyboard navigation skips hidden cards, focus stays recoverable after hiding a focused column, and hidden content cannot receive invisible drag/drop or quick-create interactions.
- [ ] Counts and any bulk-action preview make their scope clear; hidden tickets are not silently selected for operations on visible tickets.
- [ ] Table/list views retain their existing behavior; switching back to the board restores its column visibility preferences.

### Implementation notes and related work

Inspect web/BoardView.tsx column rendering and keyboard navigation, web/ProjectPage.tsx view preferences and web/model.ts filters. Related: #44 quick archive, #23 ticket clutter, #18 status customization. Do not conflate this with existing parent-group collapse or automatically create a new shared saved view.

### Human review / verification

Hide Backlog on a populated parent-grouped board, filter the remaining tickets, restore Backlog and refresh. Switch views/projects and rename a custom column. Check keyboard recovery and the all-hidden state.

meta.title: Should be able to customize and change the statuses

before.body:
## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Make workflow status customization easy to discover from the board and safe to use as the project evolves.

### Scope and approach

Settings already supports naming, roles, ordering, addition, and removal of columns. Expose a clear Customize statuses entry from the board and improve that existing editor. Retain stable IDs and explain why workflow roles control agent behavior; multiple columns can share a role, as Concept and Backlog do here.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A user can find status customization from the board, add a status, rename it, and change its order without editing configuration files.
- [ ] Renaming or reordering retains ticket associations, history, and saved views; refreshing preserves the configuration.
- [ ] The editor distinguishes display name from workflow role and validates required roles and invalid/blank names.
- [ ] Removing a populated status offers an explicit destination/migration flow or a clear route to move its tickets first; no tickets are orphaned.
- [ ] Where a role has multiple columns, default destinations for new tickets and agent role-based moves are visible and deterministic.
- [ ] Concurrent configuration changes cause reconciliation feedback rather than silent overwrites.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with web/Settings.tsx, web/ProjectPage.tsx, src/store.ts updateConfig and role-to-column lookups in src/cli.ts/src/mcp.ts. Extend existing configuration rather than introducing competing status data.

### Human review / verification

Add and rename a status, reorder it, reload, and remove an empty status. Exercise removal with tickets and ambiguous role destinations using Concept/Backlog and In Progress/Failed Review.

meta.title: Have a view in which I can sort ticket priority by vertically reordering tickets

before.body:
## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Provide a dedicated vertical planning view where dragging tickets changes the order in which work should be considered.

### Scope and approach

Build on the saved table view and existing manual/priority sorting. Offer an obvious Priority planning preset, rank tickets within priority groups, and allow explicit movement into another priority group. Ordering must not silently change workflow status or parent. Explain that priority is the urgency bucket and rank is the order within it.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The planning view shows a vertical list with priority groups and visible drag handles, including the start/end of each group.
- [ ] Dragging within a group changes persistent relative rank; dragging to another priority group updates priority and rank visibly.
- [ ] Reordering across tickets with different statuses does not move either ticket to the other status or change its parent.
- [ ] Move up/down and move-to-priority controls provide keyboard alternatives, including first/last positions.
- [ ] Reloading or returning to the saved view retains the order; concurrent reorder failures reconcile without losing tickets.
- [ ] Filtered reordering uses defined visible anchors and preserves the relative order of hidden tickets; saved sort modes clearly indicate whether manual reordering is active.

### Implementation notes and related work

### Intended outcome

Offer a newest-first project activity feed so a human can quickly see what changed across tickets and project knowledge.

before.body:
## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Give users a Help/Playbook tab with short, copyable prompts for working with their existing coding agent and this project board.

### Scope and approach

Provide concise recipes for connection/setup, refining Concept tickets, planning an approved parent, picking up work, reporting progress, submitting review evidence, responding to feedback, documenting decisions, and maintaining the rulebook. Include screenshot feedback and shortcut help; no embedded provider or agent execution is required.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An in-app Help/Playbook entry offers searchable or clearly grouped recipes, each with its purpose, prerequisites, and a short copyable prompt.
- [ ] Prompts use real project context where available and clearly mark user-supplied placeholders; copied text contains no local auth tokens or hidden secrets.
- [ ] Ticket-specific recipes use public numbers with shell-safe examples and explain scope approval, claims, Review, and human acceptance.
- [ ] Setup guidance matches the shipped CLI/MCP protocol; the source stays easy to update alongside AGENT_GUIDE.md.
- [ ] Copy confirms success accessibly, supports keyboard use, and has a fallback if clipboard access is unavailable.
- [ ] The playbook works offline and lets the user choose where to paste/run a prompt; clicking Copy does not start an agent or mutate tickets.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with AGENT_GUIDE.md, CLI help, web/Shortcuts.tsx, web/TopNav.tsx and web/Pages.tsx. Prefer a small shared content source to duplicated instructions that drift. Related: #27 for collecting human answers.

### Human review / verification

Follow the setup and review recipes against a disposable project using current CLI commands. Copy a ticket-specific prompt and verify correct number/context, no secrets, and no automatic execution.

meta.title: Should be able to customize and change the statuses

before.body:
## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Make workflow status customization easy to discover from the board and safe to use as the project evolves.

### Scope and approach

Settings already supports naming, roles, ordering, addition, and removal of columns. Expose a clear Customize statuses entry from the board and improve that existing editor. Retain stable IDs and explain why workflow roles control agent behavior; multiple columns can share a role, as Concept and Backlog do here.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A user can find status customization from the board, add a status, rename it, and change its order without editing configuration files.
- [ ] Renaming or reordering retains ticket associations, history, and saved views; refreshing preserves the configuration.
- [ ] The editor distinguishes display name from workflow role and validates required roles and invalid/blank names.
- [ ] Removing a populated status offers an explicit destination/migration flow or a clear route to move its tickets first; no tickets are orphaned.
- [ ] Where a role has multiple columns, default destinations for new tickets and agent role-based moves are visible and deterministic.
- [ ] Concurrent configuration changes cause reconciliation feedback rather than silent overwrites.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with web/Settings.tsx, web/ProjectPage.tsx, src/store.ts updateConfig and role-to-column lookups in src/cli.ts/src/mcp.ts. Extend existing configuration rather than introducing competing status data.

### Human review / verification

Add and rename a status, reorder it, reload, and remove an empty status. Exercise removal with tickets and ambiguous role destinations using Concept/Backlog and In Progress/Failed Review.

before.body:
I would like a way to click a swimlane and turn on/off the tickets in that swimline from being visible. For example backlog can be large and I want to turn off backlog and just view the other swimlanes. Maybe a little human eye icon that is in the swimlane header you can click and quickly turn on/off visibility.

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started. Proposed behavior below remains subject to human scope review.

### Intended outcome

Temporarily hide tickets in a busy status column such as Backlog with one click, then restore them just as easily.

### Scope and approach

The Backlog example refers to workflow/status columns (called swimlanes in the request). Add an eye-style visibility toggle to each column header. Hide that column's ticket content across all parent/label groups, retaining a compact labeled header or equivalent visible restore control. This is a visibility preference, not an archive or ticket-status change.

Proposed default: remember hidden column IDs per project and saved view in personal UI preferences, without rewriting the shared view's search query. Keep visibility independent of existing horizontal group collapse. Provide Show all columns and a clear indication of hidden columns.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] One click hides Backlog's cards across all groups and leaves other columns usable. A visible control restores Backlog with one click.
- [ ] Header controls expose an accessible name and pressed/expanded state, work by keyboard, and clearly distinguish hidden from empty columns.
- [ ] No ticket, claim, stage, archive flag or parent relationship changes when toggling visibility.
- [ ] Search/filter changes compose with visibility without losing the user's query. Hidden columns remain identifiable, and Show all recovers from every column being hidden.
- [ ] Visibility is remembered for that project/view after refresh without leaking to another project/view; custom column rename/reorder preserves it by stable ID, and deleted IDs are safely ignored.
- [ ] Board keyboard navigation skips hidden cards, focus stays recoverable after hiding a focused column, and hidden content cannot receive invisible drag/drop or quick-create interactions.
- [ ] Counts and any bulk-action preview make their scope clear; hidden tickets are not silently selected for operations on visible tickets.
- [ ] Table/list views retain their existing behavior; switching back to the board restores its column visibility preferences.

### Implementation notes and related work

Inspect web/BoardView.tsx column rendering and keyboard navigation, web/ProjectPage.tsx view preferences and web/model.ts filters. Related: #44 quick archive, #23 ticket clutter, #18 status customization. Do not conflate this with existing parent-group collapse or automatically create a new shared saved view.

### Human review / verification

Hide Backlog on a populated parent-grouped board, filter the remaining tickets, restore Backlog and refresh. Switch views/projects and rename a custom column. Check keyboard recovery and the all-hidden state.

after.body:
I would like a way to click a swimlane and turn on/off the tickets in that swimline from being visible. For example backlog can be large and I want to turn off backlog and just view the other swimlanes. Maybe a little human eye icon that is in the swimlane header you can click and quickly turn on/off visibility.

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started. Proposed behavior below remains subject to human scope review.

### Intended outcome

Temporarily hide tickets in a busy status column such as Backlog with one click, then restore them just as easily.

### Scope and approach

The Backlog example refers to workflow/status columns (called swimlanes in the request). Add an eye-style visibility toggle to each column header. Hide that column's ticket content across all parent/label groups, retaining a compact labeled header or equivalent visible restore control. This is a visibility preference, not an archive or ticket-status change.

Proposed default: remember hidden column IDs per project and saved view in personal UI preferences, without rewriting the shared view's search query. Keep visibility independent of existing horizontal group collapse. Provide Show all columns and a clear indication of hidden columns.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] One click hides Backlog's cards across all groups and leaves other columns usable. A visible control restores Backlog with one click.
- [ ] Header controls expose an accessible name and pressed/expanded state, work by keyboard, and clearly distinguish hidden from empty columns.
- [ ] No ticket, claim, stage, archive flag or parent relationship changes when toggling visibility.
- [ ] Search/filter changes compose with visibility without losing the user's query. Hidden columns remain identifiable, and Show all recovers from every column being hidden.
- [ ] Visibility is remembered for that project/view after refresh without leaking to another project/view; custom column rename/reorder preserves it by stable ID, and deleted IDs are safely ignored.
- [ ] Board keyboard navigation skips hidden cards, focus stays recoverable after hiding a focused column, and hidden content cannot receive invisible drag/drop or quick-create interactions.
- [ ] Counts and any bulk-action preview make their scope clear; hidden tickets are not silently selected for operations on visible tickets.
- [ ] Table/list views retain their existing behavior; switching back to the board restores its column visibility preferences.

### Implementation notes and related work

Inspect web/BoardView.tsx column rendering and keyboard navigation, web/ProjectPage.tsx view preferences and web/model.ts filters. Related: #44 quick archive, #23 ticket clutter, #18 status customization. Do not conflate this with existing parent-group collapse or automatically create a new shared saved view.

### Human review / verification

Hide Backlog on a populated parent-grouped board, filter the remaining tickets, restore Backlog and refresh. Switch views/projects and rename a custom column. Check keyboard recovery and the all-hidden state.

before.body:
If the LLM has questions about a ticket, they can add a questionaire with multiple choice questions or text questions to a ticket and mark it as needing human feedback. 

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Let an agent attach a structured questionnaire to a ticket and request human input, keeping questions and answers in the ticket’s conversation.

### Scope and approach

Support one or more multiple-choice or free-text questions, an explicit needs-feedback state, and answering at the human’s pace. Store structured data durably in Markdown records/metadata and expose it through CLI/MCP context. Keep this distinct from mandatory ticket creation forms.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An agent can submit a questionnaire with stable question IDs, clear prompts, answer types, and optional recommended choices; users can provide custom text where choices are offered.
- [ ] The ticket appears in Needs you with a direct route to its unanswered questionnaire; a separate flag does not silently change its workflow stage.
- [ ] Questions never time out or disappear because the user pauses. Draft answers persist across closing/reopening and refresh, and can be submitted explicitly.
- [ ] No recommended/preselected option counts as an answer until the human submits; required unanswered questions remain visible.
- [ ] Submitted answers retain human attribution, question wording, and timestamps in the conversation, and are readable by agent context and wait-for-update workflows.
- [ ] Question edits/replacements and amended answers retain history; stale submissions do not overwrite a newer questionnaire, and resolving one request does not clear unrelated open questions.

### Implementation notes and related work

Extend src/types.ts, src/store.ts comments/context, src/server.ts, src/cli.ts/src/mcp.ts, web/RecordDetail.tsx and web/model.ts attention handling. Reuse the existing question/resolve flow where possible. Related: #26.

### Human review / verification

Submit a mixed questionnaire, leave it unanswered beyond ordinary UI timers, save a partial draft, reload, and finish later. Confirm that an agent receives the explicit answers and that a concurrent question edit triggers reconciliation.

after.body:
If the LLM has questions about a ticket, they can add a questionaire with multiple choice questions or text questions to a ticket and mark it as needing human feedback. 

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Let an agent attach a structured questionnaire to a ticket and request human input, keeping questions and answers in the ticket’s conversation.

### Scope and approach

Support one or more multiple-choice or free-text questions, an explicit needs-feedback state, and answering at the human’s pace. Store structured data durably in Markdown records/metadata and expose it through CLI/MCP context. Keep this distinct from mandatory ticket creation forms.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An agent can submit a questionnaire with stable question IDs, clear prompts, answer types, and optional recommended choices; users can provide custom text where choices are offered.
- [ ] The ticket appears in Needs you with a direct route to its unanswered questionnaire; a separate flag does not silently change its workflow stage.
- [ ] Questions never time out or disappear because the user pauses. Draft answers persist across closing/reopening and refresh, and can be submitted explicitly.
- [ ] No recommended/preselected option counts as an answer until the human submits; required unanswered questions remain visible.
- [ ] Submitted answers retain human attribution, question wording, and timestamps in the conversation, and are readable by agent context and wait-for-update workflows.
- [ ] Question edits/replacements and amended answers retain history; stale submissions do not overwrite a newer questionnaire, and resolving one request does not clear unrelated open questions.

### Implementation notes and related work

Extend src/types.ts, src/store.ts comments/context, src/server.ts, src/cli.ts/src/mcp.ts, web/RecordDetail.tsx and web/model.ts attention handling. Reuse the existing question/resolve flow where possible. Related: #26.

### Human review / verification

Submit a mixed questionnaire, leave it unanswered beyond ordinary UI timers, save a partial draft, reload, and finish later. Confirm that an agent receives the explicit answers and that a concurrent question edit triggers reconciliation.

before.body:
If the LLM has questions about a ticket, they can add a questionaire with multiple choice questions or text questions to a ticket and mark it as needing human feedback. 

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Let an agent attach a structured questionnaire to a ticket and request human input, keeping questions and answers in the ticket’s conversation.

### Scope and approach

Support one or more multiple-choice or free-text questions, an explicit needs-feedback state, and answering at the human’s pace. Store structured data durably in Markdown records/metadata and expose it through CLI/MCP context. Keep this distinct from mandatory ticket creation forms.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An agent can submit a questionnaire with stable question IDs, clear prompts, answer types, and optional recommended choices; users can provide custom text where choices are offered.
- [ ] The ticket appears in Needs you with a direct route to its unanswered questionnaire; a separate flag does not silently change its workflow stage.
- [ ] Questions never time out or disappear because the user pauses. Draft answers persist across closing/reopening and refresh, and can be submitted explicitly.
- [ ] No recommended/preselected option counts as an answer until the human submits; required unanswered questions remain visible.
- [ ] Submitted answers retain human attribution, question wording, and timestamps in the conversation, and are readable by agent context and wait-for-update workflows.
- [ ] Question edits/replacements and amended answers retain history; stale submissions do not overwrite a newer questionnaire, and resolving one request does not clear unrelated open questions.

### Implementation notes and related work

Extend src/types.ts, src/store.ts comments/context, src/server.ts, src/cli.ts/src/mcp.ts, web/RecordDetail.tsx and web/model.ts attention handling. Reuse the existing question/resolve flow where possible. Related: #26.

### Human review / verification

Submit a mixed questionnaire, leave it unanswered beyond ordinary UI timers, save a partial draft, reload, and finish later. Confirm that an agent receives the explicit answers and that a concurrent question edit triggers reconciliation.

before.body:
Already experiencing effects, maybe have a way to quick archive the "Done" swimlane and also a way to go back and view past archived done tickets and unarchive return to active if possible

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started. Proposed behavior below remains subject to human scope review.

### Intended outcome

Clear completed tickets from the active board quickly, while keeping their history easy to browse and restore.

### Scope and approach

Add an Archive completed tickets action to a Done-status column header. Proposed first-release behavior: archive only unarchived tickets in that column that match the current view/search filters, across its visible groups. Before applying, show the exact count and scope, with a way to inspect the affected tickets. Provide an obvious Archived tickets view with search and an Unarchive action.

Unarchiving returns a ticket to the active board in its existing workflow stage (usually Done); moving it back into development remains a separate explicit action. Archiving a parent does not implicitly archive its children. This is a focused implementation follow-up to #23; it need not wait for every clutter-management recommendation.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A Done-role column offers the archive action, including renamed/custom Done columns; non-Done columns do not silently offer the same completed-work operation.
- [ ] The preview names the column, filter scope and affected ticket count. Empty sets are harmless; cancel changes nothing. Tickets outside the preview are never archived.
- [ ] Each write uses the previewed ticket revision. Concurrent changes are rejected for that ticket, with clear success/failure counts and a refresh/review path; no stale record is overwritten.
- [ ] Archived tickets disappear from ordinary active views and remain searchable in an explicitly labeled archive view.
- [ ] A ticket can be opened and unarchived from the archive view. Its status, number, prose, comments, attachments, decisions and parent/child links survive the round trip.
- [ ] Archiving preserves decision/rule discovery and does not delete local screenshots or implicitly archive linked records.
- [ ] The action and archive navigation work with keyboard input, and the chosen scope stays explicit when filters or column visibility change.

### Implementation notes and related work

Reuse the existing archived metadata and is:archived filtering in web/model.ts and the detail Unarchive action. Inspect web/BoardView.tsx, web/ProjectPage.tsx and revision-checked record updates in src/store.ts. Related: parent #23, #17 bulk actions, #46 column visibility. Scheduled/automatic archiving and deletion are outside this ticket.

### Human review / verification

On a fixture with completed parent/child tickets and active work, archive a filtered Done subset, find it through Archived tickets, then restore one ticket. Verify unrelated tickets and linked project knowledge remain intact. Exercise a concurrent edit during the preview to confirm it is reported rather than overwritten.

It should return in its existing stage with its details and conversation intact. Collapsed groups and hidden columns are excluded.

## Outcome
Allow a human-authorized chat orchestrator to take over an interrupted managed worker ticket under its own identity, without impersonating the worker or bypassing record protections.

## Reproduction
On #67 the user explicitly requested direct implementation by the chat. Stopping Sol run run-55ab1dec62f77f03 halted execution but retained the acknowledged service-owned assignment. A claim by Codex chat orchestrator returned HTTP 409: Assigned to Sol. Ordinary record updates and manual review submission remain subject to the same assignment guard. The implementation can be completed safely in the stopped checkout, but the board cannot represent the takeover through its existing API.

## Acceptance criteria
- Provide an explicit authorized release/reassignment operation for the configured orchestrator or a human.
- Verify all owned/original worker processes have exited; refuse takeover of active or uncertain processes.
- Serialize the change with current ticket revision and assignment/run identity checks.
- Preserve prior assignment, run, worktree, logs and attribution in history; release only the obsolete claim.
- Allow the new actor to claim, report progress and submit human review using its own identity.
- Do not grant scope approval, reset attempt limits, self-accept an implementation, or forge human attribution.
- Cover active-process refusal, stale revisions, unauthorized workers, successful stopped-run takeover, and unrelated assignment preservation.

## Implementation references
src/orchestration.ts stop(), src/store.ts claim()/updateNow(), src/server.ts orchestration routes.

## Scope
Backlog finding only; not implemented as part of the #67 scrolling correction.

meta.title: Need a way to clear trash

before.body:
## Visual feedback

[![Screenshot](/api/images/image-a4860976e73b1010/base)](#image=image-a4860976e73b1010)



## Backlog refinement

### Intended outcome

Permanently clear unwanted screenshots from Trash, including clearing the whole Trash in one action, and reclaim their local image/preview storage.

### Evidence and current behavior

The attached screenshot shows four selected items in Trash with Restore selected available and no permanent-delete action. Current trashImage only records trashedAt/trashedBy; it retains the base image, preview, annotations and links indefinitely.

### Proposed scope

Add Delete permanently for selected trashed screenshots and an Empty Trash action. Use an explicit confirmation preview with an exact count and image list. Preserve useful ticket/conversation references and annotation instructions through a small deletion record or equivalent placeholder; do not silently rewrite unrelated Markdown or delete linked tickets.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Trash offers Delete permanently for selected items and Empty Trash for all currently trashed items; the normal screenshot library continues to use reversible Move to Trash behavior.
- [ ] Confirmation names the exact images/count and explains that local image/preview files will be removed. Empty Trash clearly covers the entire Trash, even when a search filter is active; selection deletion covers only its explicit selection.
- [ ] Cancellation makes no changes. Confirmation freezes the candidate list and revisions; newly trashed images are not swept into an already-open confirmation.
- [ ] Only currently trashed images are eligible. An image restored or edited after the preview is rejected individually rather than being deleted with a stale revision.
- [ ] Successful deletion removes base/preview assets and removes the entry from the ordinary Trash list. Empty and repeated-delete states are handled consistently.
- [ ] Linked tickets and conversation prose remain intact. Their screenshot references clearly indicate permanent deletion, with retained written annotation context where available; a missing or purged image never crashes board/detail/context rendering.
- [ ] Partial failures identify confirmed deletions and remaining items without replaying uncertain destructive requests automatically. Controls prevent duplicate submissions.
- [ ] Existing backups are not modified. Export/restore handles deletion records consistently, and a pre-deletion backup can restore the original image and links through the existing restore workflow.
- [ ] Keyboard focus, confirmation defaults, narrow layouts and both density modes work. Tests exercise cancellation, filtered selection, full-Trash scope, concurrent restore/edit, missing files, linked images and partial failures using disposable assets.

### Implementation notes

Inspect src/media.ts, src/server.ts, src/types.ts, web/Screenshots.tsx and screenshot/context/backup consumers. Choose the deletion-record format during implementation and document the rationale; annotation metadata is Git-tracked, while image assets are local. Do not use real project screenshots for destructive tests.

### Human review

On disposable screenshots, compare deleting a selection with Empty Trash while filtered. Cancel once, then confirm. Check a ticket linked to a deleted screenshot, and restore an older backup in a disposable project. This ticket is refined into Backlog and still awaits scope approval; no screenshots have been deleted.

meta.title: Need a way to merge or relate tickets in case of duplicates

before.body:
## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Connect overlapping tickets and consolidate genuine duplicates without losing their discussion, images, decisions, or history.

### Scope and approach

Support a lightweight Related tickets relationship and a separate explicit merge action that chooses a surviving ticket. Show a reviewable merge preview. Retain the source ticket as an archived duplicate pointing to the survivor rather than deleting its record; preserve original attribution and links.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Find related tickets by number/title, add or remove a relationship, and see reciprocal links in both details and agent context without treating related work as a blocking dependency.
- [ ] A merge preview identifies the survivor and source, content to preserve, and conflicts in parent, status, owner, priority, or acceptance criteria; conflicting metadata is not silently overwritten.
- [ ] The survivor retains access to source descriptions, comments, attachments/annotations, and decision/rule references with their original provenance. Existing links to the source still resolve and show the survivor.
- [ ] Source tickets are explicitly marked as duplicates and excluded from ordinary active views after merge; this does not claim the work was completed or accepted into Done.
- [ ] Incoming parent/dependency links are handled deliberately, with cycle/self-link validation, and both records retain an audit trail.
- [ ] Merge uses revision checks on every affected record and reports partial failure/recovery clearly; repeated requests must not duplicate content. Related links remain independently editable.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with src/types.ts, src/store.ts relationship/context/archive behavior, and web/RecordDetail.tsx. Add CLI/MCP support so agents can identify duplicates and retrieve related context. Coordinate with #23; related, duplicate, parent, and dependency are distinct relationships.

### Human review / verification

Relate two tickets, then preview and merge duplicates containing different comments/images and conflicting metadata. Follow old links, retrieve agent context, and simulate stale input. Confirm that no content or attribution disappears and no ticket is falsely accepted as Done.

meta.title: Have a view in which I can sort ticket priority by vertically reordering tickets

before.body:
## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Provide a dedicated vertical planning view where dragging tickets changes the order in which work should be considered.

### Scope and approach

Build on the saved table view and existing manual/priority sorting. Offer an obvious Priority planning preset, rank tickets within priority groups, and allow explicit movement into another priority group. Ordering must not silently change workflow status or parent. Explain that priority is the urgency bucket and rank is the order within it.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The planning view shows a vertical list with priority groups and visible drag handles, including the start/end of each group.
- [ ] Dragging within a group changes persistent relative rank; dragging to another priority group updates priority and rank visibly.
- [ ] Reordering across tickets with different statuses does not move either ticket to the other status or change its parent.
- [ ] Move up/down and move-to-priority controls provide keyboard alternatives, including first/last positions.
- [ ] Reloading or returning to the saved view retains the order; concurrent reorder failures reconcile without losing tickets.
- [ ] Filtered reordering uses defined visible anchors and preserves the relative order of hidden tickets; saved sort modes clearly indicate whether manual reordering is active.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with web/ProjectPage.tsx place/peersOf, web/TableView.tsx and web/model.ts sortTickets. Current place also copies the target status, so reuse needs care. Coordinate drag preview with #22; prefer existing order metadata over a second competing ranking field.

### Human review / verification

Rank tickets across several stages and priorities, move to first/last, refresh, and repeat with a filter and keyboard controls. Confirm that status/parent stay unchanged and priority changes only when crossing an explicit priority group.

after.body:
## Outcome
Allow a human-authorized chat orchestrator to take over an interrupted managed worker ticket under its own identity, without impersonating the worker or bypassing record protections.

## Reproduction
On #67 the user explicitly requested direct implementation by the chat. Stopping Sol run run-55ab1dec62f77f03 halted execution but retained the acknowledged service-owned assignment. A claim by Codex chat orchestrator returned HTTP 409: Assigned to Sol. Ordinary record updates and manual review submission remain subject to the same assignment guard. The implementation can be completed safely in the stopped checkout, but the board cannot represent the takeover through its existing API.

## Acceptance criteria
- Provide an explicit authorized release/reassignment operation for the configured orchestrator or a human.
- Verify all owned/original worker processes have exited; refuse takeover of active or uncertain processes.
- Serialize the change with current ticket revision and assignment/run identity checks.
- Preserve prior assignment, run, worktree, logs and attribution in history; release only the obsolete claim.
- Allow the new actor to claim, report progress and submit human review using its own identity.
- Do not grant scope approval, reset attempt limits, self-accept an implementation, or forge human attribution.
- Cover active-process refusal, stale revisions, unauthorized workers, successful stopped-run takeover, and unrelated assignment preservation.

## Implementation references
src/orchestration.ts stop(), src/store.ts claim()/updateNow(), src/server.ts orchestration routes.

## Scope
Backlog finding only; not implemented as part of the #67 scrolling correction.

## Outcome
Allow a human-authorized chat orchestrator to take over an interrupted managed worker ticket under its own identity, without impersonating the worker or bypassing record protections.

## Reproduction
On #67 the user explicitly requested direct implementation by the chat. Stopping Sol run run-55ab1dec62f77f03 halted execution but retained the acknowledged service-owned assignment. A claim by Codex chat orchestrator returned HTTP 409: Assigned to Sol. Ordinary record updates and manual review submission remain subject to the same assignment guard. The implementation can be completed safely in the stopped checkout, but the board cannot represent the takeover through its existing API.

## Acceptance criteria
- Provide an explicit authorized release/reassignment operation for the configured orchestrator or a human.
- Verify all owned/original worker processes have exited; refuse takeover of active or uncertain processes.
- Serialize the change with current ticket revision and assignment/run identity checks.
- Preserve prior assignment, run, worktree, logs and attribution in history; release only the obsolete claim.
- Allow the new actor to claim, report progress and submit human review using its own identity.
- Do not grant scope approval, reset attempt limits, self-accept an implementation, or forge human attribution.
- Cover active-process refusal, stale revisions, unauthorized workers, successful stopped-run takeover, and unrelated assignment preservation.

## Implementation references
src/orchestration.ts stop(), src/store.ts claim()/updateNow(), src/server.ts orchestration routes.

## Scope
Backlog finding only; not implemented as part of the #67 scrolling correction.

meta.title: Need a way to merge or relate tickets in case of duplicates

before.body:
## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Connect overlapping tickets and consolidate genuine duplicates without losing their discussion, images, decisions, or history.

### Scope and approach

Support a lightweight Related tickets relationship and a separate explicit merge action that chooses a surviving ticket. Show a reviewable merge preview. Retain the source ticket as an archived duplicate pointing to the survivor rather than deleting its record; preserve original attribution and links.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Find related tickets by number/title, add or remove a relationship, and see reciprocal links in both details and agent context without treating related work as a blocking dependency.
- [ ] A merge preview identifies the survivor and source, content to preserve, and conflicts in parent, status, owner, priority, or acceptance criteria; conflicting metadata is not silently overwritten.
- [ ] The survivor retains access to source descriptions, comments, attachments/annotations, and decision/rule references with their original provenance. Existing links to the source still resolve and show the survivor.
- [ ] Source tickets are explicitly marked as duplicates and excluded from ordinary active views after merge; this does not claim the work was completed or accepted into Done.
- [ ] Incoming parent/dependency links are handled deliberately, with cycle/self-link validation, and both records retain an audit trail.
- [ ] Merge uses revision checks on every affected record and reports partial failure/recovery clearly; repeated requests must not duplicate content. Related links remain independently editable.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with src/types.ts, src/store.ts relationship/context/archive behavior, and web/RecordDetail.tsx. Add CLI/MCP support so agents can identify duplicates and retrieve related context. Coordinate with #23; related, duplicate, parent, and dependency are distinct relationships.

### Human review / verification

Relate two tickets, then preview and merge duplicates containing different comments/images and conflicting metadata. Follow old links, retrieve agent context, and simulate stale input. Confirm that no content or attribution disappears and no ticket is falsely accepted as Done.

meta.title: Need a way to clear trash

before.body:
## Visual feedback

[![Screenshot](/api/images/image-a4860976e73b1010/base)](#image=image-a4860976e73b1010)



## Backlog refinement

### Intended outcome

Permanently clear unwanted screenshots from Trash, including clearing the whole Trash in one action, and reclaim their local image/preview storage.

### Evidence and current behavior

The attached screenshot shows four selected items in Trash with Restore selected available and no permanent-delete action. Current trashImage only records trashedAt/trashedBy; it retains the base image, preview, annotations and links indefinitely.

### Proposed scope

Add Delete permanently for selected trashed screenshots and an Empty Trash action. Use an explicit confirmation preview with an exact count and image list. Preserve useful ticket/conversation references and annotation instructions through a small deletion record or equivalent placeholder; do not silently rewrite unrelated Markdown or delete linked tickets.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Trash offers Delete permanently for selected items and Empty Trash for all currently trashed items; the normal screenshot library continues to use reversible Move to Trash behavior.
- [ ] Confirmation names the exact images/count and explains that local image/preview files will be removed. Empty Trash clearly covers the entire Trash, even when a search filter is active; selection deletion covers only its explicit selection.
- [ ] Cancellation makes no changes. Confirmation freezes the candidate list and revisions; newly trashed images are not swept into an already-open confirmation.
- [ ] Only currently trashed images are eligible. An image restored or edited after the preview is rejected individually rather than being deleted with a stale revision.
- [ ] Successful deletion removes base/preview assets and removes the entry from the ordinary Trash list. Empty and repeated-delete states are handled consistently.
- [ ] Linked tickets and conversation prose remain intact. Their screenshot references clearly indicate permanent deletion, with retained written annotation context where available; a missing or purged image never crashes board/detail/context rendering.
- [ ] Partial failures identify confirmed deletions and remaining items without replaying uncertain destructive requests automatically. Controls prevent duplicate submissions.
- [ ] Existing backups are not modified. Export/restore handles deletion records consistently, and a pre-deletion backup can restore the original image and links through the existing restore workflow.
- [ ] Keyboard focus, confirmation defaults, narrow layouts and both density modes work. Tests exercise cancellation, filtered selection, full-Trash scope, concurrent restore/edit, missing files, linked images and partial failures using disposable assets.

### Implementation notes

Inspect src/media.ts, src/server.ts, src/types.ts, web/Screenshots.tsx and screenshot/context/backup consumers. Choose the deletion-record format during implementation and document the rationale; annotation metadata is Git-tracked, while image assets are local. Do not use real project screenshots for destructive tests.

### Human review

On disposable screenshots, compare deleting a selection with Empty Trash while filtered. Cancel once, then confirm. Check a ticket linked to a deleted screenshot, and restore an older backup in a disposable project. This ticket is refined into Backlog and still awaits scope approval; no screenshots have been deleted.

before.body:
## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Connect overlapping tickets and consolidate genuine duplicates without losing their discussion, images, decisions, or history.

### Scope and approach

Support a lightweight Related tickets relationship and a separate explicit merge action that chooses a surviving ticket. Show a reviewable merge preview. Retain the source ticket as an archived duplicate pointing to the survivor rather than deleting its record; preserve original attribution and links.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Find related tickets by number/title, add or remove a relationship, and see reciprocal links in both details and agent context without treating related work as a blocking dependency.
- [ ] A merge preview identifies the survivor and source, content to preserve, and conflicts in parent, status, owner, priority, or acceptance criteria; conflicting metadata is not silently overwritten.
- [ ] The survivor retains access to source descriptions, comments, attachments/annotations, and decision/rule references with their original provenance. Existing links to the source still resolve and show the survivor.
- [ ] Source tickets are explicitly marked as duplicates and excluded from ordinary active views after merge; this does not claim the work was completed or accepted into Done.
- [ ] Incoming parent/dependency links are handled deliberately, with cycle/self-link validation, and both records retain an audit trail.
- [ ] Merge uses revision checks on every affected record and reports partial failure/recovery clearly; repeated requests must not duplicate content. Related links remain independently editable.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with src/types.ts, src/store.ts relationship/context/archive behavior, and web/RecordDetail.tsx. Add CLI/MCP support so agents can identify duplicates and retrieve related context. Coordinate with #23; related, duplicate, parent, and dependency are distinct relationships.

### Human review / verification

Relate two tickets, then preview and merge duplicates containing different comments/images and conflicting metadata. Follow old links, retrieve agent context, and simulate stale input. Confirm that no content or attribution disappears and no ticket is falsely accepted as Done.

I would like a way to click a swimlane and turn on/off the tickets in that swimline from being visible. For example backlog can be large and I want to turn off backlog and just view the other swimlanes. Maybe a little human eye icon that is in the swimlane header you can click and quickly turn on/off visibility.

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started. Proposed behavior below remains subject to human scope review.

### Intended outcome

Temporarily hide tickets in a busy status column such as Backlog with one click, then restore them just as easily.

### Scope and approach

The Backlog example refers to workflow/status columns (called swimlanes in the request). Add an eye-style visibility toggle to each column header. Hide that column's ticket content across all parent/label groups, retaining a compact labeled header or equivalent visible restore control. This is a visibility preference, not an archive or ticket-status change.

Proposed default: remember hidden column IDs per project and saved view in personal UI preferences, without rewriting the shared view's search query. Keep visibility independent of existing horizontal group collapse. Provide Show all columns and a clear indication of hidden columns.

- [ ] Counts and any bulk-action preview make their scope clear; hidden tickets are not silently selected for operations on visible tickets.
- [ ] Table/list views retain their existing behavior; switching back to the board restores its column visibility preferences.
