## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Make workflow status customization easy to discover from the board and safe to use as the project evolves.

### Scope and approach

Settings already supports naming, roles, ordering, addition, and removal of columns. Expose a clear Customize statuses entry from the board and improve that existing editor. Retain stable IDs and explain why workflow roles control agent behavior; multiple columns can share a role, as Concept and Backlog do here.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A user can find status customization from the board, add a status, rename it, and change its order without editing configuration files.
- [ ] Renaming or reordering retains ticket associations, history, and saved views; refreshing preserves the configuration.
- [ ] The editor distinguishes display name from workflow role and validates required roles and invalid/blank names.
- [ ] Removing a populated status offers an explicit destination/migration flow or a clear route to move its tickets first; no tickets are orphaned.
- [ ] Where a role has multiple columns, default destinations for new tickets and agent role-based moves are visible and deterministic.
- [ ] Concurrent configuration changes cause reconciliation feedback rather than silent overwrites.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with web/Settings.tsx, web/ProjectPage.tsx, src/store.ts updateConfig and role-to-column lookups in src/cli.ts/src/mcp.ts. Extend existing configuration rather than introducing competing status data.

### Human review / verification

Add and rename a status, reorder it, reload, and remove an empty status. Exercise removal with tickets and ambiguous role destinations using Concept/Backlog and In Progress/Failed Review.

agentReview.rationale: The status editor improvements are useful, but concurrent configuration updates silently discard local edits before Save, violating the reconciliation requirement.
agentReview.criteria: Retain the editor baseline and unsaved name/column/shortcut drafts when configRevision changes externally. Show explicit reconciliation feedback and provide deliberate reload/reapply choices; never automatically replace dirty drafts with remote config. Add a browser regression that changes a status locally, updates config through another client, verifies the draft remains with conflict feedback, then reconciles and saves without losing the other client changes. Also exercise board entry, rename/reorder persistence and populated-column removal in the UI.
agentReview.evidence: Independent source review of exact commit8fc37e3. The new Settings useEffect on state.configRevision unconditionally calls setName, setColumns, setRevision and setShortcut. The SSE state refresh therefore replaces unsaved edits immediately and adopts the new revision, so the Save catch for Configuration changed is never reached in the ordinary concurrent-update case. The added tests/views.test.ts only exercises Store config revisions and cannot detect this UI data loss. Return a corrected snapshot within existing #18 scope; do not merge/deploy.

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Make workflow status customization easy to discover from the board and safe to use as the project evolves.

### Scope and approach

Settings already supports naming, roles, ordering, addition, and removal of columns. Expose a clear Customize statuses entry from the board and improve that existing editor. Retain stable IDs and explain why workflow roles control agent behavior; multiple columns can share a role, as Concept and Backlog do here.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A user can find status customization from the board, add a status, rename it, and change its order without editing configuration files.
- [ ] Renaming or reordering retains ticket associations, history, and saved views; refreshing preserves the configuration.
- [ ] The editor distinguishes display name from workflow role and validates required roles and invalid/blank names.
- [ ] Removing a populated status offers an explicit destination/migration flow or a clear route to move its tickets first; no tickets are orphaned.
- [ ] Where a role has multiple columns, default destinations for new tickets and agent role-based moves are visible and deterministic.
- [ ] Concurrent configuration changes cause reconciliation feedback rather than silent overwrites.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with web/Settings.tsx, web/ProjectPage.tsx, src/store.ts updateConfig and role-to-column lookups in src/cli.ts/src/mcp.ts. Extend existing configuration rather than introducing competing status data.

### Human review / verification

Add and rename a status, reorder it, reload, and remove an empty status. Exercise removal with tickets and ambiguous role destinations using Concept/Backlog and In Progress/Failed Review.

meta.title: Preserve duplicate ticket provenance and transact records with their audit history

after.body:
## Choice

Keep duplicate sources as archived records pointing to their survivor. Retrieve original descriptions, discussions, images, decisions and rules through provenance links rather than copying them into competing records. Related links remain reciprocal and non-blocking. Merge previews freeze every affected record revision and require explicit conflict choices.

## Rationale

The approved ticket requires consolidation without losing attribution or changing old links. Record changes and their audit entries use one local before/after recovery journal. Partial writes roll back together; completed writes retain their audit entries; independent edits block recovery. Merging cannot accept work into Done or bypass managed ownership and claims.

## Alternatives and tradeoffs

Deleting sources loses provenance; copying all content creates duplicates and ambiguous attribution. Linked sources keep the original records authoritative, so they remain accessible in archive history. A local transaction journal adds recovery complexity and rewrites the audit file during infrequent merge/relationship operations, but preserves the existing Markdown format and avoids a second database. Normal comments and progress retain the existing append path.

## Attribution

Chosen by Codex chat orchestrator within approved #29 while completing the retained Sol implementation after an explicit stopped-run takeover. This records an implementation decision, not an inferred human answer or additional scope approval.

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Give users a Help/Playbook tab with short, copyable prompts for working with their existing coding agent and this project board.

### Scope and approach

Provide concise recipes for connection/setup, refining Concept tickets, planning an approved parent, picking up work, reporting progress, submitting review evidence, responding to feedback, documenting decisions, and maintaining the rulebook. Include screenshot feedback and shortcut help; no embedded provider or agent execution is required.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An in-app Help/Playbook entry offers searchable or clearly grouped recipes, each with its purpose, prerequisites, and a short copyable prompt.
- [ ] Prompts use real project context where available and clearly mark user-supplied placeholders; copied text contains no local auth tokens or hidden secrets.
- [ ] Ticket-specific recipes use public numbers with shell-safe examples and explain scope approval, claims, Review, and human acceptance.

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Give users a Help/Playbook tab with short, copyable prompts for working with their existing coding agent and this project board.

### Scope and approach

Provide concise recipes for connection/setup, refining Concept tickets, planning an approved parent, picking up work, reporting progress, submitting review evidence, responding to feedback, documenting decisions, and maintaining the rulebook. Include screenshot feedback and shortcut help; no embedded provider or agent execution is required.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An in-app Help/Playbook entry offers searchable or clearly grouped recipes, each with its purpose, prerequisites, and a short copyable prompt.
- [ ] Prompts use real project context where available and clearly mark user-supplied placeholders; copied text contains no local auth tokens or hidden secrets.
- [ ] Ticket-specific recipes use public numbers with shell-safe examples and explain scope approval, claims, Review, and human acceptance.
- [ ] Setup guidance matches the shipped CLI/MCP protocol; the source stays easy to update alongside AGENT_GUIDE.md.
- [ ] Copy confirms success accessibly, supports keyboard use, and has a fallback if clipboard access is unavailable.
- [ ] The playbook works offline and lets the user choose where to paste/run a prompt; clicking Copy does not start an agent or mutate tickets.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with AGENT_GUIDE.md, CLI help, web/Shortcuts.tsx, web/TopNav.tsx and web/Pages.tsx. Prefer a small shared content source to duplicated instructions that drift. Related: #27 for collecting human answers.

### Human review / verification

Follow the setup and review recipes against a disposable project using current CLI commands. Copy a ticket-specific prompt and verify correct number/context, no secrets, and no automatic execution.

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Provide a dedicated vertical planning view where dragging tickets changes the order in which work should be considered.

### Scope and approach

Build on the saved table view and existing manual/priority sorting. Offer an obvious Priority planning preset, rank tickets within priority groups, and allow explicit movement into another priority group. Ordering must not silently change workflow status or parent. Explain that priority is the urgency bucket and rank is the order within it.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The planning view shows a vertical list with priority groups and visible drag handles, including the start/end of each group.
- [ ] Dragging within a group changes persistent relative rank; dragging to another priority group updates priority and rank visibly.
- [ ] Reordering across tickets with different statuses does not move either ticket to the other status or change its parent.
- [ ] Move up/down and move-to-priority controls provide keyboard alternatives, including first/last positions.
- [ ] Reloading or returning to the saved view retains the order; concurrent reorder failures reconcile without losing tickets.
- [ ] Filtered reordering uses defined visible anchors and preserves the relative order of hidden tickets; saved sort modes clearly indicate whether manual reordering is active.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with web/ProjectPage.tsx place/peersOf, web/TableView.tsx and web/model.ts sortTickets. Current place also copies the target status, so reuse needs care. Coordinate drag preview with #22; prefer existing order metadata over a second competing ranking field.

### Human review / verification

Rank tickets across several stages and priorities, move to first/last, refresh, and repeat with a filter and keyboard controls. Confirm that status/parent stay unchanged and priority changes only when crossing an explicit priority group.

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Give users a Help/Playbook tab with short, copyable prompts for working with their existing coding agent and this project board.

### Scope and approach

Provide concise recipes for connection/setup, refining Concept tickets, planning an approved parent, picking up work, reporting progress, submitting review evidence, responding to feedback, documenting decisions, and maintaining the rulebook. Include screenshot feedback and shortcut help; no embedded provider or agent execution is required.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An in-app Help/Playbook entry offers searchable or clearly grouped recipes, each with its purpose, prerequisites, and a short copyable prompt.
- [ ] Prompts use real project context where available and clearly mark user-supplied placeholders; copied text contains no local auth tokens or hidden secrets.
- [ ] Ticket-specific recipes use public numbers with shell-safe examples and explain scope approval, claims, Review, and human acceptance.
- [ ] Setup guidance matches the shipped CLI/MCP protocol; the source stays easy to update alongside AGENT_GUIDE.md.
- [ ] Copy confirms success accessibly, supports keyboard use, and has a fallback if clipboard access is unavailable.
- [ ] The playbook works offline and lets the user choose where to paste/run a prompt; clicking Copy does not start an agent or mutate tickets.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with AGENT_GUIDE.md, CLI help, web/Shortcuts.tsx, web/TopNav.tsx and web/Pages.tsx. Prefer a small shared content source to duplicated instructions that drift. Related: #27 for collecting human answers.

### Human review / verification

Follow the setup and review recipes against a disposable project using current CLI commands. Copy a ticket-specific prompt and verify correct number/context, no secrets, and no automatic execution.

Content is centralized in web/playbookContent.ts with an AGENT_GUIDE.md alignment note. Copying never invokes an agent or mutates board state; it announces success accessibly and selects the prompt for manual copying when clipboard access fails. No board records or decisions were changed. A commit was not possible because the managed worktree denies writing its Git worktree index lock; changes remain in the checkout for the controller snapshot.

agentReview.rationale: The offline playbook UI is promising, but the copied workflow prompts need to match both project-local installation and the managed-agent protocol.
agentReview.criteria: Make the connection recipe identify the installed project launcher and guide (.controlroom/controlroom and .controlroom/AGENT_GUIDE.md, with the source-checkout alternative explicitly separate). Avoid assuming a global controlroom executable. In pickup/progress/review/feedback recipes, distinguish manual agents from controller-managed assignments: managed workers return their structured handoff and do not issue manual claim/move/review/release or overwrite another assignment; stopped work requires explicit orchestrator takeover. Do not unconditionally instruct every review to wait for human Done when the configured independent orchestrator can accept it. Retain scope/identity protections. Use valid stable IDs for aria-labelledby group headings. Add browser checks for search, keyboard copy success and clipboard-denial fallback, public ticket substitution, and no mutation/execution on Copy.
agentReview.evidence: Exact commit6a65794 review: connection starts with Read AGENT_GUIDE.md and tool-source ./controlroom, while shipped installer src/cli.ts writes the project guide and launcher under .controlroom. Subsequent recipes use a global controlroom command. Pickup directs claim/move and submission directs manual review unconditionally, contrary to the managed-worker exception in the shipped guide; feedback similarly directs a manual lifecycle submission. This can reproduce already-observed assignment conflicts when users paste the recipes into managed agent workflows. Playbook.tsx also uses literal group strings with spaces in IDs and aria-labelledby, which are parsed as multiple ID references. Controller core/build passed; static recipe checks do not cover clipboard or accessibility behavior.

agentReview.criteria: Make the connection recipe identify the installed project launcher and guide (.controlroom/controlroom and .controlroom/AGENT_GUIDE.md, with the source-checkout alternative explicitly separate). before.body:
## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Give users a Help/Playbook tab with short, copyable prompts for working with their existing coding agent and this project board.

### Scope and approach

Provide concise recipes for connection/setup, refining Concept tickets, planning an approved parent, picking up work, reporting progress, submitting review evidence, responding to feedback, documenting decisions, and maintaining the rulebook. Include screenshot feedback and shortcut help; no embedded provider or agent execution is required.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An in-app Help/Playbook entry offers searchable or clearly grouped recipes, each with its purpose, prerequisites, and a short copyable prompt.
- [ ] Prompts use real project context where available and clearly mark user-supplied placeholders; copied text contains no local auth tokens or hidden secrets.
- [ ] Ticket-specific recipes use public numbers with shell-safe examples and explain scope approval, claims, Review, and human acceptance.
- [ ] Setup guidance matches the shipped CLI/MCP protocol; the source stays easy to update alongside AGENT_GUIDE.md.
- [ ] Copy confirms success accessibly, supports keyboard use, and has a fallback if clipboard access is unavailable.
- [ ] The playbook works offline and lets the user choose where to paste/run a prompt; clicking Copy does not start an agent or mutate tickets.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with AGENT_GUIDE.md, CLI help, web/Shortcuts.tsx, web/TopNav.tsx and web/Pages.tsx. Prefer a small shared content source to duplicated instructions that drift. Related: #27 for collecting human answers.

### Human review / verification

Follow the setup and review recipes against a disposable project using current CLI commands. Copy a ticket-specific prompt and verify correct number/context, no secrets, and no automatic execution.

Content is centralized in web/playbookContent.ts with an AGENT_GUIDE.md alignment note. Copying never invokes an agent or mutates board state; it announces success accessibly and selects the prompt for manual copying when clipboard access fails. No board records or decisions were changed. A commit was not possible because the managed worktree denies writing its Git worktree index lock; changes remain in the checkout for the controller snapshot.

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Give users a Help/Playbook tab with short, copyable prompts for working with their existing coding agent and this project board.

### Scope and approach

Provide concise recipes for connection/setup, refining Concept tickets, planning an approved parent, picking up work, reporting progress, submitting review evidence, responding to feedback, documenting decisions, and maintaining the rulebook. Include screenshot feedback and shortcut help; no embedded provider or agent execution is required.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An in-app Help/Playbook entry offers searchable or clearly grouped recipes, each with its purpose, prerequisites, and a short copyable prompt.
- [ ] Prompts use real project context where available and clearly mark user-supplied placeholders; copied text contains no local auth tokens or hidden secrets.
- [ ] Ticket-specific recipes use public numbers with shell-safe examples and explain scope approval, claims, Review, and human acceptance.
- [ ] Setup guidance matches the shipped CLI/MCP protocol; the source stays easy to update alongside AGENT_GUIDE.md.
- [ ] Copy confirms success accessibly, supports keyboard use, and has a fallback if clipboard access is unavailable.
- [ ] The playbook works offline and lets the user choose where to paste/run a prompt; clicking Copy does not start an agent or mutate tickets.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with AGENT_GUIDE.md, CLI help, web/Shortcuts.tsx, web/TopNav.tsx and web/Pages.tsx. Prefer a small shared content source to duplicated instructions that drift. Related: #27 for collecting human answers.

### Human review / verification

Follow the setup and review recipes against a disposable project using current CLI commands. Copy a ticket-specific prompt and verify correct number/context, no secrets, and no automatic execution.

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Provide a dedicated vertical planning view where dragging tickets changes the order in which work should be considered.

### Scope and approach

Build on the saved table view and existing manual/priority sorting. Offer an obvious Priority planning preset, rank tickets within priority groups, and allow explicit movement into another priority group. Ordering must not silently change workflow status or parent. Explain that priority is the urgency bucket and rank is the order within it.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The planning view shows a vertical list with priority groups and visible drag handles, including the start/end of each group.
- [ ] Dragging within a group changes persistent relative rank; dragging to another priority group updates priority and rank visibly.
- [ ] Reordering across tickets with different statuses does not move either ticket to the other status or change its parent.
- [ ] Move up/down and move-to-priority controls provide keyboard alternatives, including first/last positions.
- [ ] Reloading or returning to the saved view retains the order; concurrent reorder failures reconcile without losing tickets.
- [ ] Filtered reordering uses defined visible anchors and preserves the relative order of hidden tickets; saved sort modes clearly indicate whether manual reordering is active.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with web/ProjectPage.tsx place/peersOf, web/TableView.tsx and web/model.ts sortTickets. Current place also copies the target status, so reuse needs care. Coordinate drag preview with #22; prefer existing order metadata over a second competing ranking field.

### Human review / verification

Rank tickets across several stages and priorities, move to first/last, refresh, and repeat with a filter and keyboard controls. Confirm that status/parent stay unchanged and priority changes only when crossing an explicit priority group.

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Provide a dedicated vertical planning view where dragging tickets changes the order in which work should be considered.

### Scope and approach

Build on the saved table view and existing manual/priority sorting. Offer an obvious Priority planning preset, rank tickets within priority groups, and allow explicit movement into another priority group. Ordering must not silently change workflow status or parent. Explain that priority is the urgency bucket and rank is the order within it.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The planning view shows a vertical list with priority groups and visible drag handles, including the start/end of each group.
- [ ] Dragging within a group changes persistent relative rank; dragging to another priority group updates priority and rank visibly.
- [ ] Reordering across tickets with different statuses does not move either ticket to the other status or change its parent.
- [ ] Move up/down and move-to-priority controls provide keyboard alternatives, including first/last positions.
- [ ] Reloading or returning to the saved view retains the order; concurrent reorder failures reconcile without losing tickets.
- [ ] Filtered reordering uses defined visible anchors and preserves the relative order of hidden tickets; saved sort modes clearly indicate whether manual reordering is active.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with web/ProjectPage.tsx place/peersOf, web/TableView.tsx and web/model.ts sortTickets. Current place also copies the target status, so reuse needs care. Coordinate drag preview with #22; prefer existing order metadata over a second competing ranking field.

### Human review / verification

Rank tickets across several stages and priorities, move to first/last, refresh, and repeat with a filter and keyboard controls. Confirm that status/parent stay unchanged and priority changes only when crossing an explicit priority group.

agentReview.rationale: The focused queue and retained review feedback are useful, but navigating between items currently loses unsaved ticket edits and can race an in-flight review outcome.
agentReview.criteria: Route Previous/Next buttons and keyboard shortcuts through a shared guarded navigation path: preserve or safely save dirty title/body/metadata before changing tickets, retain the current ticket and feedback on a failed/conflicted save, and disable/ignore navigation while save or review submission is pending. Use a keyboard combination that does not hijack native Option+Arrow word navigation inside text fields (or ignore editable targets and keep buttons keyboard-accessible). Add regressions for dirty ticket navigation, a delayed review-outcome response, failed/stale save, and text-editing keyboard behavior; retain the feedback/history/evidence coverage.
agentReview.evidence: Independent exact submission review of commit 2c45067, snapshot 7ca602f601193935a9583f2c66f939a45a9722b196f73dcbd4cfa85a123fcecb. App.tsx previous/next directly call setSelected, remounting keyed RecordDetail and discarding mRef/bodyRef edits without its save path. RecordDetail's Alt+Arrow listener calls those callbacks without checking saving or pending.current, although buttons check saving. Thus a user can change tickets during decide(), whose eventual onReviewDone callback changes selection again. The listener also intercepts Option+Arrow in the review-feedback textarea, overriding macOS word navigation. These are correctness and keyboard-workflow regressions, not new scope. Do not merge/deploy this submission.

agentReview.rationale: The focused queue and retained review feedback are useful, but navigating between items currently loses unsaved ticket edits and can race an in-flight review outcome.
agentReview.criteria: Route Previous/Next buttons and keyboard shortcuts through a shared guarded navigation path: preserve or safely save dirty title/body/metadata before changing tickets, retain the current ticket and feedback on a failed/conflicted save, and disable/ignore navigation while save or review submission is pending. Use a keyboard combination that does not hijack native Option+Arrow word navigation inside text fields (or ignore editable targets and keep buttons keyboard-accessible). Add regressions for dirty ticket navigation, a delayed review-outcome response, failed/stale save, and text-editing keyboard behavior; retain the feedback/history/evidence coverage.
agentReview.evidence: Independent exact submission review of commit 2c45067, snapshot 7ca602f601193935a9583f2c66f939a45a9722b196f73dcbd4cfa85a123fcecb. App.tsx previous/next directly call setSelected, remounting keyed RecordDetail and discarding mRef/bodyRef edits without its save path. RecordDetail's Alt+Arrow listener calls those callbacks without checking saving or pending.current, although buttons check saving. Thus a user can change tickets during decide(), whose eventual onReviewDone callback changes selection again. The listener also intercepts Option+Arrow in the review-feedback textarea, overriding macOS word navigation. These are correctness and keyboard-workflow regressions, not new scope. Do not merge/deploy this submission.

meta.title: Need a way to clear trash

before.body:
## Visual feedback

[![Screenshot](/api/images/image-a4860976e73b1010/base)](#image=image-a4860976e73b1010)



## Backlog refinement

### Intended outcome

Permanently clear unwanted screenshots from Trash, including clearing the whole Trash in one action, and reclaim their local image/preview storage.

### Evidence and current behavior

The attached screenshot shows four selected items in Trash with Restore selected available and no permanent-delete action. Current trashImage only records trashedAt/trashedBy; it retains the base image, preview, annotations and links indefinitely.

### Proposed scope

Add Delete permanently for selected trashed screenshots and an Empty Trash action. Use an explicit confirmation preview with an exact count and image list. Preserve useful ticket/conversation references and annotation instructions through a small deletion record or equivalent placeholder; do not silently rewrite unrelated Markdown or delete linked tickets.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Trash offers Delete permanently for selected items and Empty Trash for all currently trashed items; the normal screenshot library continues to use reversible Move to Trash behavior.
- [ ] Confirmation names the exact images/count and explains that local image/preview files will be removed. Empty Trash clearly covers the entire Trash, even when a search filter is active; selection deletion covers only its explicit selection.
- [ ] Cancellation makes no changes. Confirmation freezes the candidate list and revisions; newly trashed images are not swept into an already-open confirmation.
- [ ] Only currently trashed images are eligible. An image restored or edited after the preview is rejected individually rather than being deleted with a stale revision.
- [ ] Successful deletion removes base/preview assets and removes the entry from the ordinary Trash list. Empty and repeated-delete states are handled consistently.
- [ ] Linked tickets and conversation prose remain intact. Their screenshot references clearly indicate permanent deletion, with retained written annotation context where available; a missing or purged image never crashes board/detail/context rendering.
- [ ] Partial failures identify confirmed deletions and remaining items without replaying uncertain destructive requests automatically. Controls prevent duplicate submissions.
- [ ] Existing backups are not modified. Export/restore handles deletion records consistently, and a pre-deletion backup can restore the original image and links through the existing restore workflow.
- [ ] Keyboard focus, confirmation defaults, narrow layouts and both density modes work. Tests exercise cancellation, filtered selection, full-Trash scope, concurrent restore/edit, missing files, linked images and partial failures using disposable assets.

### Implementation notes

Inspect src/media.ts, src/server.ts, src/types.ts, web/Screenshots.tsx and screenshot/context/backup consumers. Choose the deletion-record format during implementation and document the rationale; annotation metadata is Git-tracked, while image assets are local. Do not use real project screenshots for destructive tests.

### Human review

On disposable screenshots, compare deleting a selection with Empty Trash while filtered. Cancel once, then confirm. Check a ticket linked to a deleted screenshot, and restore an older backup in a disposable project. This ticket is refined into Backlog and still awaits scope approval; no screenshots have been deleted.

Help a human review several agent submissions quickly with the handoff, current verification, changes and open questions visible together. Build on existing review controls rather than duplicating them.

## Acceptance criteria

Next/previous navigation preserves unsaved feedback; current versus historical evidence is explicit; accept/request-changes respects revisions and preserves discussion; unavailable PR/diff information is represented honestly; support keyboard and narrow screens.

## Scope

Recommendation from the local Kanban comparison. Awaiting human scope approval; no implementation started.

meta.title: Quick Archive Swimlane
meta.handoff: Implemented the archive-history correction: archived tickets now render as a horizontally scrollable board with the configured workflow columns in board order. Each column has its board-style header/count and archived cards with parent context and Unarchive. Empty columns remain visible during search so lane identity stays explicit. Existing archive preview, revision-checked writes, restore behavior, and navigation were not changed. Changed: web/ArchiveTickets.tsx, web/project.css, tests/browser/archive-grouping.spec.ts. Commit was attempted but the controlled worktree denied Git index-lock creation; changes remain unstaged. Decisions: none.
meta.evidence: `git diff --check` passes. `npm ci && npm run build` passes (TypeScript and production build). `npm run test:browser -- --list` discovers `archive history uses board-style workflow columns with parent context`; the updated spec asserts same-row/different-x lane geometry and search-empty lane behavior. Full required `npm test` is sandbox-blocked before test discovery because tsx cannot create its IPC socket (`listen EPERM` under /var/folders/.../tsx-501/*.pipe). Attempted commit `Lay out archived tickets as board columns` failed only because Git could not create the worktree index lock (`Operation not permitted`).
meta.reviewInstructions: In a Done column, open ⋯ → Archive completed tickets. Check the filter, count and linked ticket list; Cancel should change nothing. Try a small filtered set and confirm the results, then open Archived tickets, search by title or number, and Unarchive one. It should return in its existing stage with its details and conversation intact. Collapsed groups and hidden columns are excluded.
meta.exceptions: Visibility is a personal preference in this browser, not shared across browsers. No known failures in the exercised workflows. Human workflow review requested. Changes remain uncommitted.

before.body:
Already experiencing effects, maybe have a way to quick archive the "Done" swimlane and also a way to go back and view past archived done tickets and unarchive return to active if possible

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started. Proposed behavior below remains subject to human scope review.

### Intended outcome

Clear completed tickets from the active board quickly, while keeping their history easy to browse and restore.

### Scope and approach

Add an Archive completed tickets action to a Done-status column header. Proposed first-release behavior: archive only unarchived tickets in that column that match the current view/search filters, across its visible groups. Before applying, show the exact count and scope, with a way to inspect the affected tickets. Provide an obvious Archived tickets view with search and an Unarchive action.

Unarchiving returns a ticket to the active board in its existing workflow stage (usually Done); moving it back into development remains a separate explicit action. Archiving a parent does not implicitly archive its children. This is a focused implementation follow-up to #23; it need not wait for every clutter-management recommendation.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A Done-role column offers the archive action, including renamed/custom Done columns; non-Done columns do not silently offer the same completed-work operation.
- [ ] The preview names the column, filter scope and affected ticket count. Empty sets are harmless; cancel changes nothing. Tickets outside the preview are never archived.
- [ ] Each write uses the previewed ticket revision. Concurrent changes are rejected for that ticket, with clear success/failure counts and a refresh/review path; no stale record is overwritten.
- [ ] Archived tickets disappear from ordinary active views and remain searchable in an explicitly labeled archive view.
- [ ] A ticket can be opened and unarchived from the archive view. Its status, number, prose, comments, attachments, decisions and parent/child links survive the round trip.
- [ ] Archiving preserves decision/rule discovery and does not delete local screenshots or implicitly archive linked records.
- [ ] The action and archive navigation work with keyboard input, and the chosen scope stays explicit when filters or column visibility change.

### Implementation notes and related work

Reuse the existing archived metadata and is:archived filtering in web/model.ts and the detail Unarchive action. Inspect web/BoardView.tsx, web/ProjectPage.tsx and revision-checked record updates in src/store.ts. Related: parent #23, #17 bulk actions, #46 column visibility. Scheduled/automatic archiving and deletion are outside this ticket.

### Human review / verification

On a fixture with completed parent/child tickets and active work, archive a filtered Done subset, find it through Archived tickets, then restore one ticket. Verify unrelated tickets and linked project knowledge remain intact. Exercise a concurrent edit during the preview to confirm it is reported rather than overwritten.

meta.title: Quick Archive Swimlane
meta.handoff: Implemented the archive-history correction: archived tickets now render as a horizontally scrollable board with the configured workflow columns in board order. Each column has its board-style header/count and archived cards with parent context and Unarchive. Empty columns remain visible during search so lane identity stays explicit. Existing archive preview, revision-checked writes, restore behavior, and navigation were not changed. Changed: web/ArchiveTickets.tsx, web/project.css, tests/browser/archive-grouping.spec.ts. Commit was attempted but the controlled worktree denied Git index-lock creation; changes remain unstaged. Decisions: none.
meta.evidence: `git diff --check` passes. `npm ci && npm run build` passes (TypeScript and production build). `npm run test:browser -- --list` discovers `archive history uses board-style workflow columns with parent context`; the updated spec asserts same-row/different-x lane geometry and search-empty lane behavior. Full required `npm test` is sandbox-blocked before test discovery because tsx cannot create its IPC socket (`listen EPERM` under /var/folders/.../tsx-501/*.pipe). Attempted commit `Lay out archived tickets as board columns` failed only because Git could not create the worktree index lock (`Operation not permitted`).
meta.reviewInstructions: In a Done column, open ⋯ → Archive completed tickets. Check the filter, count and linked ticket list; Cancel should change nothing. Try a small filtered set and confirm the results, then open Archived tickets, search by title or number, and Unarchive one. It should return in its existing stage with its details and conversation intact. Collapsed groups and hidden columns are excluded.
meta.exceptions: Visibility is a personal preference in this browser, not shared across browsers. No known failures in the exercised workflows. Human workflow review requested. Changes remain uncommitted.

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started. Proposed behavior below remains subject to human scope review.

### Intended outcome

Clear completed tickets from the active board quickly, while keeping their history easy to browse and restore.

### Scope and approach

Add an Archive completed tickets action to a Done-status column header. Proposed first-release behavior: archive only unarchived tickets in that column that match the current view/search filters, across its visible groups. Before applying, show the exact count and scope, with a way to inspect the affected tickets. Provide an obvious Archived tickets view with search and an Unarchive action.

Unarchiving returns a ticket to the active board in its existing workflow stage (usually Done); moving it back into development remains a separate explicit action. Archiving a parent does not implicitly archive its children. This is a focused implementation follow-up to #23; it need not wait for every clutter-management recommendation.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A Done-role column offers the archive action, including renamed/custom Done columns; non-Done columns do not silently offer the same completed-work operation.
- [ ] The preview names the column, filter scope and affected ticket count. Empty sets are harmless; cancel changes nothing. Tickets outside the preview are never archived.
- [ ] Each write uses the previewed ticket revision. Concurrent changes are rejected for that ticket, with clear success/failure counts and a refresh/review path; no stale record is overwritten.
- [ ] Archived tickets disappear from ordinary active views and remain searchable in an explicitly labeled archive view.
- [ ] A ticket can be opened and unarchived from the archive view. Its status, number, prose, comments, attachments, decisions and parent/child links survive the round trip.
- [ ] Archiving preserves decision/rule discovery and does not delete local screenshots or implicitly archive linked records.
- [ ] The action and archive navigation work with keyboard input, and the chosen scope stays explicit when filters or column visibility change.

### Implementation notes and related work

Reuse the existing archived metadata and is:archived filtering in web/model.ts and the detail Unarchive action. Inspect web/BoardView.tsx, web/ProjectPage.tsx and revision-checked record updates in src/store.ts. Related: parent #23, #17 bulk actions, #46 column visibility. Scheduled/automatic archiving and deletion are outside this ticket.

### Human review / verification

On a fixture with completed parent/child tickets and active work, archive a filtered Done subset, find it through Archived tickets, then restore one ticket. Verify unrelated tickets and linked project knowledge remain intact. Exercise a concurrent edit during the preview to confirm it is reported rather than overwritten.

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Provide a dedicated vertical planning view where dragging tickets changes the order in which work should be considered.

### Scope and approach

Build on the saved table view and existing manual/priority sorting. Offer an obvious Priority planning preset, rank tickets within priority groups, and allow explicit movement into another priority group. Ordering must not silently change workflow status or parent. Explain that priority is the urgency bucket and rank is the order within it.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The planning view shows a vertical list with priority groups and visible drag handles, including the start/end of each group.
- [ ] Dragging within a group changes persistent relative rank; dragging to another priority group updates priority and rank visibly.
- [ ] Reordering across tickets with different statuses does not move either ticket to the other status or change its parent.
- [ ] Move up/down and move-to-priority controls provide keyboard alternatives, including first/last positions.
- [ ] Reloading or returning to the saved view retains the order; concurrent reorder failures reconcile without losing tickets.
- [ ] Filtered reordering uses defined visible anchors and preserves the relative order of hidden tickets; saved sort modes clearly indicate whether manual reordering is active.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with web/ProjectPage.tsx place/peersOf, web/TableView.tsx and web/model.ts sortTickets. Current place also copies the target status, so reuse needs care. Coordinate drag preview with #22; prefer existing order metadata over a second competing ranking field.

### Human review / verification

Rank tickets across several stages and priorities, move to first/last, refresh, and repeat with a filter and keyboard controls. Confirm that status/parent stay unchanged and priority changes only when crossing an explicit priority group.

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Provide a dedicated vertical planning view where dragging tickets changes the order in which work should be considered.

### Scope and approach

Build on the saved table view and existing manual/priority sorting. Offer an obvious Priority planning preset, rank tickets within priority groups, and allow explicit movement into another priority group. Ordering must not silently change workflow status or parent. Explain that priority is the urgency bucket and rank is the order within it.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The planning view shows a vertical list with priority groups and visible drag handles, including the start/end of each group.
- [ ] Dragging within a group changes persistent relative rank; dragging to another priority group updates priority and rank visibly.
- [ ] Reordering across tickets with different statuses does not move either ticket to the other status or change its parent.
- [ ] Move up/down and move-to-priority controls provide keyboard alternatives, including first/last positions.
- [ ] Reloading or returning to the saved view retains the order; concurrent reorder failures reconcile without losing tickets.
- [ ] Filtered reordering uses defined visible anchors and preserves the relative order of hidden tickets; saved sort modes clearly indicate whether manual reordering is active.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with web/ProjectPage.tsx place/peersOf, web/TableView.tsx and web/model.ts sortTickets. Current place also copies the target status, so reuse needs care. Coordinate drag preview with #22; prefer existing order metadata over a second competing ranking field.

### Human review / verification

Rank tickets across several stages and priorities, move to first/last, refresh, and repeat with a filter and keyboard controls. Confirm that status/parent stay unchanged and priority changes only when crossing an explicit priority group.

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Provide a dedicated vertical planning view where dragging tickets changes the order in which work should be considered.

### Scope and approach

Build on the saved table view and existing manual/priority sorting. Offer an obvious Priority planning preset, rank tickets within priority groups, and allow explicit movement into another priority group. Ordering must not silently change workflow status or parent. Explain that priority is the urgency bucket and rank is the order within it.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The planning view shows a vertical list with priority groups and visible drag handles, including the start/end of each group.
- [ ] Dragging within a group changes persistent relative rank; dragging to another priority group updates priority and rank visibly.
- [ ] Reordering across tickets with different statuses does not move either ticket to the other status or change its parent.
- [ ] Move up/down and move-to-priority controls provide keyboard alternatives, including first/last positions.
- [ ] Reloading or returning to the saved view retains the order; concurrent reorder failures reconcile without losing tickets.
- [ ] Filtered reordering uses defined visible anchors and preserves the relative order of hidden tickets; saved sort modes clearly indicate whether manual reordering is active.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with web/ProjectPage.tsx place/peersOf, web/TableView.tsx and web/model.ts sortTickets. Current place also copies the target status, so reuse needs care. Coordinate drag preview with #22; prefer existing order metadata over a second competing ranking field.

### Human review / verification

Rank tickets across several stages and priorities, move to first/last, refresh, and repeat with a filter and keyboard controls. Confirm that status/parent stay unchanged and priority changes only when crossing an explicit priority group.

meta.title: Retain screenshot deletion records and written annotations after clearing Trash

after.body:
## Choice

Remove local image derivatives only after an explicit frozen Trash confirmation. Retain the existing attachment JSON and Markdown annotation instructions with permanent-deletion timestamp and actor. Old ticket and conversation links display a deletion placeholder; no unrelated prose or ticket record is rewritten.

## Rationale

Approved #53 requires reclaiming ignored image storage while preserving project knowledge and existing references. The same durable record ID keeps pre-deletion backups restorable and post-deletion backups honest about missing pixels. Each candidate is checked against its confirmation revision and current Trash state.

## Alternatives and tradeoffs

Deleting metadata would break old links and lose instructions. Rewriting every reference would touch unrelated Markdown and attribution. Retaining small records preserves this context at negligible storage cost. Filesystem removal can partially fail; report each result separately and distinguish removed pixels from failure to save the final deletion record. Never automatically replay uncertain requests. A later explicit confirmation can finish a record for already missing pixels. Existing backups remain untouched.

## Attribution

Codex chat orchestrator chose this format within approved #53, completing Sol's retained implementation after an explicit stopped-run takeover. This is not a human acceptance or new scope approval.

## Visual feedback

[![Screenshot](/api/images/image-a4860976e73b1010/base)](#image=image-a4860976e73b1010)



## Backlog refinement

### Intended outcome

Permanently clear unwanted screenshots from Trash, including clearing the whole Trash in one action, and reclaim their local image/preview storage.

### Evidence and current behavior

The attached screenshot shows four selected items in Trash with Restore selected available and no permanent-delete action. Current trashImage only records trashedAt/trashedBy; it retains the base image, preview, annotations and links indefinitely.

### Proposed scope

Add Delete permanently for selected trashed screenshots and an Empty Trash action. Use an explicit confirmation preview with an exact count and image list. Preserve useful ticket/conversation references and annotation instructions through a small deletion record or equivalent placeholder; do not silently rewrite unrelated Markdown or delete linked tickets.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Trash offers Delete permanently for selected items and Empty Trash for all currently trashed items; the normal screenshot library continues to use reversible Move to Trash behavior.
- [ ] Confirmation names the exact images/count and explains that local image/preview files will be removed. Empty Trash clearly covers the entire Trash, even when a search filter is active; selection deletion covers only its explicit selection.
- [ ] Cancellation makes no changes. Confirmation freezes the candidate list and revisions; newly trashed images are not swept into an already-open confirmation.
- [ ] Only currently trashed images are eligible. An image restored or edited after the preview is rejected individually rather than being deleted with a stale revision.
- [ ] Successful deletion removes base/preview assets and removes the entry from the ordinary Trash list. Empty and repeated-delete states are handled consistently.
- [ ] Linked tickets and conversation prose remain intact. Their screenshot references clearly indicate permanent deletion, with retained written annotation context where available; a missing or purged image never crashes board/detail/context rendering.
- [ ] Partial failures identify confirmed deletions and remaining items without replaying uncertain destructive requests automatically. Controls prevent duplicate submissions.
- [ ] Existing backups are not modified. Export/restore handles deletion records consistently, and a pre-deletion backup can restore the original image and links through the existing restore workflow.
- [ ] Keyboard focus, confirmation defaults, narrow layouts and both density modes work. Tests exercise cancellation, filtered selection, full-Trash scope, concurrent restore/edit, missing files, linked images and partial failures using disposable assets.

### Implementation notes

Inspect src/media.ts, src/server.ts, src/types.ts, web/Screenshots.tsx and screenshot/context/backup consumers. Choose the deletion-record format during implementation and document the rationale; annotation metadata is Git-tracked, while image assets are local. Do not use real project screenshots for destructive tests.

### Human review

On disposable screenshots, compare deleting a selection with Empty Trash while filtered. Cancel once, then confirm. Check a ticket linked to a deleted screenshot, and restore an older backup in a disposable project. This ticket is refined into Backlog and still awaits scope approval; no screenshots have been deleted.

before.body:
Already experiencing effects, maybe have a way to quick archive the "Done" swimlane and also a way to go back and view past archived done tickets and unarchive return to active if possible

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started. Proposed behavior below remains subject to human scope review.

### Intended outcome

Clear completed tickets from the active board quickly, while keeping their history easy to browse and restore.

### Scope and approach

Add an Archive completed tickets action to a Done-status column header. Proposed first-release behavior: archive only unarchived tickets in that column that match the current view/search filters, across its visible groups. Before applying, show the exact count and scope, with a way to inspect the affected tickets. Provide an obvious Archived tickets view with search and an Unarchive action.

Unarchiving returns a ticket to the active board in its existing workflow stage (usually Done); moving it back into development remains a separate explicit action. Archiving a parent does not implicitly archive its children. This is a focused implementation follow-up to #23; it need not wait for every clutter-management recommendation.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A Done-role column offers the archive action, including renamed/custom Done columns; non-Done columns do not silently offer the same completed-work operation.
- [ ] The preview names the column, filter scope and affected ticket count. Empty sets are harmless; cancel changes nothing. Tickets outside the preview are never archived.
- [ ] Each write uses the previewed ticket revision. Concurrent changes are rejected for that ticket, with clear success/failure counts and a refresh/review path; no stale record is overwritten.
- [ ] Archived tickets disappear from ordinary active views and remain searchable in an explicitly labeled archive view.
- [ ] A ticket can be opened and unarchived from the archive view. Its status, number, prose, comments, attachments, decisions and parent/child links survive the round trip.
- [ ] Archiving preserves decision/rule discovery and does not delete local screenshots or implicitly archive linked records.
- [ ] The action and archive navigation work with keyboard input, and the chosen scope stays explicit when filters or column visibility change.

### Implementation notes and related work

Reuse the existing archived metadata and is:archived filtering in web/model.ts and the detail Unarchive action. Inspect web/BoardView.tsx, web/ProjectPage.tsx and revision-checked record updates in src/store.ts. Related: parent #23, #17 bulk actions, #46 column visibility. Scheduled/automatic archiving and deletion are outside this ticket.

### Human review / verification

On a fixture with completed parent/child tickets and active work, archive a filtered Done subset, find it through Archived tickets, then restore one ticket. Verify unrelated tickets and linked project knowledge remain intact. Exercise a concurrent edit during the preview to confirm it is reported rather than overwritten.

It should return in its existing stage with its details and conversation intact. Collapsed groups and hidden columns are excluded.

Already experiencing effects, maybe have a way to quick archive the "Done" swimlane and also a way to go back and view past archived done tickets and unarchive return to active if possible

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started. Proposed behavior below remains subject to human scope review.

### Intended outcome

Clear completed tickets from the active board quickly, while keeping their history easy to browse and restore.

### Scope and approach

Add an Archive completed tickets action to a Done-status column header. Proposed first-release behavior: archive only unarchived tickets in that column that match the current view/search filters, across its visible groups. Before applying, show the exact count and scope, with a way to inspect the affected tickets. Provide an obvious Archived tickets view with search and an Unarchive action.

Unarchiving returns a ticket to the active board in its existing workflow stage (usually Done); moving it back into development remains a separate explicit action. Archiving a parent does not implicitly archive its children. This is a focused implementation follow-up to #23; it need not wait for every clutter-management recommendation.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A Done-role column offers the archive action, including renamed/custom Done columns; non-Done columns do not silently offer the same completed-work operation.
- [ ] The preview names the column, filter scope and affected ticket count. Empty sets are harmless; cancel changes nothing. Tickets outside the preview are never archived.
- [ ] Each write uses the previewed ticket revision. Concurrent changes are rejected for that ticket, with clear success/failure counts and a refresh/review path; no stale record is overwritten.
- [ ] Archived tickets disappear from ordinary active views and remain searchable in an explicitly labeled archive view.
- [ ] A ticket can be opened and unarchived from the archive view. Its status, number, prose, comments, attachments, decisions and parent/child links survive the round trip.
- [ ] Archiving preserves decision/rule discovery and does not delete local screenshots or implicitly archive linked records.
- [ ] The action and archive navigation work with keyboard input, and the chosen scope stays explicit when filters or column visibility change.

### Implementation notes and related work

Reuse the existing archived metadata and is:archived filtering in web/model.ts and the detail Unarchive action. Inspect web/BoardView.tsx, web/ProjectPage.tsx and revision-checked record updates in src/store.ts. Related: parent #23, #17 bulk actions, #46 column visibility. Scheduled/automatic archiving and deletion are outside this ticket.

### Human review / verification

On a fixture with completed parent/child tickets and active work, archive a filtered Done subset, find it through Archived tickets, then restore one ticket. Verify unrelated tickets and linked project knowledge remain intact. Exercise a concurrent edit during the preview to confirm it is reported rather than overwritten.

agentReview.rationale: The status editor improvements are useful, but concurrent configuration updates silently discard local edits before Save, violating the reconciliation requirement.
agentReview.criteria: Retain the editor baseline and unsaved name/column/shortcut drafts when configRevision changes externally. Show explicit reconciliation feedback and provide deliberate reload/reapply choices; never automatically replace dirty drafts with remote config. Add a browser regression that changes a status locally, updates config through another client, verifies the draft remains with conflict feedback, then reconciles and saves without losing the other client changes. Also exercise board entry, rename/reorder persistence and populated-column removal in the UI.
agentReview.evidence: Independent source review of exact commit8fc37e3. The new Settings useEffect on state.configRevision unconditionally calls setName, setColumns, setRevision and setShortcut. The SSE state refresh therefore replaces unsaved edits immediately and adopts the new revision, so the Save catch for Configuration changed is never reached in the ordinary concurrent-update case. The added tests/views.test.ts only exercises Store config revisions and cannot detect this UI data loss. Return a corrected snapshot within existing #18 scope; do not merge/deploy.

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Make workflow status customization easy to discover from the board and safe to use as the project evolves.

### Scope and approach

Settings already supports naming, roles, ordering, addition, and removal of columns. Expose a clear Customize statuses entry from the board and improve that existing editor. Retain stable IDs and explain why workflow roles control agent behavior; multiple columns can share a role, as Concept and Backlog do here.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A user can find status customization from the board, add a status, rename it, and change its order without editing configuration files.
- [ ] Renaming or reordering retains ticket associations, history, and saved views; refreshing preserves the configuration.
- [ ] The editor distinguishes display name from workflow role and validates required roles and invalid/blank names.
- [ ] Removing a populated status offers an explicit destination/migration flow or a clear route to move its tickets first; no tickets are orphaned.
- [ ] Where a role has multiple columns, default destinations for new tickets and agent role-based moves are visible and deterministic.
- [ ] Concurrent configuration changes cause reconciliation feedback rather than silent overwrites.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with web/Settings.tsx, web/ProjectPage.tsx, src/store.ts updateConfig and role-to-column lookups in src/cli.ts/src/mcp.ts. Extend existing configuration rather than introducing competing status data.

### Human review / verification

Add and rename a status, reorder it, reload, and remove an empty status. Exercise removal with tickets and ambiguous role destinations using Concept/Backlog and In Progress/Failed Review.

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Make workflow status customization easy to discover from the board and safe to use as the project evolves.

### Scope and approach

Settings already supports naming, roles, ordering, addition, and removal of columns. Expose a clear Customize statuses entry from the board and improve that existing editor. Retain stable IDs and explain why workflow roles control agent behavior; multiple columns can share a role, as Concept and Backlog do here.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A user can find status customization from the board, add a status, rename it, and change its order without editing configuration files.
- [ ] Renaming or reordering retains ticket associations, history, and saved views; refreshing preserves the configuration.
- [ ] The editor distinguishes display name from workflow role and validates required roles and invalid/blank names.
- [ ] Removing a populated status offers an explicit destination/migration flow or a clear route to move its tickets first; no tickets are orphaned.
- [ ] Where a role has multiple columns, default destinations for new tickets and agent role-based moves are visible and deterministic.
- [ ] Concurrent configuration changes cause reconciliation feedback rather than silent overwrites.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with web/Settings.tsx, web/ProjectPage.tsx, src/store.ts updateConfig and role-to-column lookups in src/cli.ts/src/mcp.ts. Extend existing configuration rather than introducing competing status data.

### Human review / verification

Add and rename a status, reorder it, reload, and remove an empty status. Exercise removal with tickets and ambiguous role destinations using Concept/Backlog and In Progress/Failed Review.

agentReview.rationale: The focused queue and retained review feedback are useful, but navigating between items currently loses unsaved ticket edits and can race an in-flight review outcome.
agentReview.criteria: Route Previous/Next buttons and keyboard shortcuts through a shared guarded navigation path: preserve or safely save dirty title/body/metadata before changing tickets, retain the current ticket and feedback on a failed/conflicted save, and disable/ignore navigation while save or review submission is pending. Use a keyboard combination that does not hijack native Option+Arrow word navigation inside text fields (or ignore editable targets and keep buttons keyboard-accessible). Add regressions for dirty ticket navigation, a delayed review-outcome response, failed/stale save, and text-editing keyboard behavior; retain the feedback/history/evidence coverage.
agentReview.evidence: Independent exact submission review of commit 2c45067, snapshot 7ca602f601193935a9583f2c66f939a45a9722b196f73dcbd4cfa85a123fcecb. App.tsx previous/next directly call setSelected, remounting keyed RecordDetail and discarding mRef/bodyRef edits without its save path. RecordDetail's Alt+Arrow listener calls those callbacks without checking saving or pending.current, although buttons check saving. Thus a user can change tickets during decide(), whose eventual onReviewDone callback changes selection again. The listener also intercepts Option+Arrow in the review-feedback textarea, overriding macOS word navigation. These are correctness and keyboard-workflow regressions, not new scope. Do not merge/deploy this submission.

## Intended outcome

Help a human review several agent submissions quickly with the handoff, current verification, changes and open questions visible together. Build on existing review controls rather than duplicating them.

## Acceptance criteria

Next/previous navigation preserves unsaved feedback; current versus historical evidence is explicit; accept/request-changes respects revisions and preserves discussion; unavailable PR/diff information is represented honestly; support keyboard and narrow screens.

## Scope

Recommendation from the local Kanban comparison. Awaiting human scope approval; no implementation started.

meta.title: Create a focused keyboard-friendly review queue
meta.handoff: Implemented the review follow-up in the working tree. Queue Previous/Next now save dirty ticket drafts through the existing conflict-aware save path before changing tickets, retain the current ticket on save failure/conflict, and ignore navigation during save or review-outcome requests. Option/Alt+Arrow remains native in text controls; focused queue buttons still support keyboard navigation. Added browser regressions for draft-save navigation, failed saves, delayed review outcomes, and editable-field shortcuts. Decisions: none. Commit attempt was blocked by sandbox denial of the worktree Git index lock; the three modified files remain uncommitted for controller snapshotting.

Browser test execution is likewise unavailable in this sandbox due local-service binding restrictions. App.tsx sorts reviewRecords by meta.updatedAt on every render; navigateReview now calls save(false,false), which changes updatedAt and reloads before invoking a closure over the old queue. A first review saved then Next can become last in the new queue, so Previous no longer returns to it and later items can be skipped. This is independent of the fixed input shortcut guard. after.body:
## Intended outcome

Help a human review several agent submissions quickly with the handoff, current verification, changes and open questions visible together. Build on existing review controls rather than duplicating them.

## Acceptance criteria

Next/previous navigation preserves unsaved feedback; current versus historical evidence is explicit; accept/request-changes respects revisions and preserves discussion; unavailable PR/diff information is represented honestly; support keyboard and narrow screens.

## Scope

Recommendation from the local Kanban comparison. Awaiting human scope approval; no implementation started.

meta.handoff: Corrected #44 archive-board regression validation. Archive lane headers are semantic headings; each lane is aria-labelledby by its matching header/count. The browser spec now asserts header count, lane geometry, narrow-viewport horizontal scrolling, reachable Unarchive, search-empty lanes, parent context, and restoration.

meta.reviewInstructions: In a Done column, open ⋯ → Archive completed tickets. Check the filter, count and linked ticket list; Cancel should change nothing. Try a small filtered set and confirm the results, then open Archived tickets, search by title or number, and Unarchive one. It should return in its existing stage with its details and conversation intact. Collapsed groups and hidden columns are excluded.
meta.exceptions: Visibility is a personal preference in this browser, not shared across browsers. No known failures in the exercised workflows. Human workflow review requested. Changes remain uncommitted.

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started. Proposed behavior below remains subject to human scope review.

### Intended outcome

Clear completed tickets from the active board quickly, while keeping their history easy to browse and restore.

### Scope and approach

Add an Archive completed tickets action to a Done-status column header. Proposed first-release behavior: archive only unarchived tickets in that column that match the current view/search filters, across its visible groups. Before applying, show the exact count and scope, with a way to inspect the affected tickets. Provide an obvious Archived tickets view with search and an Unarchive action.

Unarchiving returns a ticket to the active board in its existing workflow stage (usually Done); moving it back into development remains a separate explicit action. Archiving a parent does not implicitly archive its children. This is a focused implementation follow-up to #23; it need not wait for every clutter-management recommendation.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A Done-role column offers the archive action, including renamed/custom Done columns; non-Done columns do not silently offer the same completed-work operation.
- [ ] The preview names the column, filter scope and affected ticket count. Empty sets are harmless; cancel changes nothing. Tickets outside the preview are never archived.
- [ ] Each write uses the previewed ticket revision. Concurrent changes are rejected for that ticket, with clear success/failure counts and a refresh/review path; no stale record is overwritten.
- [ ] Archived tickets disappear from ordinary active views and remain searchable in an explicitly labeled archive view.
- [ ] A ticket can be opened and unarchived from the archive view. Its status, number, prose, comments, attachments, decisions and parent/child links survive the round trip.
- [ ] Archiving preserves decision/rule discovery and does not delete local screenshots or implicitly archive linked records.
- [ ] The action and archive navigation work with keyboard input, and the chosen scope stays explicit when filters or column visibility change.

### Implementation notes and related work

Reuse the existing archived metadata and is:archived filtering in web/model.ts and the detail Unarchive action. Inspect web/BoardView.tsx, web/ProjectPage.tsx and revision-checked record updates in src/store.ts. Related: parent #23, #17 bulk actions, #46 column visibility. Scheduled/automatic archiving and deletion are outside this ticket.

### Human review / verification

On a fixture with completed parent/child tickets and active work, archive a filtered Done subset, find it through Archived tickets, then restore one ticket. Verify unrelated tickets and linked project knowledge remain intact. Exercise a concurrent edit during the preview to confirm it is reported rather than overwritten.

before.body:
Already experiencing effects, maybe have a way to quick archive the "Done" swimlane and also a way to go back and view past archived done tickets and unarchive return to active if possible

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started. Proposed behavior below remains subject to human scope review.

### Intended outcome

Clear completed tickets from the active board quickly, while keeping their history easy to browse and restore.

### Scope and approach

Add an Archive completed tickets action to a Done-status column header. Proposed first-release behavior: archive only unarchived tickets in that column that match the current view/search filters, across its visible groups. Before applying, show the exact count and scope, with a way to inspect the affected tickets. Provide an obvious Archived tickets view with search and an Unarchive action.

Unarchiving returns a ticket to the active board in its existing workflow stage (usually Done); moving it back into development remains a separate explicit action. Archiving a parent does not implicitly archive its children. This is a focused implementation follow-up to #23; it need not wait for every clutter-management recommendation.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A Done-role column offers the archive action, including renamed/custom Done columns; non-Done columns do not silently offer the same completed-work operation.
- [ ] The preview names the column, filter scope and affected ticket count. Empty sets are harmless; cancel changes nothing. Tickets outside the preview are never archived.
- [ ] Each write uses the previewed ticket revision. Concurrent changes are rejected for that ticket, with clear success/failure counts and a refresh/review path; no stale record is overwritten.
- [ ] Archived tickets disappear from ordinary active views and remain searchable in an explicitly labeled archive view.
- [ ] A ticket can be opened and unarchived from the archive view. Its status, number, prose, comments, attachments, decisions and parent/child links survive the round trip.
- [ ] Archiving preserves decision/rule discovery and does not delete local screenshots or implicitly archive linked records.
- [ ] The action and archive navigation work with keyboard input, and the chosen scope stays explicit when filters or column visibility change.

### Implementation notes and related work

Reuse the existing archived metadata and is:archived filtering in web/model.ts and the detail Unarchive action. Inspect web/BoardView.tsx, web/ProjectPage.tsx and revision-checked record updates in src/store.ts. Related: parent #23, #17 bulk actions, #46 column visibility. Scheduled/automatic archiving and deletion are outside this ticket.

### Human review / verification

On a fixture with completed parent/child tickets and active work, archive a filtered Done subset, find it through Archived tickets, then restore one ticket. Verify unrelated tickets and linked project knowledge remain intact. Exercise a concurrent edit during the preview to confirm it is reported rather than overwritten.

It should return in its existing stage with its details and conversation intact. Collapsed groups and hidden columns are excluded.

Archiving a parent does not implicitly archive its children. This is a focused implementation follow-up to #23; it need not wait for every clutter-management recommendation.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A Done-role column offers the archive action, including renamed/custom Done columns; non-Done columns do not silently offer the same completed-work operation.
- [ ] The preview names the column, filter scope and affected ticket count. Empty sets are harmless; cancel changes nothing. Tickets outside the preview are never archived.
- [ ] Each write uses the previewed ticket revision. Concurrent changes are rejected for that ticket, with clear success/failure counts and a refresh/review path; no stale record is overwritten.
- [ ] Archived tickets disappear from ordinary active views and remain searchable in an explicitly labeled archive view.
- [ ] A ticket can be opened and unarchived from the archive view. Its status, number, prose, comments, attachments, decisions and parent/child links survive the round trip.
- [ ] Archiving preserves decision/rule discovery and does not delete local screenshots or implicitly archive linked records.
- [ ] The action and archive navigation work with keyboard input, and the chosen scope stays explicit when filters or column visibility change.

### Implementation notes and related work

Reuse the existing archived metadata and is:archived filtering in web/model.ts and the detail Unarchive action. Inspect web/BoardView.tsx, web/ProjectPage.tsx and revision-checked record updates in src/store.ts. Related: parent #23, #17 bulk actions, #46 column visibility. Scheduled/automatic archiving and deletion are outside this ticket.

### Human review / verification

On a fixture with completed parent/child tickets and active work, archive a filtered Done subset, find it through Archived tickets, then restore one ticket. Verify unrelated tickets and linked project knowledge remain intact. Exercise a concurrent edit during the preview to confirm it is reported rather than overwritten.
