before.body:
## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Make workflow status customization easy to discover from the board and safe to use as the project evolves.

### Scope and approach

Settings already supports naming, roles, ordering, addition, and removal of columns. Expose a clear Customize statuses entry from the board and improve that existing editor. Retain stable IDs and explain why workflow roles control agent behavior; multiple columns can share a role, as Concept and Backlog do here.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A user can find status customization from the board, add a status, rename it, and change its order without editing configuration files.
- [ ] Renaming or reordering retains ticket associations, history, and saved views; refreshing preserves the configuration.
- [ ] The editor distinguishes display name from workflow role and validates required roles and invalid/blank names.
- [ ] Removing a populated status offers an explicit destination/migration flow or a clear route to move its tickets first; no tickets are orphaned.
- [ ] Where a role has multiple columns, default destinations for new tickets and agent role-based moves are visible and deterministic.
- [ ] Concurrent configuration changes cause reconciliation feedback rather than silent overwrites.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with web/Settings.tsx, web/ProjectPage.tsx, src/store.ts updateConfig and role-to-column lookups in src/cli.ts/src/mcp.ts. Extend existing configuration rather than introducing competing status data.

### Human review / verification

Add and rename a status, reorder it, reload, and remove an empty status. Exercise removal with tickets and ambiguous role destinations using Concept/Backlog and In Progress/Failed Review.

Added a browser regression covering board entry, concurrent update, reapply/save, add/rename/reorder/reload, and populated-status removal guidance. ## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Make workflow status customization easy to discover from the board and safe to use as the project evolves.

### Scope and approach

Settings already supports naming, roles, ordering, addition, and removal of columns. Expose a clear Customize statuses entry from the board and improve that existing editor. Retain stable IDs and explain why workflow roles control agent behavior; multiple columns can share a role, as Concept and Backlog do here.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A user can find status customization from the board, add a status, rename it, and change its order without editing configuration files.
- [ ] Renaming or reordering retains ticket associations, history, and saved views; refreshing preserves the configuration.
- [ ] The editor distinguishes display name from workflow role and validates required roles and invalid/blank names.
- [ ] Removing a populated status offers an explicit destination/migration flow or a clear route to move its tickets first; no tickets are orphaned.
- [ ] Where a role has multiple columns, default destinations for new tickets and agent role-based moves are visible and deterministic.
- [ ] Concurrent configuration changes cause reconciliation feedback rather than silent overwrites.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with web/Settings.tsx, web/ProjectPage.tsx, src/store.ts updateConfig and role-to-column lookups in src/cli.ts/src/mcp.ts. Extend existing configuration rather than introducing competing status data.

### Human review / verification

Add and rename a status, reorder it, reload, and remove an empty status. Exercise removal with tickets and ambiguous role destinations using Concept/Backlog and In Progress/Failed Review.

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Give users a Help/Playbook tab with short, copyable prompts for working with their existing coding agent and this project board.

### Scope and approach

Provide concise recipes for connection/setup, refining Concept tickets, planning an approved parent, picking up work, reporting progress, submitting review evidence, responding to feedback, documenting decisions, and maintaining the rulebook. Include screenshot feedback and shortcut help; no embedded provider or agent execution is required.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An in-app Help/Playbook entry offers searchable or clearly grouped recipes, each with its purpose, prerequisites, and a short copyable prompt.
- [ ] Prompts use real project context where available and clearly mark user-supplied placeholders; copied text contains no local auth tokens or hidden secrets.
- [ ] Ticket-specific recipes use public numbers with shell-safe examples and explain scope approval, claims, Review, and human acceptance.
- [ ] Setup guidance matches the shipped CLI/MCP protocol; the source stays easy to update alongside AGENT_GUIDE.md.
- [ ] Copy confirms success accessibly, supports keyboard use, and has a fallback if clipboard access is unavailable.
- [ ] The playbook works offline and lets the user choose where to paste/run a prompt; clicking Copy does not start an agent or mutate tickets.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with AGENT_GUIDE.md, CLI help, web/Shortcuts.tsx, web/TopNav.tsx and web/Pages.tsx. Prefer a small shared content source to duplicated instructions that drift. Related: #27 for collecting human answers.

### Human review / verification

Follow the setup and review recipes against a disposable project using current CLI commands. Copy a ticket-specific prompt and verify correct number/context, no secrets, and no automatic execution.

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Give users a Help/Playbook tab with short, copyable prompts for working with their existing coding agent and this project board.

### Scope and approach

Provide concise recipes for connection/setup, refining Concept tickets, planning an approved parent, picking up work, reporting progress, submitting review evidence, responding to feedback, documenting decisions, and maintaining the rulebook. Include screenshot feedback and shortcut help; no embedded provider or agent execution is required.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An in-app Help/Playbook entry offers searchable or clearly grouped recipes, each with its purpose, prerequisites, and a short copyable prompt.
- [ ] Prompts use real project context where available and clearly mark user-supplied placeholders; copied text contains no local auth tokens or hidden secrets.
- [ ] Ticket-specific recipes use public numbers with shell-safe examples and explain scope approval, claims, Review, and human acceptance.
- [ ] Setup guidance matches the shipped CLI/MCP protocol; the source stays easy to update alongside AGENT_GUIDE.md.
- [ ] Copy confirms success accessibly, supports keyboard use, and has a fallback if clipboard access is unavailable.
- [ ] The playbook works offline and lets the user choose where to paste/run a prompt; clicking Copy does not start an agent or mutate tickets.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with AGENT_GUIDE.md, CLI help, web/Shortcuts.tsx, web/TopNav.tsx and web/Pages.tsx. Prefer a small shared content source to duplicated instructions that drift. Related: #27 for collecting human answers.

### Human review / verification

Follow the setup and review recipes against a disposable project using current CLI commands. Copy a ticket-specific prompt and verify correct number/context, no secrets, and no automatic execution.

meta.handoff: Implemented the Help & playbook tab. It provides 12 grouped, searchable, offline recipes with purpose, prerequisites, and copyable prompts. Ticket recipes accept a numeric public ticket number, interpolate project/branch context, use shell-safe numeric CLI examples, and distinguish claims, Review, and human acceptance. Content is centralized in web/playbookContent.ts with an AGENT_GUIDE.md alignment note. Copying never invokes an agent or mutates board state; it announces success accessibly and selects the prompt for manual copying when clipboard access fails. No board records or decisions were changed. A commit was not possible because the managed worktree denies writing its Git worktree index lock; changes remain in the checkout for the controller snapshot.

agentReview.rationale: The offline playbook UI is promising, but the copied workflow prompts need to match both project-local installation and the managed-agent protocol.
agentReview.criteria: Make the connection recipe identify the installed project launcher and guide (.controlroom/controlroom and .controlroom/AGENT_GUIDE.md, with the source-checkout alternative explicitly separate). Avoid assuming a global controlroom executable. In pickup/progress/review/feedback recipes, distinguish manual agents from controller-managed assignments: managed workers return their structured handoff and do not issue manual claim/move/review/release or overwrite another assignment; stopped work requires explicit orchestrator takeover. Do not unconditionally instruct every review to wait for human Done when the configured independent orchestrator can accept it. Retain scope/identity protections. Use valid stable IDs for aria-labelledby group headings. Add browser checks for search, keyboard copy success and clipboard-denial fallback, public ticket substitution, and no mutation/execution on Copy.
agentReview.evidence: Exact commit6a65794 review: connection starts with Read AGENT_GUIDE.md and tool-source ./controlroom, while shipped installer src/cli.ts writes the project guide and launcher under .controlroom. Subsequent recipes use a global controlroom command. Pickup directs claim/move and submission directs manual review unconditionally, contrary to the managed-worker exception in the shipped guide; feedback similarly directs a manual lifecycle submission. This can reproduce already-observed assignment conflicts when users paste the recipes into managed agent workflows. Playbook.tsx also uses literal group strings with spaces in IDs and aria-labelledby, which are parsed as multiple ID references. Controller core/build passed; static recipe checks do not cover clipboard or accessibility behavior.

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Provide a dedicated vertical planning view where dragging tickets changes the order in which work should be considered.

### Scope and approach

Build on the saved table view and existing manual/priority sorting. Offer an obvious Priority planning preset, rank tickets within priority groups, and allow explicit movement into another priority group. Ordering must not silently change workflow status or parent. Explain that priority is the urgency bucket and rank is the order within it.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The planning view shows a vertical list with priority groups and visible drag handles, including the start/end of each group.
- [ ] Dragging within a group changes persistent relative rank; dragging to another priority group updates priority and rank visibly.
- [ ] Reordering across tickets with different statuses does not move either ticket to the other status or change its parent.
- [ ] Move up/down and move-to-priority controls provide keyboard alternatives, including first/last positions.
- [ ] Reloading or returning to the saved view retains the order; concurrent reorder failures reconcile without losing tickets.
- [ ] Filtered reordering uses defined visible anchors and preserves the relative order of hidden tickets; saved sort modes clearly indicate whether manual reordering is active.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with web/ProjectPage.tsx place/peersOf, web/TableView.tsx and web/model.ts sortTickets. Current place also copies the target status, so reuse needs care. Coordinate drag preview with #22; prefer existing order metadata over a second competing ranking field.

### Human review / verification

Rank tickets across several stages and priorities, move to first/last, refresh, and repeat with a filter and keyboard controls. Confirm that status/parent stay unchanged and priority changes only when crossing an explicit priority group.

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Make workflow status customization easy to discover from the board and safe to use as the project evolves.

### Scope and approach

Settings already supports naming, roles, ordering, addition, and removal of columns. Expose a clear Customize statuses entry from the board and improve that existing editor. Retain stable IDs and explain why workflow roles control agent behavior; multiple columns can share a role, as Concept and Backlog do here.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A user can find status customization from the board, add a status, rename it, and change its order without editing configuration files.
- [ ] Renaming or reordering retains ticket associations, history, and saved views; refreshing preserves the configuration.
- [ ] The editor distinguishes display name from workflow role and validates required roles and invalid/blank names.
- [ ] Removing a populated status offers an explicit destination/migration flow or a clear route to move its tickets first; no tickets are orphaned.
- [ ] Where a role has multiple columns, default destinations for new tickets and agent role-based moves are visible and deterministic.
- [ ] Concurrent configuration changes cause reconciliation feedback rather than silent overwrites.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with web/Settings.tsx, web/ProjectPage.tsx, src/store.ts updateConfig and role-to-column lookups in src/cli.ts/src/mcp.ts. Extend existing configuration rather than introducing competing status data.

### Human review / verification

Add and rename a status, reorder it, reload, and remove an empty status. Exercise removal with tickets and ambiguous role destinations using Concept/Backlog and In Progress/Failed Review.

meta.handoff: Corrected #18 reconciliation: unsaved status drafts now remain intact on external config changes, with explicit Reload remote configuration and Reapply my draft actions. Reapply performs a three-way merge so unrelated remote status changes survive. Added a browser regression covering board entry, concurrent update, reapply/save, add/rename/reorder/reload, and populated-status removal guidance. Changes are uncommitted because Git index locking is sandbox-denied.

Required `npm test` could not start because sandbox denies tsx IPC socket creation (`listen EPERM`); browser regression could not run because sandbox denies local TCP binding. Commit attempt failed on sandbox-denied Git `index.lock`. Modified: web/Settings.tsx, web/styles.css; added tests/browser/status-customization.spec.ts. No decisions created or changed.

before.body:
## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Offer a newest-first project activity feed so a human can quickly see what changed across tickets and project knowledge.

### Scope and approach

Add a Feed view combining meaningful ticket transitions/edits, comments, review submissions, and decision/rule changes. Reuse durable history and comments with stable event identities; keep Needs you focused on actionable items rather than replacing it.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Entries show actor, time, event type, ticket number/title or knowledge title, and a concise change summary; clicking opens the relevant record/conversation.
- [ ] New activity appears at the top while the user is at the top; when reading older items, offer a new-updates indicator without yanking scroll position.
- [ ] Refresh/reconnect does not duplicate entries; ordering is deterministic for equal timestamps and older history can be loaded incrementally.
- [ ] Filter by actor, event type, and related ticket; group noisy edits without hiding review requests or human questions.
- [ ] Durable comments and record history remain the source of truth; the feed is reconstructible and retains attribution.
- [ ] Archived-ticket events stay traceable, malformed/missing references degrade gracefully, and unrelated routine heartbeats do not flood the feed.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with src/store.ts historyFor/state/index, src/server.ts state updates, web/useProjectState.ts, web/Pages.tsx and web/TopNav.tsx. Account for current JSONL history and supported legacy events. Related: #23 and #28.

### Human review / verification

Create comments, submit review, change a rule, and update a ticket; verify newest-first attribution and deep links after reload. Test scrolling while new events arrive and loading older events without duplication.

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Provide a dedicated vertical planning view where dragging tickets changes the order in which work should be considered.

### Scope and approach

Build on the saved table view and existing manual/priority sorting. Offer an obvious Priority planning preset, rank tickets within priority groups, and allow explicit movement into another priority group. Ordering must not silently change workflow status or parent. Explain that priority is the urgency bucket and rank is the order within it.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The planning view shows a vertical list with priority groups and visible drag handles, including the start/end of each group.
- [ ] Dragging within a group changes persistent relative rank; dragging to another priority group updates priority and rank visibly.
- [ ] Reordering across tickets with different statuses does not move either ticket to the other status or change its parent.
- [ ] Move up/down and move-to-priority controls provide keyboard alternatives, including first/last positions.
- [ ] Reloading or returning to the saved view retains the order; concurrent reorder failures reconcile without losing tickets.
- [ ] Filtered reordering uses defined visible anchors and preserves the relative order of hidden tickets; saved sort modes clearly indicate whether manual reordering is active.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with web/ProjectPage.tsx place/peersOf, web/TableView.tsx and web/model.ts sortTickets. Current place also copies the target status, so reuse needs care. Coordinate drag preview with #22; prefer existing order metadata over a second competing ranking field.

### Human review / verification

Rank tickets across several stages and priorities, move to first/last, refresh, and repeat with a filter and keyboard controls. Confirm that status/parent stay unchanged and priority changes only when crossing an explicit priority group.

before.body:
## Intended outcome

Help a human review several agent submissions quickly with the handoff, current verification, changes and open questions visible together. Build on existing review controls rather than duplicating them.

## Acceptance criteria

Next/previous navigation preserves unsaved feedback; current versus historical evidence is explicit; accept/request-changes respects revisions and preserves discussion; unavailable PR/diff information is represented honestly; support keyboard and narrow screens.

## Scope

Recommendation from the local Kanban comparison. Awaiting human scope approval; no implementation started.

meta.title: Create a focused keyboard-friendly review queue
meta.handoff: Implemented the review follow-up in the working tree. Queue Previous/Next now save dirty ticket drafts through the existing conflict-aware save path before changing tickets, retain the current ticket on save failure/conflict, and ignore navigation during save or review-outcome requests. Option/Alt+Arrow remains native in text controls; focused queue buttons still support keyboard navigation. Added browser regressions for draft-save navigation, failed saves, delayed review outcomes, and editable-field shortcuts. Decisions: none. Commit attempt was blocked by sandbox denial of the worktree Git index lock; the three modified files remain uncommitted for controller snapshotting.
meta.evidence: Passed: `git diff --check`; Prettier check; `npm run build`; `node --import tsx --test tests/review-outcome.test.ts tests/review-evidence.test.ts` (4/4). Prescribed command completed `npm ci` and build, but `npm test` could not start because sandbox policy denies tsx IPC pipe creation (`listen EPERM`) before tests load. Browser test execution is likewise unavailable in this sandbox due local-service binding restrictions. Modified: `web/RecordDetail.tsx`, `web/Shortcuts.tsx`, `tests/browser/review-queue.spec.ts` (78 insertions, 6 deletions relative to HEAD).

Independent disposable Store probe (/private/tmp/cr59-review-probe.mjs) creates a ticket as Actual agent with supplied exceptionHistory naming Someone else/human and an arbitrary January timestamp; the supplied history is accepted. updateNow protects this field but createNow does not. The same probe references existing ticket #0 and its canonical WB-ID: #0 is classified path/missing with emptytarget, while the WB-ID is available. Existing project decisions use public #numbers, so this creates false broken-reference warnings. No real board records were modified by the probe. Strengthen the rulebook as project memory: connect rules to existing token/component references, explain why a rule applies and surface unresolved deviations in review. Avoid a second competing token source.

## Acceptance criteria

Context explains matching scope and references; changed guidance flags only linked open work; exceptions retain rationale and attribution; archived originating tickets do not hide rules; broken implementation references are visible.

## Scope

Recommendation from the local Kanban comparison. Awaiting human scope approval; no implementation started.

meta.title: Make design rule applicability and exceptions actionable
meta.handoff: Implemented ticket #59. Rule context now explains applicability and canonical references; rulebook/detail views surface missing references; changed-rule attention targets only linked/reviewed open work; and exception history preserves rationale, actor, and timestamp across review cycles. Archived originating tickets remain valid references. No decisions or board records were changed. Changes remain uncommitted because the sandbox denied creation of the Git worktree index lock; the controller can snapshot them.
meta.evidence: `npm ci` passed. `npm run build` passed. Focused typecheck and core/view suite passed 31/31. `git diff --check` passed. The prescribed `npm test` was blocked by sandbox-denied tsx IPC (`listen EPERM`). Running all tests through the IPC-free Node loader passed 110/117; all seven remaining failures required prohibited localhost/socket service startup. Diff: 10 files, 505 insertions, 73 deletions.

agentReview.rationale: Rule applicability is implemented, but exception attribution can be fabricated during ticket creation and public ticket references are incorrectly reported as broken paths.
agentReview.criteria: Treat exceptionHistory as service-owned on create as well as update. Reject caller-supplied history and record any initial nonempty exceptions using the actual creating actor and service timestamp; retain the existing immutable amendment history. Recognize supported public ticket references such as #0 alongside canonical record IDs, without rewriting stored prose. Add focused regressions for create attribution, #0/archived public references and missing references, and browser coverage of the new rule-reference/exception UI.
agentReview.evidence: Reviewed exact f757b7a, snapshot c921583cfddc55b733cf1989bea5efc113126e58050435c472e6bd5d9e1daf3b. Controller build and117core passed. Independent disposable Store probe (/private/tmp/cr59-review-probe.mjs) creates a ticket as Actual agent with supplied exceptionHistory naming Someone else/human and an arbitrary January timestamp; the supplied history is accepted. updateNow protects this field but createNow does not. The same probe references existing ticket #0 and its canonical WB-ID: #0 is classified path/missing with emptytarget, while the WB-ID is available. Existing project decisions use public #numbers, so this creates false broken-reference warnings. No real board records were modified by the probe. Preserve prior rule-context, open-work attention and archived-origin behavior.

before.body:
Already experiencing effects, maybe have a way to quick archive the "Done" swimlane and also a way to go back and view past archived done tickets and unarchive return to active if possible

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started. Proposed behavior below remains subject to human scope review.

### Intended outcome

Clear completed tickets from the active board quickly, while keeping their history easy to browse and restore.

### Scope and approach

Add an Archive completed tickets action to a Done-status column header. Proposed first-release behavior: archive only unarchived tickets in that column that match the current view/search filters, across its visible groups. Before applying, show the exact count and scope, with a way to inspect the affected tickets. Provide an obvious Archived tickets view with search and an Unarchive action.

Unarchiving returns a ticket to the active board in its existing workflow stage (usually Done); moving it back into development remains a separate explicit action. Archiving a parent does not implicitly archive its children. This is a focused implementation follow-up to #23; it need not wait for every clutter-management recommendation.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A Done-role column offers the archive action, including renamed/custom Done columns; non-Done columns do not silently offer the same completed-work operation.
- [ ] The preview names the column, filter scope and affected ticket count. Empty sets are harmless; cancel changes nothing. Tickets outside the preview are never archived.
- [ ] Each write uses the previewed ticket revision. Concurrent changes are rejected for that ticket, with clear success/failure counts and a refresh/review path; no stale record is overwritten.
- [ ] Archived tickets disappear from ordinary active views and remain searchable in an explicitly labeled archive view.
- [ ] A ticket can be opened and unarchived from the archive view. Its status, number, prose, comments, attachments, decisions and parent/child links survive the round trip.
- [ ] Archiving preserves decision/rule discovery and does not delete local screenshots or implicitly archive linked records.
- [ ] The action and archive navigation work with keyboard input, and the chosen scope stays explicit when filters or column visibility change.

### Implementation notes and related work

Reuse the existing archived metadata and is:archived filtering in web/model.ts and the detail Unarchive action. Inspect web/BoardView.tsx, web/ProjectPage.tsx and revision-checked record updates in src/store.ts. Related: parent #23, #17 bulk actions, #46 column visibility. Scheduled/automatic archiving and deletion are outside this ticket.

### Human review / verification

On a fixture with completed parent/child tickets and active work, archive a filtered Done subset, find it through Archived tickets, then restore one ticket. Verify unrelated tickets and linked project knowledge remain intact. Exercise a concurrent edit during the preview to confirm it is reported rather than overwritten.

after.body:
Already experiencing effects, maybe have a way to quick archive the "Done" swimlane and also a way to go back and view past archived done tickets and unarchive return to active if possible

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started. Proposed behavior below remains subject to human scope review.

### Intended outcome

Clear completed tickets from the active board quickly, while keeping their history easy to browse and restore.

### Scope and approach

Add an Archive completed tickets action to a Done-status column header. Proposed first-release behavior: archive only unarchived tickets in that column that match the current view/search filters, across its visible groups. Before applying, show the exact count and scope, with a way to inspect the affected tickets. Provide an obvious Archived tickets view with search and an Unarchive action.

Unarchiving returns a ticket to the active board in its existing workflow stage (usually Done); moving it back into development remains a separate explicit action. Archiving a parent does not implicitly archive its children. This is a focused implementation follow-up to #23; it need not wait for every clutter-management recommendation.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A Done-role column offers the archive action, including renamed/custom Done columns; non-Done columns do not silently offer the same completed-work operation.
- [ ] The preview names the column, filter scope and affected ticket count. Empty sets are harmless; cancel changes nothing. Tickets outside the preview are never archived.
- [ ] Each write uses the previewed ticket revision. Concurrent changes are rejected for that ticket, with clear success/failure counts and a refresh/review path; no stale record is overwritten.
- [ ] Archived tickets disappear from ordinary active views and remain searchable in an explicitly labeled archive view.
- [ ] A ticket can be opened and unarchived from the archive view. Its status, number, prose, comments, attachments, decisions and parent/child links survive the round trip.
- [ ] Archiving preserves decision/rule discovery and does not delete local screenshots or implicitly archive linked records.
- [ ] The action and archive navigation work with keyboard input, and the chosen scope stays explicit when filters or column visibility change.

### Implementation notes and related work

Reuse the existing archived metadata and is:archived filtering in web/model.ts and the detail Unarchive action. Inspect web/BoardView.tsx, web/ProjectPage.tsx and revision-checked record updates in src/store.ts. Related: parent #23, #17 bulk actions, #46 column visibility. Scheduled/automatic archiving and deletion are outside this ticket.

### Human review / verification

On a fixture with completed parent/child tickets and active work, archive a filtered Done subset, find it through Archived tickets, then restore one ticket. Verify unrelated tickets and linked project knowledge remain intact. Exercise a concurrent edit during the preview to confirm it is reported rather than overwritten.

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Provide a dedicated vertical planning view where dragging tickets changes the order in which work should be considered.

### Scope and approach

Build on the saved table view and existing manual/priority sorting. Offer an obvious Priority planning preset, rank tickets within priority groups, and allow explicit movement into another priority group. Ordering must not silently change workflow status or parent. Explain that priority is the urgency bucket and rank is the order within it.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The planning view shows a vertical list with priority groups and visible drag handles, including the start/end of each group.
- [ ] Dragging within a group changes persistent relative rank; dragging to another priority group updates priority and rank visibly.
- [ ] Reordering across tickets with different statuses does not move either ticket to the other status or change its parent.
- [ ] Move up/down and move-to-priority controls provide keyboard alternatives, including first/last positions.
- [ ] Reloading or returning to the saved view retains the order; concurrent reorder failures reconcile without losing tickets.
- [ ] Filtered reordering uses defined visible anchors and preserves the relative order of hidden tickets; saved sort modes clearly indicate whether manual reordering is active.

Start with web/ProjectPage.tsx place/peersOf, web/TableView.tsx and web/model.ts sortTickets. Current place also copies the target status, so reuse needs care. Coordinate drag preview with #22; prefer existing order metadata over a second competing ranking field.

### Human review / verification

Rank tickets across several stages and priorities, move to first/last, refresh, and repeat with a filter and keyboard controls. Confirm that status/parent stay unchanged and priority changes only when crossing an explicit priority group.

before.body:
Already experiencing effects, maybe have a way to quick archive the "Done" swimlane and also a way to go back and view past archived done tickets and unarchive return to active if possible

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started. Proposed behavior below remains subject to human scope review.

### Intended outcome

Clear completed tickets from the active board quickly, while keeping their history easy to browse and restore.

### Scope and approach

Add an Archive completed tickets action to a Done-status column header. Proposed first-release behavior: archive only unarchived tickets in that column that match the current view/search filters, across its visible groups. Before applying, show the exact count and scope, with a way to inspect the affected tickets. Provide an obvious Archived tickets view with search and an Unarchive action.

Unarchiving returns a ticket to the active board in its existing workflow stage (usually Done); moving it back into development remains a separate explicit action. Archiving a parent does not implicitly archive its children. This is a focused implementation follow-up to #23; it need not wait for every clutter-management recommendation.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A Done-role column offers the archive action, including renamed/custom Done columns; non-Done columns do not silently offer the same completed-work operation.
- [ ] The preview names the column, filter scope and affected ticket count. Empty sets are harmless; cancel changes nothing. Tickets outside the preview are never archived.
- [ ] Each write uses the previewed ticket revision. Concurrent changes are rejected for that ticket, with clear success/failure counts and a refresh/review path; no stale record is overwritten.
- [ ] Archived tickets disappear from ordinary active views and remain searchable in an explicitly labeled archive view.
- [ ] A ticket can be opened and unarchived from the archive view. Its status, number, prose, comments, attachments, decisions and parent/child links survive the round trip.
- [ ] Archiving preserves decision/rule discovery and does not delete local screenshots or implicitly archive linked records.
- [ ] The action and archive navigation work with keyboard input, and the chosen scope stays explicit when filters or column visibility change.

### Implementation notes and related work

Reuse the existing archived metadata and is:archived filtering in web/model.ts and the detail Unarchive action. Inspect web/BoardView.tsx, web/ProjectPage.tsx and revision-checked record updates in src/store.ts. Related: parent #23, #17 bulk actions, #46 column visibility. Scheduled/automatic archiving and deletion are outside this ticket.

### Human review / verification

On a fixture with completed parent/child tickets and active work, archive a filtered Done subset, find it through Archived tickets, then restore one ticket. Verify unrelated tickets and linked project knowledge remain intact. Exercise a concurrent edit during the preview to confirm it is reported rather than overwritten.

agentReview.rationale: The offline playbook UI is promising, but the copied workflow prompts need to match both project-local installation and the managed-agent protocol.
agentReview.criteria: Make the connection recipe identify the installed project launcher and guide (.controlroom/controlroom and .controlroom/AGENT_GUIDE.md, with the source-checkout alternative explicitly separate). Avoid assuming a global controlroom executable. In pickup/progress/review/feedback recipes, distinguish manual agents from controller-managed assignments: managed workers return their structured handoff and do not issue manual claim/move/review/release or overwrite another assignment; stopped work requires explicit orchestrator takeover. Do not unconditionally instruct every review to wait for human Done when the configured independent orchestrator can accept it. Retain scope/identity protections. Use valid stable IDs for aria-labelledby group headings. Add browser checks for search, keyboard copy success and clipboard-denial fallback, public ticket substitution, and no mutation/execution on Copy.
agentReview.evidence: Exact commit6a65794 review: connection starts with Read AGENT_GUIDE.md and tool-source ./controlroom, while shipped installer src/cli.ts writes the project guide and launcher under .controlroom. Subsequent recipes use a global controlroom command. Pickup directs claim/move and submission directs manual review unconditionally, contrary to the managed-worker exception in the shipped guide; feedback similarly directs a manual lifecycle submission. This can reproduce already-observed assignment conflicts when users paste the recipes into managed agent workflows. Playbook.tsx also uses literal group strings with spaces in IDs and aria-labelledby, which are parsed as multiple ID references. Controller core/build passed; static recipe checks do not cover clipboard or accessibility behavior.

before.body:
## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Give users a Help/Playbook tab with short, copyable prompts for working with their existing coding agent and this project board.

### Scope and approach

Provide concise recipes for connection/setup, refining Concept tickets, planning an approved parent, picking up work, reporting progress, submitting review evidence, responding to feedback, documenting decisions, and maintaining the rulebook. Include screenshot feedback and shortcut help; no embedded provider or agent execution is required.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An in-app Help/Playbook entry offers searchable or clearly grouped recipes, each with its purpose, prerequisites, and a short copyable prompt.
- [ ] Prompts use real project context where available and clearly mark user-supplied placeholders; copied text contains no local auth tokens or hidden secrets.
- [ ] Ticket-specific recipes use public numbers with shell-safe examples and explain scope approval, claims, Review, and human acceptance.
- [ ] Setup guidance matches the shipped CLI/MCP protocol; the source stays easy to update alongside AGENT_GUIDE.md.
- [ ] Copy confirms success accessibly, supports keyboard use, and has a fallback if clipboard access is unavailable.
- [ ] The playbook works offline and lets the user choose where to paste/run a prompt; clicking Copy does not start an agent or mutate tickets.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with AGENT_GUIDE.md, CLI help, web/Shortcuts.tsx, web/TopNav.tsx and web/Pages.tsx. Prefer a small shared content source to duplicated instructions that drift. Related: #27 for collecting human answers.

### Human review / verification

Follow the setup and review recipes against a disposable project using current CLI commands. Copy a ticket-specific prompt and verify correct number/context, no secrets, and no automatic execution.

meta.title: Create playbook and help tab containing short prompts you can send to LLM
meta.handoff: Implemented the Help & playbook tab. It provides 12 grouped, searchable, offline recipes with purpose, prerequisites, and copyable prompts. Ticket recipes accept a numeric public ticket number, interpolate project/branch context, use shell-safe numeric CLI examples, and distinguish claims, Review, and human acceptance. Content is centralized in web/playbookContent.ts with an AGENT_GUIDE.md alignment note. Copying never invokes an agent or mutates board state; it announces success accessibly and selects the prompt for manual copying when clipboard access fails. No board records or decisions were changed. A commit was not possible because the managed worktree denies writing its Git worktree index lock; changes remain in the checkout for the controller snapshot.
meta.evidence: npm ci completed. npm run build passed (TypeScript, Vite, and CLI bundle). Focused static validation passed for all 12 recipes, public ticket interpolation, required fields, and no secret-like strings. git diff --check passed; Prettier check passed for changed TypeScript files. npm test could not start because the sandbox denied tsx creation of its temporary IPC socket (EPERM at /var/folders/.../tsx-501/...pipe); no tests were discovered or run. Modified/new files: web/App.tsx, web/TopNav.tsx, web/styles.css, web/Playbook.tsx, web/playbookContent.ts.

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Give users a Help/Playbook tab with short, copyable prompts for working with their existing coding agent and this project board.

### Scope and approach

Provide concise recipes for connection/setup, refining Concept tickets, planning an approved parent, picking up work, reporting progress, submitting review evidence, responding to feedback, documenting decisions, and maintaining the rulebook. Include screenshot feedback and shortcut help; no embedded provider or agent execution is required.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An in-app Help/Playbook entry offers searchable or clearly grouped recipes, each with its purpose, prerequisites, and a short copyable prompt.
- [ ] Prompts use real project context where available and clearly mark user-supplied placeholders; copied text contains no local auth tokens or hidden secrets.
- [ ] Ticket-specific recipes use public numbers with shell-safe examples and explain scope approval, claims, Review, and human acceptance.
- [ ] Setup guidance matches the shipped CLI/MCP protocol; the source stays easy to update alongside AGENT_GUIDE.md.
- [ ] Copy confirms success accessibly, supports keyboard use, and has a fallback if clipboard access is unavailable.
- [ ] The playbook works offline and lets the user choose where to paste/run a prompt; clicking Copy does not start an agent or mutate tickets.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with AGENT_GUIDE.md, CLI help, web/Shortcuts.tsx, web/TopNav.tsx and web/Pages.tsx. Prefer a small shared content source to duplicated instructions that drift. Related: #27 for collecting human answers.

### Human review / verification

Follow the setup and review recipes against a disposable project using current CLI commands. Copy a ticket-specific prompt and verify correct number/context, no secrets, and no automatic execution.

before.body:
Already experiencing effects, maybe have a way to quick archive the "Done" swimlane and also a way to go back and view past archived done tickets and unarchive return to active if possible

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started. Proposed behavior below remains subject to human scope review.

### Intended outcome

Clear completed tickets from the active board quickly, while keeping their history easy to browse and restore.

### Scope and approach

Add an Archive completed tickets action to a Done-status column header. Proposed first-release behavior: archive only unarchived tickets in that column that match the current view/search filters, across its visible groups. Before applying, show the exact count and scope, with a way to inspect the affected tickets. Provide an obvious Archived tickets view with search and an Unarchive action.

Unarchiving returns a ticket to the active board in its existing workflow stage (usually Done); moving it back into development remains a separate explicit action. Archiving a parent does not implicitly archive its children. This is a focused implementation follow-up to #23; it need not wait for every clutter-management recommendation.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A Done-role column offers the archive action, including renamed/custom Done columns; non-Done columns do not silently offer the same completed-work operation.
- [ ] The preview names the column, filter scope and affected ticket count. Empty sets are harmless; cancel changes nothing. Tickets outside the preview are never archived.
- [ ] Each write uses the previewed ticket revision. Concurrent changes are rejected for that ticket, with clear success/failure counts and a refresh/review path; no stale record is overwritten.
- [ ] Archived tickets disappear from ordinary active views and remain searchable in an explicitly labeled archive view.
- [ ] A ticket can be opened and unarchived from the archive view. Its status, number, prose, comments, attachments, decisions and parent/child links survive the round trip.
- [ ] Archiving preserves decision/rule discovery and does not delete local screenshots or implicitly archive linked records.
- [ ] The action and archive navigation work with keyboard input, and the chosen scope stays explicit when filters or column visibility change.

### Implementation notes and related work

Reuse the existing archived metadata and is:archived filtering in web/model.ts and the detail Unarchive action. Inspect web/BoardView.tsx, web/ProjectPage.tsx and revision-checked record updates in src/store.ts. Related: parent #23, #17 bulk actions, #46 column visibility. Scheduled/automatic archiving and deletion are outside this ticket.

### Human review / verification

On a fixture with completed parent/child tickets and active work, archive a filtered Done subset, find it through Archived tickets, then restore one ticket. Verify unrelated tickets and linked project knowledge remain intact. Exercise a concurrent edit during the preview to confirm it is reported rather than overwritten.

after.body:
Already experiencing effects, maybe have a way to quick archive the "Done" swimlane and also a way to go back and view past archived done tickets and unarchive return to active if possible

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started. Proposed behavior below remains subject to human scope review.

### Intended outcome

Clear completed tickets from the active board quickly, while keeping their history easy to browse and restore.

### Scope and approach

Add an Archive completed tickets action to a Done-status column header. Proposed first-release behavior: archive only unarchived tickets in that column that match the current view/search filters, across its visible groups. Before applying, show the exact count and scope, with a way to inspect the affected tickets. Provide an obvious Archived tickets view with search and an Unarchive action.

Unarchiving returns a ticket to the active board in its existing workflow stage (usually Done); moving it back into development remains a separate explicit action. Archiving a parent does not implicitly archive its children. This is a focused implementation follow-up to #23; it need not wait for every clutter-management recommendation.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A Done-role column offers the archive action, including renamed/custom Done columns; non-Done columns do not silently offer the same completed-work operation.
- [ ] The preview names the column, filter scope and affected ticket count. Empty sets are harmless; cancel changes nothing. Tickets outside the preview are never archived.
- [ ] Each write uses the previewed ticket revision. Concurrent changes are rejected for that ticket, with clear success/failure counts and a refresh/review path; no stale record is overwritten.
- [ ] Archived tickets disappear from ordinary active views and remain searchable in an explicitly labeled archive view.
- [ ] A ticket can be opened and unarchived from the archive view. Its status, number, prose, comments, attachments, decisions and parent/child links survive the round trip.
- [ ] Archiving preserves decision/rule discovery and does not delete local screenshots or implicitly archive linked records.
- [ ] The action and archive navigation work with keyboard input, and the chosen scope stays explicit when filters or column visibility change.

### Implementation notes and related work

Reuse the existing archived metadata and is:archived filtering in web/model.ts and the detail Unarchive action. Inspect web/BoardView.tsx, web/ProjectPage.tsx and revision-checked record updates in src/store.ts. Related: parent #23, #17 bulk actions, #46 column visibility. Scheduled/automatic archiving and deletion are outside this ticket.

### Human review / verification

On a fixture with completed parent/child tickets and active work, archive a filtered Done subset, find it through Archived tickets, then restore one ticket. Verify unrelated tickets and linked project knowledge remain intact. Exercise a concurrent edit during the preview to confirm it is reported rather than overwritten.

meta.title: Create playbook and help tab containing short prompts you can send to LLM
meta.handoff: Implemented the Help & playbook tab. It provides 12 grouped, searchable, offline recipes with purpose, prerequisites, and copyable prompts. Ticket recipes accept a numeric public ticket number, interpolate project/branch context, use shell-safe numeric CLI examples, and distinguish claims, Review, and human acceptance. Content is centralized in web/playbookContent.ts with an AGENT_GUIDE.md alignment note. Copying never invokes an agent or mutates board state; it announces success accessibly and selects the prompt for manual copying when clipboard access fails. No board records or decisions were changed. A commit was not possible because the managed worktree denies writing its Git worktree index lock; changes remain in the checkout for the controller snapshot.

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Give users a Help/Playbook tab with short, copyable prompts for working with their existing coding agent and this project board.

### Scope and approach

Provide concise recipes for connection/setup, refining Concept tickets, planning an approved parent, picking up work, reporting progress, submitting review evidence, responding to feedback, documenting decisions, and maintaining the rulebook. Include screenshot feedback and shortcut help; no embedded provider or agent execution is required.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An in-app Help/Playbook entry offers searchable or clearly grouped recipes, each with its purpose, prerequisites, and a short copyable prompt.
- [ ] Prompts use real project context where available and clearly mark user-supplied placeholders; copied text contains no local auth tokens or hidden secrets.
- [ ] Ticket-specific recipes use public numbers with shell-safe examples and explain scope approval, claims, Review, and human acceptance.
- [ ] Setup guidance matches the shipped CLI/MCP protocol; the source stays easy to update alongside AGENT_GUIDE.md.
- [ ] Copy confirms success accessibly, supports keyboard use, and has a fallback if clipboard access is unavailable.
- [ ] The playbook works offline and lets the user choose where to paste/run a prompt; clicking Copy does not start an agent or mutate tickets.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with AGENT_GUIDE.md, CLI help, web/Shortcuts.tsx, web/TopNav.tsx and web/Pages.tsx. Prefer a small shared content source to duplicated instructions that drift. Related: #27 for collecting human answers.

### Human review / verification

Follow the setup and review recipes against a disposable project using current CLI commands. Copy a ticket-specific prompt and verify correct number/context, no secrets, and no automatic execution.

Prompts now use the project-local ./.controlroom/controlroom launcher and guide, separate the tool-source alternative, distinguish managed workers from manual agents, require explicit orchestrator takeover for stopped managed work, and allow an enabled independent orchestrator to accept managed work. No board data or decisions changed. Commit was attempted but denied because the managed worktree cannot create its shared Git index.lock; the controller can snapshot the listed working-tree changes.

The required npm test runner could not begin because this sandbox denies tsx IPC sockets (EPERM on /var/folders/.../tsx-501/...pipe; reproduces with TMPDIR=/private/tmp). Focused Playwright coverage likewise cannot start its local server because the sandbox denies listen on 127.0.0.1:4178. These occur before test discovery/execution and require controller verification outside this sandbox.

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Make workflow status customization easy to discover from the board and safe to use as the project evolves.

### Scope and approach

Settings already supports naming, roles, ordering, addition, and removal of columns. Expose a clear Customize statuses entry from the board and improve that existing editor. Retain stable IDs and explain why workflow roles control agent behavior; multiple columns can share a role, as Concept and Backlog do here.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A user can find status customization from the board, add a status, rename it, and change its order without editing configuration files.
- [ ] Renaming or reordering retains ticket associations, history, and saved views; refreshing preserves the configuration.
- [ ] The editor distinguishes display name from workflow role and validates required roles and invalid/blank names.
- [ ] Removing a populated status offers an explicit destination/migration flow or a clear route to move its tickets first; no tickets are orphaned.
- [ ] Where a role has multiple columns, default destinations for new tickets and agent role-based moves are visible and deterministic.
- [ ] Concurrent configuration changes cause reconciliation feedback rather than silent overwrites.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with web/Settings.tsx, web/ProjectPage.tsx, src/store.ts updateConfig and role-to-column lookups in src/cli.ts/src/mcp.ts. Extend existing configuration rather than introducing competing status data.

### Human review / verification

Add and rename a status, reorder it, reload, and remove an empty status. Exercise removal with tickets and ambiguous role destinations using Concept/Backlog and In Progress/Failed Review.

agentReview.rationale: The status editor improvements are useful, but concurrent configuration updates silently discard local edits before Save, violating the reconciliation requirement.
agentReview.criteria: Retain the editor baseline and unsaved name/column/shortcut drafts when configRevision changes externally. Show explicit reconciliation feedback and provide deliberate reload/reapply choices; never automatically replace dirty drafts with remote config. Add a browser regression that changes a status locally, updates config through another client, verifies the draft remains with conflict feedback, then reconciles and saves without losing the other client changes. Also exercise board entry, rename/reorder persistence and populated-column removal in the UI.
agentReview.evidence: Independent source review of exact commit8fc37e3. The new Settings useEffect on state.configRevision unconditionally calls setName, setColumns, setRevision and setShortcut. The SSE state refresh therefore replaces unsaved edits immediately and adopts the new revision, so the Save catch for Configuration changed is never reached in the ordinary concurrent-update case. The added tests/views.test.ts only exercises Store config revisions and cannot detect this UI data loss. Return a corrected snapshot within existing #18 scope; do not merge/deploy.

before.body:
## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Make workflow status customization easy to discover from the board and safe to use as the project evolves.

### Scope and approach

Settings already supports naming, roles, ordering, addition, and removal of columns. Expose a clear Customize statuses entry from the board and improve that existing editor. Retain stable IDs and explain why workflow roles control agent behavior; multiple columns can share a role, as Concept and Backlog do here.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A user can find status customization from the board, add a status, rename it, and change its order without editing configuration files.
- [ ] Renaming or reordering retains ticket associations, history, and saved views; refreshing preserves the configuration.
- [ ] The editor distinguishes display name from workflow role and validates required roles and invalid/blank names.
- [ ] Removing a populated status offers an explicit destination/migration flow or a clear route to move its tickets first; no tickets are orphaned.
- [ ] Where a role has multiple columns, default destinations for new tickets and agent role-based moves are visible and deterministic.
- [ ] Concurrent configuration changes cause reconciliation feedback rather than silent overwrites.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with web/Settings.tsx, web/ProjectPage.tsx, src/store.ts updateConfig and role-to-column lookups in src/cli.ts/src/mcp.ts. Extend existing configuration rather than introducing competing status data.

### Human review / verification

Add and rename a status, reorder it, reload, and remove an empty status. Exercise removal with tickets and ambiguous role destinations using Concept/Backlog and In Progress/Failed Review.

meta.title: Should be able to customize and change the statuses
meta.handoff: #18 implementation is present and committed at 37cbaa2 (following 8fc37e3). It adds board-level Customize statuses entry, status display-name/role editor, add/reorder/remove safeguards, deterministic role-default visibility, and explicit concurrent-config reconciliation with reload or three-way reapply.
meta.evidence: Clean worktree; git diff --check passed. `npm ci && npm run build` passed. `node --import tsx --test tests/views.test.ts` passed 7/7, including status display/order persistence and stale-config protection. Required `npm test` is blocked before discovery here by sandbox-denied tsx IPC socket (`listen EPERM`). The non-IPC network test reproduces the controller’s reported ENOENT because its child server cannot create its local service after the sandbox denies listening; browser regression is likewise blocked by `listen EPERM 127.0.0.1:4178`. No out-of-scope network/test changes were made.

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Make workflow status customization easy to discover from the board and safe to use as the project evolves.

### Scope and approach

Settings already supports naming, roles, ordering, addition, and removal of columns. Expose a clear Customize statuses entry from the board and improve that existing editor. Retain stable IDs and explain why workflow roles control agent behavior; multiple columns can share a role, as Concept and Backlog do here.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A user can find status customization from the board, add a status, rename it, and change its order without editing configuration files.
- [ ] Renaming or reordering retains ticket associations, history, and saved views; refreshing preserves the configuration.
- [ ] The editor distinguishes display name from workflow role and validates required roles and invalid/blank names.
- [ ] Removing a populated status offers an explicit destination/migration flow or a clear route to move its tickets first; no tickets are orphaned.
- [ ] Where a role has multiple columns, default destinations for new tickets and agent role-based moves are visible and deterministic.
- [ ] Concurrent configuration changes cause reconciliation feedback rather than silent overwrites.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with web/Settings.tsx, web/ProjectPage.tsx, src/store.ts updateConfig and role-to-column lookups in src/cli.ts/src/mcp.ts. Extend existing configuration rather than introducing competing status data.

### Human review / verification

Add and rename a status, reorder it, reload, and remove an empty status. Exercise removal with tickets and ambiguous role destinations using Concept/Backlog and In Progress/Failed Review.

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Offer a newest-first project activity feed so a human can quickly see what changed across tickets and project knowledge.

### Scope and approach

Add a Feed view combining meaningful ticket transitions/edits, comments, review submissions, and decision/rule changes. Reuse durable history and comments with stable event identities; keep Needs you focused on actionable items rather than replacing it.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Entries show actor, time, event type, ticket number/title or knowledge title, and a concise change summary; clicking opens the relevant record/conversation.
- [ ] New activity appears at the top while the user is at the top; when reading older items, offer a new-updates indicator without yanking scroll position.
- [ ] Refresh/reconnect does not duplicate entries; ordering is deterministic for equal timestamps and older history can be loaded incrementally.
- [ ] Filter by actor, event type, and related ticket; group noisy edits without hiding review requests or human questions.
- [ ] Durable comments and record history remain the source of truth; the feed is reconstructible and retains attribution.
- [ ] Archived-ticket events stay traceable, malformed/missing references degrade gracefully, and unrelated routine heartbeats do not flood the feed.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with src/store.ts historyFor/state/index, src/server.ts state updates, web/useProjectState.ts, web/Pages.tsx and web/TopNav.tsx. Account for current JSONL history and supported legacy events. Related: #23 and #28.

### Human review / verification

Create comments, submit review, change a rule, and update a ticket; verify newest-first attribution and deep links after reload. Test scrolling while new events arrive and loading older events without duplication.

before.body:
## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Approve work from the board or table without opening each ticket. Make scope approval and acceptance of completed work separate, clearly named actions.

### Scope and approach

Provide Approve scope for unapproved planned work, and Accept into Done for tickets in Review. Show the result inline. Batch actions share the selection model from #17. Scope approval alone should not silently select, start, or complete a ticket.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A human can approve a ticket’s scope from its card/row; approved and inherited-scope states are visually distinguishable.
- [ ] A human can accept a Review ticket into Done directly; its summary and evidence remain accessible before accepting.
- [ ] Selected tickets can receive the same eligible approval action with a visible selection count; ineligible items are identified rather than silently changed.
- [ ] Agent requests cannot approve scope or accept work into Done, including through the new bulk path.
- [ ] Stale revisions and partial failures are shown per ticket; successful changes retain human attribution and do not overwrite unrelated fields.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with web/TicketCard.tsx, web/TableView.tsx, web/ProjectPage.tsx and src/store.ts authority/history. Related: #17. Keep the two meanings of approval explicit in copy and action availability.

### Human review / verification

Approve scope on a single item and selected items, then accept a reviewed item. Check that status is unchanged by scope approval, agent calls remain rejected, and a stale item produces a clear result.

agentReview.rationale: The offline playbook UI is promising, but the copied workflow prompts need to match both project-local installation and the managed-agent protocol.
agentReview.criteria: Make the connection recipe identify the installed project launcher and guide (.controlroom/controlroom and .controlroom/AGENT_GUIDE.md, with the source-checkout alternative explicitly separate). Avoid assuming a global controlroom executable. In pickup/progress/review/feedback recipes, distinguish manual agents from controller-managed assignments: managed workers return their structured handoff and do not issue manual claim/move/review/release or overwrite another assignment; stopped work requires explicit orchestrator takeover. Do not unconditionally instruct every review to wait for human Done when the configured independent orchestrator can accept it. Retain scope/identity protections. Use valid stable IDs for aria-labelledby group headings. Add browser checks for search, keyboard copy success and clipboard-denial fallback, public ticket substitution, and no mutation/execution on Copy.

Subsequent recipes use a global controlroom command. Pickup directs claim/move and submission directs manual review unconditionally, contrary to the managed-worker exception in the shipped guide; feedback similarly directs a manual lifecycle submission. This can reproduce already-observed assignment conflicts when users paste the recipes into managed agent workflows. Playbook.tsx also uses literal group strings with spaces in IDs and aria-labelledby, which are parsed as multiple ID references. Controller core/build passed; static recipe checks do not cover clipboard or accessibility behavior.

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Give users a Help/Playbook tab with short, copyable prompts for working with their existing coding agent and this project board.

### Scope and approach

Provide concise recipes for connection/setup, refining Concept tickets, planning an approved parent, picking up work, reporting progress, submitting review evidence, responding to feedback, documenting decisions, and maintaining the rulebook. Include screenshot feedback and shortcut help; no embedded provider or agent execution is required.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An in-app Help/Playbook entry offers searchable or clearly grouped recipes, each with its purpose, prerequisites, and a short copyable prompt.
- [ ] Prompts use real project context where available and clearly mark user-supplied placeholders; copied text contains no local auth tokens or hidden secrets.
- [ ] Ticket-specific recipes use public numbers with shell-safe examples and explain scope approval, claims, Review, and human acceptance.
- [ ] Setup guidance matches the shipped CLI/MCP protocol; the source stays easy to update alongside AGENT_GUIDE.md.
- [ ] Copy confirms success accessibly, supports keyboard use, and has a fallback if clipboard access is unavailable.
- [ ] The playbook works offline and lets the user choose where to paste/run a prompt; clicking Copy does not start an agent or mutate tickets.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with AGENT_GUIDE.md, CLI help, web/Shortcuts.tsx, web/TopNav.tsx and web/Pages.tsx. Prefer a small shared content source to duplicated instructions that drift. Related: #27 for collecting human answers.

### Human review / verification

Follow the setup and review recipes against a disposable project using current CLI commands. Copy a ticket-specific prompt and verify correct number/context, no secrets, and no automatic execution.

meta.handoff: Implemented the Help & playbook tab and corrected its workflow guidance. The retained checkout includes the UI/content from commit 6a65794 plus uncommitted review corrections in web/Playbook.tsx and web/playbookContent.ts, and new browser coverage in tests/browser/playbook.spec.ts. Prompts now use the project-local ./.controlroom/controlroom launcher and guide, separate the tool-source alternative, distinguish managed workers from manual agents, require explicit orchestrator takeover for stopped managed work, and allow an enabled independent orchestrator to accept managed work. No board data or decisions changed. Commit was attempted but denied because the managed worktree cannot create its shared Git index.lock; the controller can snapshot the listed working-tree changes.
meta.evidence: Passed: npm ci; npm run build; Prettier check for changed TypeScript; git diff --check; static runtime validation of all 12 recipes, numeric interpolation, absence of secret-like prompt text, managed/manual routing, and independent-orchestrator review language. The required npm test runner could not begin because this sandbox denies tsx IPC sockets (EPERM on /var/folders/.../tsx-501/...pipe; reproduces with TMPDIR=/private/tmp). Focused Playwright coverage likewise cannot start its local server because the sandbox denies listen on 127.0.0.1:4178. These occur before test discovery/execution and require controller verification outside this sandbox.

before.body:
## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Approve work from the board or table without opening each ticket. Make scope approval and acceptance of completed work separate, clearly named actions.

### Scope and approach

Provide Approve scope for unapproved planned work, and Accept into Done for tickets in Review. Show the result inline. Batch actions share the selection model from #17. Scope approval alone should not silently select, start, or complete a ticket.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A human can approve a ticket’s scope from its card/row; approved and inherited-scope states are visually distinguishable.
- [ ] A human can accept a Review ticket into Done directly; its summary and evidence remain accessible before accepting.
- [ ] Selected tickets can receive the same eligible approval action with a visible selection count; ineligible items are identified rather than silently changed.
- [ ] Agent requests cannot approve scope or accept work into Done, including through the new bulk path.
- [ ] Stale revisions and partial failures are shown per ticket; successful changes retain human attribution and do not overwrite unrelated fields.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with web/TicketCard.tsx, web/TableView.tsx, web/ProjectPage.tsx and src/store.ts authority/history. Related: #17. Keep the two meanings of approval explicit in copy and action availability.

### Human review / verification

Approve scope on a single item and selected items, then accept a reviewed item. Check that status is unchanged by scope approval, agent calls remain rejected, and a stale item produces a clear result.

meta.handoff: Implemented ticket #16 in commit 84e561e. Added quick scope approval and Review acceptance to board cards and table rows, plus selected-ticket actions with eligible counts and per-ticket outcomes. Review summaries/evidence are shown before acceptance. Added a human-only bulk API with attribution, revision validation, and partial-failure handling. No board records or decisions were changed; worktree is clean.
meta.evidence: Production build and typecheck passed. 34 focused/core tests passed, including new coverage for mixed success/stale/inherited batches, field preservation, attribution, Review evidence retention, and agent rejection. The prescribed npm ci and npm run build passed; npm test could not start because the sandbox rejects tsx’s IPC socket with EPERM. Running the suite via node --import tsx exercised 120 tests: 113 passed and 7 service/network tests failed solely because loopback binding is prohibited in this sandbox. git diff --check passed.

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Approve work from the board or table without opening each ticket. Make scope approval and acceptance of completed work separate, clearly named actions.

### Scope and approach

Provide Approve scope for unapproved planned work, and Accept into Done for tickets in Review. Show the result inline. Batch actions share the selection model from #17. Scope approval alone should not silently select, start, or complete a ticket.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A human can approve a ticket’s scope from its card/row; approved and inherited-scope states are visually distinguishable.
- [ ] A human can accept a Review ticket into Done directly; its summary and evidence remain accessible before accepting.
- [ ] Selected tickets can receive the same eligible approval action with a visible selection count; ineligible items are identified rather than silently changed.
- [ ] Agent requests cannot approve scope or accept work into Done, including through the new bulk path.
- [ ] Stale revisions and partial failures are shown per ticket; successful changes retain human attribution and do not overwrite unrelated fields.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with web/TicketCard.tsx, web/TableView.tsx, web/ProjectPage.tsx and src/store.ts authority/history. Related: #17. Keep the two meanings of approval explicit in copy and action availability.

### Human review / verification

Approve scope on a single item and selected items, then accept a reviewed item. Check that status is unchanged by scope approval, agent calls remain rejected, and a stale item produces a clear result.

before.body:
## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Approve work from the board or table without opening each ticket. Make scope approval and acceptance of completed work separate, clearly named actions.

### Scope and approach

Provide Approve scope for unapproved planned work, and Accept into Done for tickets in Review. Show the result inline. Batch actions share the selection model from #17. Scope approval alone should not silently select, start, or complete a ticket.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A human can approve a ticket’s scope from its card/row; approved and inherited-scope states are visually distinguishable.
- [ ] A human can accept a Review ticket into Done directly; its summary and evidence remain accessible before accepting.
- [ ] Selected tickets can receive the same eligible approval action with a visible selection count; ineligible items are identified rather than silently changed.
- [ ] Agent requests cannot approve scope or accept work into Done, including through the new bulk path.
- [ ] Stale revisions and partial failures are shown per ticket; successful changes retain human attribution and do not overwrite unrelated fields.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with web/TicketCard.tsx, web/TableView.tsx, web/ProjectPage.tsx and src/store.ts authority/history. Related: #17. Keep the two meanings of approval explicit in copy and action availability.

### Human review / verification

Approve scope on a single item and selected items, then accept a reviewed item. Check that status is unchanged by scope approval, agent calls remain rejected, and a stale item produces a clear result.

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Approve work from the board or table without opening each ticket. Make scope approval and acceptance of completed work separate, clearly named actions.

### Scope and approach

Provide Approve scope for unapproved planned work, and Accept into Done for tickets in Review. Show the result inline. Batch actions share the selection model from #17. Scope approval alone should not silently select, start, or complete a ticket.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A human can approve a ticket’s scope from its card/row; approved and inherited-scope states are visually distinguishable.
- [ ] A human can accept a Review ticket into Done directly; its summary and evidence remain accessible before accepting.
- [ ] Selected tickets can receive the same eligible approval action with a visible selection count; ineligible items are identified rather than silently changed.
- [ ] Agent requests cannot approve scope or accept work into Done, including through the new bulk path.
- [ ] Stale revisions and partial failures are shown per ticket; successful changes retain human attribution and do not overwrite unrelated fields.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with web/TicketCard.tsx, web/TableView.tsx, web/ProjectPage.tsx and src/store.ts authority/history. Related: #17. Keep the two meanings of approval explicit in copy and action availability.

### Human review / verification

Approve scope on a single item and selected items, then accept a reviewed item. Check that status is unchanged by scope approval, agent calls remain rejected, and a stale item produces a clear result.

Review summaries/evidence are shown before acceptance. Added a human-only bulk API with attribution, revision validation, and partial-failure handling. No board records or decisions were changed; worktree is clean.

The prescribed npm ci and npm run build passed; npm test could not start because the sandbox rejects tsx’s IPC socket with EPERM. Running the suite via node --import tsx exercised 120 tests: 113 passed and 7 service/network tests failed solely because loopback binding is prohibited in this sandbox. git diff --check passed.
