## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Approve work from the board or table without opening each ticket. Make scope approval and acceptance of completed work separate, clearly named actions.

### Scope and approach

Provide Approve scope for unapproved planned work, and Accept into Done for tickets in Review. Show the result inline. Batch actions share the selection model from #17. Scope approval alone should not silently select, start, or complete a ticket.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A human can approve a ticket’s scope from its card/row; approved and inherited-scope states are visually distinguishable.
- [ ] A human can accept a Review ticket into Done directly; its summary and evidence remain accessible before accepting.
- [ ] Selected tickets can receive the same eligible approval action with a visible selection count; ineligible items are identified rather than silently changed.
- [ ] Agent requests cannot approve scope or accept work into Done, including through the new bulk path.
- [ ] Stale revisions and partial failures are shown per ticket; successful changes retain human attribution and do not overwrite unrelated fields.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with web/TicketCard.tsx, web/TableView.tsx, web/ProjectPage.tsx and src/store.ts authority/history. Related: #17. Keep the two meanings of approval explicit in copy and action availability.

### Human review / verification

Approve scope on a single item and selected items, then accept a reviewed item. Check that status is unchanged by scope approval, agent calls remain rejected, and a stale item produces a clear result.

meta.title: A feed feature would be nice always showing latest updates up top

before.body:
## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Offer a newest-first project activity feed so a human can quickly see what changed across tickets and project knowledge.

### Scope and approach

Add a Feed view combining meaningful ticket transitions/edits, comments, review submissions, and decision/rule changes. Reuse durable history and comments with stable event identities; keep Needs you focused on actionable items rather than replacing it.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Entries show actor, time, event type, ticket number/title or knowledge title, and a concise change summary; clicking opens the relevant record/conversation.
- [ ] New activity appears at the top while the user is at the top; when reading older items, offer a new-updates indicator without yanking scroll position.
- [ ] Refresh/reconnect does not duplicate entries; ordering is deterministic for equal timestamps and older history can be loaded incrementally.
- [ ] Filter by actor, event type, and related ticket; group noisy edits without hiding review requests or human questions.
- [ ] Durable comments and record history remain the source of truth; the feed is reconstructible and retains attribution.
- [ ] Archived-ticket events stay traceable, malformed/missing references degrade gracefully, and unrelated routine heartbeats do not flood the feed.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with src/store.ts historyFor/state/index, src/server.ts state updates, web/useProjectState.ts, web/Pages.tsx and web/TopNav.tsx. Account for current JSONL history and supported legacy events. Related: #23 and #28.

### Human review / verification

Create comments, submit review, change a rule, and update a ticket; verify newest-first attribution and deep links after reload. Test scrolling while new events arrive and loading older events without duplication.

before.body:
## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Offer a newest-first project activity feed so a human can quickly see what changed across tickets and project knowledge.

### Scope and approach

Add a Feed view combining meaningful ticket transitions/edits, comments, review submissions, and decision/rule changes. Reuse durable history and comments with stable event identities; keep Needs you focused on actionable items rather than replacing it.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Entries show actor, time, event type, ticket number/title or knowledge title, and a concise change summary; clicking opens the relevant record/conversation.
- [ ] New activity appears at the top while the user is at the top; when reading older items, offer a new-updates indicator without yanking scroll position.
- [ ] Refresh/reconnect does not duplicate entries; ordering is deterministic for equal timestamps and older history can be loaded incrementally.
- [ ] Filter by actor, event type, and related ticket; group noisy edits without hiding review requests or human questions.
- [ ] Durable comments and record history remain the source of truth; the feed is reconstructible and retains attribution.
- [ ] Archived-ticket events stay traceable, malformed/missing references degrade gracefully, and unrelated routine heartbeats do not flood the feed.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with src/store.ts historyFor/state/index, src/server.ts state updates, web/useProjectState.ts, web/Pages.tsx and web/TopNav.tsx. Account for current JSONL history and supported legacy events. Related: #23 and #28.

### Human review / verification

Create comments, submit review, change a rule, and update a ticket; verify newest-first attribution and deep links after reload. Test scrolling while new events arrive and loading older events without duplication.

Added a reconstructible `/api/feed` projection over durable JSONL/legacy history and comments, stable event identities, deterministic cursor pagination, edit grouping, actor/type/record filters, archived and missing-record handling, and heartbeat suppression. Added the Feed navigation/UI, live-at-top insertion, a new-updates indicator that preserves scroll position, incremental older loading, and record/conversation deep links with focused comments. Added store/API tests and a browser acceptance test. No project decisions were created or changed. Commit was attempted but the sandbox cannot write the parent worktree Git index; changes remain ready for controller snapshot.

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Offer a newest-first project activity feed so a human can quickly see what changed across tickets and project knowledge.

### Scope and approach

Add a Feed view combining meaningful ticket transitions/edits, comments, review submissions, and decision/rule changes. Reuse durable history and comments with stable event identities; keep Needs you focused on actionable items rather than replacing it.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Entries show actor, time, event type, ticket number/title or knowledge title, and a concise change summary; clicking opens the relevant record/conversation.
- [ ] New activity appears at the top while the user is at the top; when reading older items, offer a new-updates indicator without yanking scroll position.
- [ ] Refresh/reconnect does not duplicate entries; ordering is deterministic for equal timestamps and older history can be loaded incrementally.
- [ ] Filter by actor, event type, and related ticket; group noisy edits without hiding review requests or human questions.
- [ ] Durable comments and record history remain the source of truth; the feed is reconstructible and retains attribution.
- [ ] Archived-ticket events stay traceable, malformed/missing references degrade gracefully, and unrelated routine heartbeats do not flood the feed.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with src/store.ts historyFor/state/index, src/server.ts state updates, web/useProjectState.ts, web/Pages.tsx and web/TopNav.tsx. Account for current JSONL history and supported legacy events. Related: #23 and #28.

### Human review / verification

Create comments, submit review, change a rule, and update a ticket; verify newest-first attribution and deep links after reload. Test scrolling while new events arrive and loading older events without duplication.

before.body:
## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Approve work from the board or table without opening each ticket. Make scope approval and acceptance of completed work separate, clearly named actions.

### Scope and approach

Provide Approve scope for unapproved planned work, and Accept into Done for tickets in Review. Show the result inline. Batch actions share the selection model from #17. Scope approval alone should not silently select, start, or complete a ticket.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A human can approve a ticket’s scope from its card/row; approved and inherited-scope states are visually distinguishable.
- [ ] A human can accept a Review ticket into Done directly; its summary and evidence remain accessible before accepting.
- [ ] Selected tickets can receive the same eligible approval action with a visible selection count; ineligible items are identified rather than silently changed.
- [ ] Agent requests cannot approve scope or accept work into Done, including through the new bulk path.
- [ ] Stale revisions and partial failures are shown per ticket; successful changes retain human attribution and do not overwrite unrelated fields.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with web/TicketCard.tsx, web/TableView.tsx, web/ProjectPage.tsx and src/store.ts authority/history. Related: #17. Keep the two meanings of approval explicit in copy and action availability.

### Human review / verification

Approve scope on a single item and selected items, then accept a reviewed item. Check that status is unchanged by scope approval, agent calls remain rejected, and a stale item produces a clear result.

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Approve work from the board or table without opening each ticket. Make scope approval and acceptance of completed work separate, clearly named actions.

### Scope and approach

Provide Approve scope for unapproved planned work, and Accept into Done for tickets in Review. Show the result inline. Batch actions share the selection model from #17. Scope approval alone should not silently select, start, or complete a ticket.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A human can approve a ticket’s scope from its card/row; approved and inherited-scope states are visually distinguishable.
- [ ] A human can accept a Review ticket into Done directly; its summary and evidence remain accessible before accepting.
- [ ] Selected tickets can receive the same eligible approval action with a visible selection count; ineligible items are identified rather than silently changed.
- [ ] Agent requests cannot approve scope or accept work into Done, including through the new bulk path.
- [ ] Stale revisions and partial failures are shown per ticket; successful changes retain human attribution and do not overwrite unrelated fields.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with web/TicketCard.tsx, web/TableView.tsx, web/ProjectPage.tsx and src/store.ts authority/history. Related: #17. Keep the two meanings of approval explicit in copy and action availability.

### Human review / verification

Approve scope on a single item and selected items, then accept a reviewed item. Check that status is unchanged by scope approval, agent calls remain rejected, and a stale item produces a clear result.

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Offer a newest-first project activity feed so a human can quickly see what changed across tickets and project knowledge.

### Scope and approach

Add a Feed view combining meaningful ticket transitions/edits, comments, review submissions, and decision/rule changes. Reuse durable history and comments with stable event identities; keep Needs you focused on actionable items rather than replacing it.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Entries show actor, time, event type, ticket number/title or knowledge title, and a concise change summary; clicking opens the relevant record/conversation.
- [ ] New activity appears at the top while the user is at the top; when reading older items, offer a new-updates indicator without yanking scroll position.
- [ ] Refresh/reconnect does not duplicate entries; ordering is deterministic for equal timestamps and older history can be loaded incrementally.
- [ ] Filter by actor, event type, and related ticket; group noisy edits without hiding review requests or human questions.
- [ ] Durable comments and record history remain the source of truth; the feed is reconstructible and retains attribution.
- [ ] Archived-ticket events stay traceable, malformed/missing references degrade gracefully, and unrelated routine heartbeats do not flood the feed.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with src/store.ts historyFor/state/index, src/server.ts state updates, web/useProjectState.ts, web/Pages.tsx and web/TopNav.tsx. Account for current JSONL history and supported legacy events. Related: #23 and #28.

### Human review / verification

Create comments, submit review, change a rule, and update a ticket; verify newest-first attribution and deep links after reload. Test scrolling while new events arrive and loading older events without duplication.

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Offer a newest-first project activity feed so a human can quickly see what changed across tickets and project knowledge.

### Scope and approach

Add a Feed view combining meaningful ticket transitions/edits, comments, review submissions, and decision/rule changes. Reuse durable history and comments with stable event identities; keep Needs you focused on actionable items rather than replacing it.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Entries show actor, time, event type, ticket number/title or knowledge title, and a concise change summary; clicking opens the relevant record/conversation.
- [ ] New activity appears at the top while the user is at the top; when reading older items, offer a new-updates indicator without yanking scroll position.
- [ ] Refresh/reconnect does not duplicate entries; ordering is deterministic for equal timestamps and older history can be loaded incrementally.
- [ ] Filter by actor, event type, and related ticket; group noisy edits without hiding review requests or human questions.
- [ ] Durable comments and record history remain the source of truth; the feed is reconstructible and retains attribution.
- [ ] Archived-ticket events stay traceable, malformed/missing references degrade gracefully, and unrelated routine heartbeats do not flood the feed.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with src/store.ts historyFor/state/index, src/server.ts state updates, web/useProjectState.ts, web/Pages.tsx and web/TopNav.tsx. Account for current JSONL history and supported legacy events. Related: #23 and #28.

### Human review / verification

Create comments, submit review, change a rule, and update a ticket; verify newest-first attribution and deep links after reload. Test scrolling while new events arrive and loading older events without duplication.

meta.title: A feed feature would be nice always showing latest updates up top
meta.handoff: Implemented #25 as a newest-first Feed view. Added a reconstructible `/api/feed` projection over durable JSONL/legacy history and comments, stable event identities, deterministic cursor pagination, edit grouping, actor/type/record filters, archived and missing-record handling, and heartbeat suppression. Added the Feed navigation/UI, live-at-top insertion, a new-updates indicator that preserves scroll position, incremental older loading, and record/conversation deep links with focused comments. Added store/API tests and a browser acceptance test. No project decisions were created or changed. Commit was attempted but the sandbox cannot write the parent worktree Git index; changes remain ready for controller snapshot.

Controller’s prior run passed all three feed tests and 119/120 repository tests; its sole failure was the unrelated LAN listener test.
The exact command completed `npm ci` and build, but this managed sandbox denied tsx’s local IPC socket with `listen EPERM`. The isolated LAN test likewise could not create its listener/service file, and the browser test server was blocked from binding `127.0.0.1:4178`. These are environment restrictions, not feed failures; controller verification should run them in its network-enabled environment.
Human review: create a comment, submit a review, change a rule, and update/archive a ticket; confirm newest-first attribution and deep links after reload. Scroll down before another update and verify the indicator appears without moving the viewport, then load older activity and confirm no duplicates.

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Offer a newest-first project activity feed so a human can quickly see what changed across tickets and project knowledge.

### Scope and approach

Add a Feed view combining meaningful ticket transitions/edits, comments, review submissions, and decision/rule changes. Reuse durable history and comments with stable event identities; keep Needs you focused on actionable items rather than replacing it.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Entries show actor, time, event type, ticket number/title or knowledge title, and a concise change summary; clicking opens the relevant record/conversation.
- [ ] New activity appears at the top while the user is at the top; when reading older items, offer a new-updates indicator without yanking scroll position.
- [ ] Refresh/reconnect does not duplicate entries; ordering is deterministic for equal timestamps and older history can be loaded incrementally.
- [ ] Filter by actor, event type, and related ticket; group noisy edits without hiding review requests or human questions.
- [ ] Durable comments and record history remain the source of truth; the feed is reconstructible and retains attribution.
- [ ] Archived-ticket events stay traceable, malformed/missing references degrade gracefully, and unrelated routine heartbeats do not flood the feed.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with src/store.ts historyFor/state/index, src/server.ts state updates, web/useProjectState.ts, web/Pages.tsx and web/TopNav.tsx. Account for current JSONL history and supported legacy events. Related: #23 and #28.

### Human review / verification

Create comments, submit review, change a rule, and update a ticket; verify newest-first attribution and deep links after reload. Test scrolling while new events arrive and loading older events without duplication.

Added the Feed navigation/UI, live-at-top insertion, a new-updates indicator that preserves scroll position, incremental older loading, and record/conversation deep links with focused comments. Added store/API tests and a browser acceptance test. No project decisions were created or changed. Commit was attempted but the sandbox cannot write the parent worktree Git index; changes remain ready for controller snapshot.

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Approve work from the board or table without opening each ticket. Make scope approval and acceptance of completed work separate, clearly named actions.

### Scope and approach

Provide Approve scope for unapproved planned work, and Accept into Done for tickets in Review. Show the result inline. Batch actions share the selection model from #17. Scope approval alone should not silently select, start, or complete a ticket.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A human can approve a ticket’s scope from its card/row; approved and inherited-scope states are visually distinguishable.
- [ ] A human can accept a Review ticket into Done directly; its summary and evidence remain accessible before accepting.
- [ ] Selected tickets can receive the same eligible approval action with a visible selection count; ineligible items are identified rather than silently changed.
- [ ] Agent requests cannot approve scope or accept work into Done, including through the new bulk path.
- [ ] Stale revisions and partial failures are shown per ticket; successful changes retain human attribution and do not overwrite unrelated fields.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with web/TicketCard.tsx, web/TableView.tsx, web/ProjectPage.tsx and src/store.ts authority/history. Related: #17. Keep the two meanings of approval explicit in copy and action availability.

### Human review / verification

Approve scope on a single item and selected items, then accept a reviewed item. Check that status is unchanged by scope approval, agent calls remain rejected, and a stale item produces a clear result.

Added a reconstructible `/api/feed` projection over durable JSONL/legacy history and comments, stable event identities, deterministic cursor pagination, edit grouping, actor/type/record filters, archived and missing-record handling, and heartbeat suppression. Human review: create a comment, submit a review, change a rule, and update/archive a ticket; confirm newest-first attribution and deep links after reload. Scroll down before another update and verify the indicator appears without moving the viewport, then load older activity and confirm no duplicates.

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Offer a newest-first project activity feed so a human can quickly see what changed across tickets and project knowledge.

### Scope and approach

Add a Feed view combining meaningful ticket transitions/edits, comments, review submissions, and decision/rule changes. Reuse durable history and comments with stable event identities; keep Needs you focused on actionable items rather than replacing it.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Entries show actor, time, event type, ticket number/title or knowledge title, and a concise change summary; clicking opens the relevant record/conversation.
- [ ] New activity appears at the top while the user is at the top; when reading older items, offer a new-updates indicator without yanking scroll position.
- [ ] Refresh/reconnect does not duplicate entries; ordering is deterministic for equal timestamps and older history can be loaded incrementally.
- [ ] Filter by actor, event type, and related ticket; group noisy edits without hiding review requests or human questions.
- [ ] Durable comments and record history remain the source of truth; the feed is reconstructible and retains attribution.
- [ ] Archived-ticket events stay traceable, malformed/missing references degrade gracefully, and unrelated routine heartbeats do not flood the feed.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with src/store.ts historyFor/state/index, src/server.ts state updates, web/useProjectState.ts, web/Pages.tsx and web/TopNav.tsx. Account for current JSONL history and supported legacy events. Related: #23 and #28.

### Human review / verification

Create comments, submit review, change a rule, and update a ticket; verify newest-first attribution and deep links after reload. Test scrolling while new events arrive and loading older events without duplication.

Added the Feed navigation/UI, live-at-top insertion, a new-updates indicator that preserves scroll position, incremental older loading, and record/conversation deep links with focused comments. Added store/API tests and a browser acceptance test. No project decisions were created or changed. Commit was attempted but the sandbox cannot write the parent worktree Git index; changes remain ready for controller snapshot.

before.body:
## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Approve work from the board or table without opening each ticket. Make scope approval and acceptance of completed work separate, clearly named actions.

### Scope and approach

Provide Approve scope for unapproved planned work, and Accept into Done for tickets in Review. Show the result inline. Batch actions share the selection model from #17. Scope approval alone should not silently select, start, or complete a ticket.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A human can approve a ticket’s scope from its card/row; approved and inherited-scope states are visually distinguishable.
- [ ] A human can accept a Review ticket into Done directly; its summary and evidence remain accessible before accepting.
- [ ] Selected tickets can receive the same eligible approval action with a visible selection count; ineligible items are identified rather than silently changed.
- [ ] Agent requests cannot approve scope or accept work into Done, including through the new bulk path.
- [ ] Stale revisions and partial failures are shown per ticket; successful changes retain human attribution and do not overwrite unrelated fields.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with web/TicketCard.tsx, web/TableView.tsx, web/ProjectPage.tsx and src/store.ts authority/history. Related: #17. Keep the two meanings of approval explicit in copy and action availability.

### Human review / verification

Approve scope on a single item and selected items, then accept a reviewed item. Check that status is unchanged by scope approval, agent calls remain rejected, and a stale item produces a clear result.

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Approve work from the board or table without opening each ticket. Make scope approval and acceptance of completed work separate, clearly named actions.

### Scope and approach

Provide Approve scope for unapproved planned work, and Accept into Done for tickets in Review. Show the result inline. Batch actions share the selection model from #17. Scope approval alone should not silently select, start, or complete a ticket.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A human can approve a ticket’s scope from its card/row; approved and inherited-scope states are visually distinguishable.
- [ ] A human can accept a Review ticket into Done directly; its summary and evidence remain accessible before accepting.
- [ ] Selected tickets can receive the same eligible approval action with a visible selection count; ineligible items are identified rather than silently changed.
- [ ] Agent requests cannot approve scope or accept work into Done, including through the new bulk path.
- [ ] Stale revisions and partial failures are shown per ticket; successful changes retain human attribution and do not overwrite unrelated fields.

Start with web/TicketCard.tsx, web/TableView.tsx, web/ProjectPage.tsx and src/store.ts authority/history. Related: #17. Keep the two meanings of approval explicit in copy and action availability.

### Human review / verification

Approve scope on a single item and selected items, then accept a reviewed item. Check that status is unchanged by scope approval, agent calls remain rejected, and a stale item produces a clear result.

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Approve work from the board or table without opening each ticket. Make scope approval and acceptance of completed work separate, clearly named actions.

### Scope and approach

Provide Approve scope for unapproved planned work, and Accept into Done for tickets in Review. Show the result inline. Batch actions share the selection model from #17. Scope approval alone should not silently select, start, or complete a ticket.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A human can approve a ticket’s scope from its card/row; approved and inherited-scope states are visually distinguishable.
- [ ] A human can accept a Review ticket into Done directly; its summary and evidence remain accessible before accepting.
- [ ] Selected tickets can receive the same eligible approval action with a visible selection count; ineligible items are identified rather than silently changed.
- [ ] Agent requests cannot approve scope or accept work into Done, including through the new bulk path.
- [ ] Stale revisions and partial failures are shown per ticket; successful changes retain human attribution and do not overwrite unrelated fields.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with web/TicketCard.tsx, web/TableView.tsx, web/ProjectPage.tsx and src/store.ts authority/history. Related: #17. Keep the two meanings of approval explicit in copy and action availability.

### Human review / verification

Approve scope on a single item and selected items, then accept a reviewed item. Check that status is unchanged by scope approval, agent calls remain rejected, and a stale item produces a clear result.

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Offer a newest-first project activity feed so a human can quickly see what changed across tickets and project knowledge.

### Scope and approach

Add a Feed view combining meaningful ticket transitions/edits, comments, review submissions, and decision/rule changes. Reuse durable history and comments with stable event identities; keep Needs you focused on actionable items rather than replacing it.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Entries show actor, time, event type, ticket number/title or knowledge title, and a concise change summary; clicking opens the relevant record/conversation.
- [ ] New activity appears at the top while the user is at the top; when reading older items, offer a new-updates indicator without yanking scroll position.
- [ ] Refresh/reconnect does not duplicate entries; ordering is deterministic for equal timestamps and older history can be loaded incrementally.
- [ ] Filter by actor, event type, and related ticket; group noisy edits without hiding review requests or human questions.
- [ ] Durable comments and record history remain the source of truth; the feed is reconstructible and retains attribution.
- [ ] Archived-ticket events stay traceable, malformed/missing references degrade gracefully, and unrelated routine heartbeats do not flood the feed.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with src/store.ts historyFor/state/index, src/server.ts state updates, web/useProjectState.ts, web/Pages.tsx and web/TopNav.tsx. Account for current JSONL history and supported legacy events. Related: #23 and #28.

### Human review / verification

Create comments, submit review, change a rule, and update a ticket; verify newest-first attribution and deep links after reload. Test scrolling while new events arrive and loading older events without duplication.

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Offer a newest-first project activity feed so a human can quickly see what changed across tickets and project knowledge.

### Scope and approach

Add a Feed view combining meaningful ticket transitions/edits, comments, review submissions, and decision/rule changes. Reuse durable history and comments with stable event identities; keep Needs you focused on actionable items rather than replacing it.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Entries show actor, time, event type, ticket number/title or knowledge title, and a concise change summary; clicking opens the relevant record/conversation.
- [ ] New activity appears at the top while the user is at the top; when reading older items, offer a new-updates indicator without yanking scroll position.
- [ ] Refresh/reconnect does not duplicate entries; ordering is deterministic for equal timestamps and older history can be loaded incrementally.
- [ ] Filter by actor, event type, and related ticket; group noisy edits without hiding review requests or human questions.
- [ ] Durable comments and record history remain the source of truth; the feed is reconstructible and retains attribution.
- [ ] Archived-ticket events stay traceable, malformed/missing references degrade gracefully, and unrelated routine heartbeats do not flood the feed.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with src/store.ts historyFor/state/index, src/server.ts state updates, web/useProjectState.ts, web/Pages.tsx and web/TopNav.tsx. Account for current JSONL history and supported legacy events. Related: #23 and #28.

### Human review / verification

Create comments, submit review, change a rule, and update a ticket; verify newest-first attribution and deep links after reload. Test scrolling while new events arrive and loading older events without duplication.

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Approve work from the board or table without opening each ticket. Make scope approval and acceptance of completed work separate, clearly named actions.

### Scope and approach

Provide Approve scope for unapproved planned work, and Accept into Done for tickets in Review. Show the result inline. Batch actions share the selection model from #17. Scope approval alone should not silently select, start, or complete a ticket.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A human can approve a ticket’s scope from its card/row; approved and inherited-scope states are visually distinguishable.
- [ ] A human can accept a Review ticket into Done directly; its summary and evidence remain accessible before accepting.
- [ ] Selected tickets can receive the same eligible approval action with a visible selection count; ineligible items are identified rather than silently changed.
- [ ] Agent requests cannot approve scope or accept work into Done, including through the new bulk path.
- [ ] Stale revisions and partial failures are shown per ticket; successful changes retain human attribution and do not overwrite unrelated fields.

Start with web/TicketCard.tsx, web/TableView.tsx, web/ProjectPage.tsx and src/store.ts authority/history. Related: #17. Keep the two meanings of approval explicit in copy and action availability.

### Human review / verification

Approve scope on a single item and selected items, then accept a reviewed item. Check that status is unchanged by scope approval, agent calls remain rejected, and a stale item produces a clear result.

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Offer a newest-first project activity feed so a human can quickly see what changed across tickets and project knowledge.

### Scope and approach

Add a Feed view combining meaningful ticket transitions/edits, comments, review submissions, and decision/rule changes. Reuse durable history and comments with stable event identities; keep Needs you focused on actionable items rather than replacing it.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Entries show actor, time, event type, ticket number/title or knowledge title, and a concise change summary; clicking opens the relevant record/conversation.
- [ ] New activity appears at the top while the user is at the top; when reading older items, offer a new-updates indicator without yanking scroll position.
- [ ] Refresh/reconnect does not duplicate entries; ordering is deterministic for equal timestamps and older history can be loaded incrementally.
- [ ] Filter by actor, event type, and related ticket; group noisy edits without hiding review requests or human questions.
- [ ] Durable comments and record history remain the source of truth; the feed is reconstructible and retains attribution.
- [ ] Archived-ticket events stay traceable, malformed/missing references degrade gracefully, and unrelated routine heartbeats do not flood the feed.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with src/store.ts historyFor/state/index, src/server.ts state updates, web/useProjectState.ts, web/Pages.tsx and web/TopNav.tsx. Account for current JSONL history and supported legacy events. Related: #23 and #28.

### Human review / verification

Create comments, submit review, change a rule, and update a ticket; verify newest-first attribution and deep links after reload. Test scrolling while new events arrive and loading older events without duplication.

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Approve work from the board or table without opening each ticket. Make scope approval and acceptance of completed work separate, clearly named actions.

### Scope and approach

Provide Approve scope for unapproved planned work, and Accept into Done for tickets in Review. Show the result inline. Batch actions share the selection model from #17. Scope approval alone should not silently select, start, or complete a ticket.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A human can approve a ticket’s scope from its card/row; approved and inherited-scope states are visually distinguishable.
- [ ] A human can accept a Review ticket into Done directly; its summary and evidence remain accessible before accepting.
- [ ] Selected tickets can receive the same eligible approval action with a visible selection count; ineligible items are identified rather than silently changed.
- [ ] Agent requests cannot approve scope or accept work into Done, including through the new bulk path.
- [ ] Stale revisions and partial failures are shown per ticket; successful changes retain human attribution and do not overwrite unrelated fields.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with web/TicketCard.tsx, web/TableView.tsx, web/ProjectPage.tsx and src/store.ts authority/history. Related: #17. Keep the two meanings of approval explicit in copy and action availability.

### Human review / verification

Approve scope on a single item and selected items, then accept a reviewed item. Check that status is unchanged by scope approval, agent calls remain rejected, and a stale item produces a clear result.

No board records or decisions were changed; worktree is clean.

Browser execution could not start because the sandbox denied binding 127.0.0.1:4178 (`EPERM`). The prescribed `npm ci && npm run build && npm test` completed install/build, but `npm test` could not create tsx’s IPC socket (`EPERM`). Running the suite without tsx IPC produced 114/121 passing; all 7 failures require prohibited loopback/service binding. Commit: 5d57e0d.

Fresh explicit progress reports now add a prominent cyan sweep/glow and animated 12-band decorative waveform to board cards, table rows, and ticket details. The UI labels this as “Recent reported activity” and explains that the waveform is decorative, not measured agent activity. No new decision was required; this follows the existing progress-reporting decision and human feedback. Changes are in web/ProgressReport.tsx, web/styles.css, web/project.css, and tests/browser/activity-animation.spec.ts. before.body:
If in progress would be nice to see how long llm has worked on ticket as well as estimated progress. 

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Make in-progress work easier to monitor with restrained animation, elapsed time, and agent-reported progress that clearly communicates uncertainty.

### Scope and approach

Show current owner/claim, last reported update, elapsed time since entering In Progress, and an optional agent-reported percentage or checklist progress. Elapsed wall-clock time is not measured active work. Running-agent supervision remains outside the initial product; animation must not imply a verified live process.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Cards/rows and ticket details show last reported activity and elapsed time with explicit labels; reload reconstructs elapsed time from durable timestamps.
- [ ] Agents can report a short progress note and optional bounded percentage through CLI/MCP; percentages are labeled estimates, and missing values display as unknown rather than invented.
- [ ] Checklist completion, if shown from #20, is labeled separately from overall completion; 100% never automatically moves a ticket to Done.
- [ ] Expired claims, stale reports, and blockers are visibly distinct from recent reported activity; the UI never treats a claim alone as proof an agent is running.
- [ ] Subtle in-progress animation respects reduced-motion preferences and stops or changes appropriately for blocked/stale/review/done states.
- [ ] Repeated work sessions retain useful history; displayed elapsed duration uses a documented rule for leaving and re-entering In Progress, without double-counting or inventing active hours.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with web/TicketCard.tsx, web/TableView.tsx, src/types.ts, src/store.ts claims/history and CLI/MCP update interfaces. Prefer explicit reported data and disposable derived timers over writing a record every second. Related: #20 and #25.

### Human review / verification

Exercise a fresh report, missing estimate, stale/expired claim, blocker, and re-entry into In Progress with controlled timestamps. Reload and enable reduced motion; verify the labels never claim measured agent runtime.

Fresh explicit progress reports now add a prominent cyan sweep/glow and animated 12-band decorative waveform to board cards, table rows, and ticket details. The UI labels this as “Recent reported activity” and explains that the waveform is decorative, not measured agent activity. No new decision was required; this follows the existing progress-reporting decision and human feedback. Changes are in web/ProgressReport.tsx, web/styles.css, web/project.css, and tests/browser/activity-animation.spec.ts. Commit creation was blocked because the shared Git index is outside the writable sandbox; changes remain in the worktree for controller snapshotting.

after.body:
If in progress would be nice to see how long llm has worked on ticket as well as estimated progress. 

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Make in-progress work easier to monitor with restrained animation, elapsed time, and agent-reported progress that clearly communicates uncertainty.

### Scope and approach

Show current owner/claim, last reported update, elapsed time since entering In Progress, and an optional agent-reported percentage or checklist progress. Elapsed wall-clock time is not measured active work. Running-agent supervision remains outside the initial product; animation must not imply a verified live process.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Cards/rows and ticket details show last reported activity and elapsed time with explicit labels; reload reconstructs elapsed time from durable timestamps.
- [ ] Agents can report a short progress note and optional bounded percentage through CLI/MCP; percentages are labeled estimates, and missing values display as unknown rather than invented.
- [ ] Checklist completion, if shown from #20, is labeled separately from overall completion; 100% never automatically moves a ticket to Done.
- [ ] Expired claims, stale reports, and blockers are visibly distinct from recent reported activity; the UI never treats a claim alone as proof an agent is running.
- [ ] Subtle in-progress animation respects reduced-motion preferences and stops or changes appropriately for blocked/stale/review/done states.
- [ ] Repeated work sessions retain useful history; displayed elapsed duration uses a documented rule for leaving and re-entering In Progress, without double-counting or inventing active hours.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with web/TicketCard.tsx, web/TableView.tsx, src/types.ts, src/store.ts claims/history and CLI/MCP update interfaces. Prefer explicit reported data and disposable derived timers over writing a record every second. Related: #20 and #25.

### Human review / verification

Exercise a fresh report, missing estimate, stale/expired claim, blocker, and re-entry into In Progress with controlled timestamps. Reload and enable reduced motion; verify the labels never claim measured agent runtime.

before.body:
If the LLM has questions about a ticket, they can add a questionaire with multiple choice questions or text questions to a ticket and mark it as needing human feedback. 

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Let an agent attach a structured questionnaire to a ticket and request human input, keeping questions and answers in the ticket’s conversation.

### Scope and approach

Support one or more multiple-choice or free-text questions, an explicit needs-feedback state, and answering at the human’s pace. Store structured data durably in Markdown records/metadata and expose it through CLI/MCP context. Keep this distinct from mandatory ticket creation forms.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An agent can submit a questionnaire with stable question IDs, clear prompts, answer types, and optional recommended choices; users can provide custom text where choices are offered.
- [ ] The ticket appears in Needs you with a direct route to its unanswered questionnaire; a separate flag does not silently change its workflow stage.
- [ ] Questions never time out or disappear because the user pauses. Draft answers persist across closing/reopening and refresh, and can be submitted explicitly.
- [ ] No recommended/preselected option counts as an answer until the human submits; required unanswered questions remain visible.
- [ ] Submitted answers retain human attribution, question wording, and timestamps in the conversation, and are readable by agent context and wait-for-update workflows.
- [ ] Question edits/replacements and amended answers retain history; stale submissions do not overwrite a newer questionnaire, and resolving one request does not clear unrelated open questions.

### Implementation notes and related work

Extend src/types.ts, src/store.ts comments/context, src/server.ts, src/cli.ts/src/mcp.ts, web/RecordDetail.tsx and web/model.ts attention handling. Reuse the existing question/resolve flow where possible. Related: #26.

### Human review / verification

Submit a mixed questionnaire, leave it unanswered beyond ordinary UI timers, save a partial draft, reload, and finish later. Confirm that an agent receives the explicit answers and that a concurrent question edit triggers reconciliation.

before.body:
## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Approve work from the board or table without opening each ticket. Make scope approval and acceptance of completed work separate, clearly named actions.

### Scope and approach

Provide Approve scope for unapproved planned work, and Accept into Done for tickets in Review. Show the result inline. Batch actions share the selection model from #17. Scope approval alone should not silently select, start, or complete a ticket.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A human can approve a ticket’s scope from its card/row; approved and inherited-scope states are visually distinguishable.
- [ ] A human can accept a Review ticket into Done directly; its summary and evidence remain accessible before accepting.
- [ ] Selected tickets can receive the same eligible approval action with a visible selection count; ineligible items are identified rather than silently changed.
- [ ] Agent requests cannot approve scope or accept work into Done, including through the new bulk path.
- [ ] Stale revisions and partial failures are shown per ticket; successful changes retain human attribution and do not overwrite unrelated fields.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with web/TicketCard.tsx, web/TableView.tsx, web/ProjectPage.tsx and src/store.ts authority/history. Related: #17. Keep the two meanings of approval explicit in copy and action availability.

### Human review / verification

Approve scope on a single item and selected items, then accept a reviewed item. Check that status is unchanged by scope approval, agent calls remain rejected, and a stale item produces a clear result.

meta.title: Ability to quickly approve tickets without needing to click enter each one
meta.handoff: Implemented ticket #16 and committed as 5d57e0d. Grouped parent headers now provide the same quick scope-approval and Review-acceptance controls in board and table views, including summary/evidence access and explicit/inherited scope state. Archived parents and branch-change mode remain non-writable. Browser expectations now correctly distinguish the fixture creator from the web actor `You`. No board records or decisions were changed; worktree is clean.
meta.evidence: `npm run build` passed, including TypeScript checking and production bundling. Focused storage tests passed 4/4, covering authority, stale/inherited outcomes, field preservation, evidence retention, and identical-request replay. `git diff --check` passed. Playwright discovered all 5 approval-action browser tests, including board/table keyboard flows, grouped parents, inherited state, LAN UUID fallback, and mixed batch results. Browser execution could not start because the sandbox denied binding 127.0.0.1:4178 (`EPERM`). The prescribed `npm ci && npm run build && npm test` completed install/build, but `npm test` could not create tsx’s IPC socket (`EPERM`). Running the suite without tsx IPC produced 114/121 passing; all 7 failures require prohibited loopback/service binding. Commit: 5d57e0d.

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Connect overlapping tickets and consolidate genuine duplicates without losing their discussion, images, decisions, or history.

### Scope and approach

Support a lightweight Related tickets relationship and a separate explicit merge action that chooses a surviving ticket. Show a reviewable merge preview. Retain the source ticket as an archived duplicate pointing to the survivor rather than deleting its record; preserve original attribution and links.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Find related tickets by number/title, add or remove a relationship, and see reciprocal links in both details and agent context without treating related work as a blocking dependency.
- [ ] A merge preview identifies the survivor and source, content to preserve, and conflicts in parent, status, owner, priority, or acceptance criteria; conflicting metadata is not silently overwritten.
- [ ] The survivor retains access to source descriptions, comments, attachments/annotations, and decision/rule references with their original provenance. Existing links to the source still resolve and show the survivor.
- [ ] Source tickets are explicitly marked as duplicates and excluded from ordinary active views after merge; this does not claim the work was completed or accepted into Done.
- [ ] Incoming parent/dependency links are handled deliberately, with cycle/self-link validation, and both records retain an audit trail.

Relate two tickets, then preview and merge duplicates containing different comments/images and conflicting metadata. Follow old links, retrieve agent context, and simulate stale input. Confirm that no content or attribution disappears and no ticket is falsely accepted as Done.

meta.title: Need a way to clear trash

before.body:
## Visual feedback

[![Screenshot](/api/images/image-a4860976e73b1010/base)](#image=image-a4860976e73b1010)



## Backlog refinement

### Intended outcome

Permanently clear unwanted screenshots from Trash, including clearing the whole Trash in one action, and reclaim their local image/preview storage.

### Evidence and current behavior

The attached screenshot shows four selected items in Trash with Restore selected available and no permanent-delete action. Current trashImage only records trashedAt/trashedBy; it retains the base image, preview, annotations and links indefinitely.

### Proposed scope

Add Delete permanently for selected trashed screenshots and an Empty Trash action. Use an explicit confirmation preview with an exact count and image list. Preserve useful ticket/conversation references and annotation instructions through a small deletion record or equivalent placeholder; do not silently rewrite unrelated Markdown or delete linked tickets.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Trash offers Delete permanently for selected items and Empty Trash for all currently trashed items; the normal screenshot library continues to use reversible Move to Trash behavior.
- [ ] Confirmation names the exact images/count and explains that local image/preview files will be removed. Empty Trash clearly covers the entire Trash, even when a search filter is active; selection deletion covers only its explicit selection.
- [ ] Cancellation makes no changes. Confirmation freezes the candidate list and revisions; newly trashed images are not swept into an already-open confirmation.
- [ ] Only currently trashed images are eligible. An image restored or edited after the preview is rejected individually rather than being deleted with a stale revision.
- [ ] Successful deletion removes base/preview assets and removes the entry from the ordinary Trash list. Empty and repeated-delete states are handled consistently.
- [ ] Linked tickets and conversation prose remain intact. Their screenshot references clearly indicate permanent deletion, with retained written annotation context where available; a missing or purged image never crashes board/detail/context rendering.
- [ ] Partial failures identify confirmed deletions and remaining items without replaying uncertain destructive requests automatically. Controls prevent duplicate submissions.
- [ ] Existing backups are not modified. Export/restore handles deletion records consistently, and a pre-deletion backup can restore the original image and links through the existing restore workflow.
- [ ] Keyboard focus, confirmation defaults, narrow layouts and both density modes work. Tests exercise cancellation, filtered selection, full-Trash scope, concurrent restore/edit, missing files, linked images and partial failures using disposable assets.

### Implementation notes

Inspect src/media.ts, src/server.ts, src/types.ts, web/Screenshots.tsx and screenshot/context/backup consumers. Choose the deletion-record format during implementation and document the rationale; annotation metadata is Git-tracked, while image assets are local. Do not use real project screenshots for destructive tests.

### Human review

On disposable screenshots, compare deleting a selection with Empty Trash while filtered. Cancel once, then confirm. Check a ticket linked to a deleted screenshot, and restore an older backup in a disposable project. This ticket is refined into Backlog and still awaits scope approval; no screenshots have been deleted.

meta.title: Report progress as attributed estimates and current-session wall-clock time

before.body:
## Choice

The service stamps progress reports with the acting identity and timestamp. Optional percentages are bounded from 0 to 100 and labeled estimates. Entering an In Progress role from another role starts a new session timestamp; moves between In Progress columns retain the session. Prior sessions remain in record history. Displayed elapsed time is derived in the browser rather than written periodically to disk.

## Context and rationale

The tool coordinates agents but does not supervise their execution. A claim or recent report is not proof that an agent process is running. Expired claims and reports older than 30 minutes are labeled explicitly. A percentage, elapsed timer or completed checklist never moves a ticket to Done.

## Alternatives and tradeoffs

Tracking CPU/process time would require an agent execution supervisor outside this release. A lifetime timer would conflate separate implementation attempts. Existing tickets without a session timestamp show Start unknown until their next entry into In Progress; no start time is invented.

## Attribution

Implemented by Codex fixes within approved #28 scope; no new execution-supervision capability is implied.

## References

src/store.ts, web/ProgressReport.tsx, src/cli.ts, src/mcp.ts

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Approve work from the board or table without opening each ticket. Make scope approval and acceptance of completed work separate, clearly named actions.

### Scope and approach

Provide Approve scope for unapproved planned work, and Accept into Done for tickets in Review. Show the result inline. Batch actions share the selection model from #17. Scope approval alone should not silently select, start, or complete a ticket.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A human can approve a ticket’s scope from its card/row; approved and inherited-scope states are visually distinguishable.
- [ ] A human can accept a Review ticket into Done directly; its summary and evidence remain accessible before accepting.
- [ ] Selected tickets can receive the same eligible approval action with a visible selection count; ineligible items are identified rather than silently changed.
- [ ] Agent requests cannot approve scope or accept work into Done, including through the new bulk path.
- [ ] Stale revisions and partial failures are shown per ticket; successful changes retain human attribution and do not overwrite unrelated fields.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with web/TicketCard.tsx, web/TableView.tsx, web/ProjectPage.tsx and src/store.ts authority/history. Related: #17. Keep the two meanings of approval explicit in copy and action availability.

### Human review / verification

Approve scope on a single item and selected items, then accept a reviewed item. Check that status is unchanged by scope approval, agent calls remain rejected, and a stale item produces a clear result.

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Make workflow status customization easy to discover from the board and safe to use as the project evolves.

### Scope and approach

Settings already supports naming, roles, ordering, addition, and removal of columns. Expose a clear Customize statuses entry from the board and improve that existing editor. Retain stable IDs and explain why workflow roles control agent behavior; multiple columns can share a role, as Concept and Backlog do here.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A user can find status customization from the board, add a status, rename it, and change its order without editing configuration files.
- [ ] Renaming or reordering retains ticket associations, history, and saved views; refreshing preserves the configuration.
- [ ] The editor distinguishes display name from workflow role and validates required roles and invalid/blank names.
- [ ] Removing a populated status offers an explicit destination/migration flow or a clear route to move its tickets first; no tickets are orphaned.
- [ ] Where a role has multiple columns, default destinations for new tickets and agent role-based moves are visible and deterministic.
- [ ] Concurrent configuration changes cause reconciliation feedback rather than silent overwrites.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with web/Settings.tsx, web/ProjectPage.tsx, src/store.ts updateConfig and role-to-column lookups in src/cli.ts/src/mcp.ts. Extend existing configuration rather than introducing competing status data.

### Human review / verification

Add and rename a status, reorder it, reload, and remove an empty status. Exercise removal with tickets and ambiguous role destinations using Concept/Backlog and In Progress/Failed Review.

meta.title: Should be able to customize and change the statuses
meta.handoff: #18 implementation is present and committed at 37cbaa2 (following 8fc37e3). It adds board-level Customize statuses entry, status display-name/role editor, add/reorder/remove safeguards, deterministic role-default visibility, and explicit concurrent-config reconciliation with reload or three-way reapply.

Required `npm test` is blocked before discovery here by sandbox-denied tsx IPC socket (`listen EPERM`). The non-IPC network test reproduces the controller’s reported ENOENT because its child server cannot create its local service after the sandbox denies listening; browser regression is likewise blocked by `listen EPERM 127.0.0.1:4178`. No out-of-scope network/test changes were made.

Add and rename a status, reorder it, reload, and remove an empty status. Exercise removal with tickets and ambiguous role destinations using Concept/Backlog and In Progress/Failed Review.

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Provide a dedicated vertical planning view where dragging tickets changes the order in which work should be considered.

### Scope and approach

Build on the saved table view and existing manual/priority sorting. Offer an obvious Priority planning preset, rank tickets within priority groups, and allow explicit movement into another priority group. Ordering must not silently change workflow status or parent. Explain that priority is the urgency bucket and rank is the order within it.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The planning view shows a vertical list with priority groups and visible drag handles, including the start/end of each group.
- [ ] Dragging within a group changes persistent relative rank; dragging to another priority group updates priority and rank visibly.
- [ ] Reordering across tickets with different statuses does not move either ticket to the other status or change its parent.
- [ ] Move up/down and move-to-priority controls provide keyboard alternatives, including first/last positions.
- [ ] Reloading or returning to the saved view retains the order; concurrent reorder failures reconcile without losing tickets.
- [ ] Filtered reordering uses defined visible anchors and preserves the relative order of hidden tickets; saved sort modes clearly indicate whether manual reordering is active.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with web/ProjectPage.tsx place/peersOf, web/TableView.tsx and web/model.ts sortTickets. Current place also copies the target status, so reuse needs care. Coordinate drag preview with #22; prefer existing order metadata over a second competing ranking field.

### Human review / verification

Rank tickets across several stages and priorities, move to first/last, refresh, and repeat with a filter and keyboard controls. Confirm that status/parent stay unchanged and priority changes only when crossing an explicit priority group.

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Provide a dedicated vertical planning view where dragging tickets changes the order in which work should be considered.

### Scope and approach

Build on the saved table view and existing manual/priority sorting. Offer an obvious Priority planning preset, rank tickets within priority groups, and allow explicit movement into another priority group. Ordering must not silently change workflow status or parent. Explain that priority is the urgency bucket and rank is the order within it.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The planning view shows a vertical list with priority groups and visible drag handles, including the start/end of each group.
- [ ] Dragging within a group changes persistent relative rank; dragging to another priority group updates priority and rank visibly.
- [ ] Reordering across tickets with different statuses does not move either ticket to the other status or change its parent.
- [ ] Move up/down and move-to-priority controls provide keyboard alternatives, including first/last positions.
- [ ] Reloading or returning to the saved view retains the order; concurrent reorder failures reconcile without losing tickets.
- [ ] Filtered reordering uses defined visible anchors and preserves the relative order of hidden tickets; saved sort modes clearly indicate whether manual reordering is active.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with web/ProjectPage.tsx place/peersOf, web/TableView.tsx and web/model.ts sortTickets. Current place also copies the target status, so reuse needs care. Coordinate drag preview with #22; prefer existing order metadata over a second competing ranking field.

### Human review / verification

Rank tickets across several stages and priorities, move to first/last, refresh, and repeat with a filter and keyboard controls. Confirm that status/parent stay unchanged and priority changes only when crossing an explicit priority group.

If in progress would be nice to see how long llm has worked on ticket as well as estimated progress. 

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Make in-progress work easier to monitor with restrained animation, elapsed time, and agent-reported progress that clearly communicates uncertainty.

### Scope and approach

Show current owner/claim, last reported update, elapsed time since entering In Progress, and an optional agent-reported percentage or checklist progress. Elapsed wall-clock time is not measured active work. Running-agent supervision remains outside the initial product; animation must not imply a verified live process.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Cards/rows and ticket details show last reported activity and elapsed time with explicit labels; reload reconstructs elapsed time from durable timestamps.
- [ ] Agents can report a short progress note and optional bounded percentage through CLI/MCP; percentages are labeled estimates, and missing values display as unknown rather than invented.
- [ ] Checklist completion, if shown from #20, is labeled separately from overall completion; 100% never automatically moves a ticket to Done.
- [ ] Expired claims, stale reports, and blockers are visibly distinct from recent reported activity; the UI never treats a claim alone as proof an agent is running.
- [ ] Subtle in-progress animation respects reduced-motion preferences and stops or changes appropriately for blocked/stale/review/done states.
- [ ] Repeated work sessions retain useful history; displayed elapsed duration uses a documented rule for leaving and re-entering In Progress, without double-counting or inventing active hours.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with web/TicketCard.tsx, web/TableView.tsx, src/types.ts, src/store.ts claims/history and CLI/MCP update interfaces. Prefer explicit reported data and disposable derived timers over writing a record every second. Related: #20 and #25.

### Human review / verification

Exercise a fresh report, missing estimate, stale/expired claim, blocker, and re-entry into In Progress with controlled timestamps. Reload and enable reduced motion; verify the labels never claim measured agent runtime.

after.body:
If in progress would be nice to see how long llm has worked on ticket as well as estimated progress. 

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Make in-progress work easier to monitor with restrained animation, elapsed time, and agent-reported progress that clearly communicates uncertainty.

### Scope and approach

Show current owner/claim, last reported update, elapsed time since entering In Progress, and an optional agent-reported percentage or checklist progress. Elapsed wall-clock time is not measured active work. Running-agent supervision remains outside the initial product; animation must not imply a verified live process.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Cards/rows and ticket details show last reported activity and elapsed time with explicit labels; reload reconstructs elapsed time from durable timestamps.
- [ ] Agents can report a short progress note and optional bounded percentage through CLI/MCP; percentages are labeled estimates, and missing values display as unknown rather than invented.
- [ ] Checklist completion, if shown from #20, is labeled separately from overall completion; 100% never automatically moves a ticket to Done.
- [ ] Expired claims, stale reports, and blockers are visibly distinct from recent reported activity; the UI never treats a claim alone as proof an agent is running.
- [ ] Subtle in-progress animation respects reduced-motion preferences and stops or changes appropriately for blocked/stale/review/done states.
- [ ] Repeated work sessions retain useful history; displayed elapsed duration uses a documented rule for leaving and re-entering In Progress, without double-counting or inventing active hours.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with web/TicketCard.tsx, web/TableView.tsx, src/types.ts, src/store.ts claims/history and CLI/MCP update interfaces. Prefer explicit reported data and disposable derived timers over writing a record every second. Related: #20 and #25.

### Human review / verification

Exercise a fresh report, missing estimate, stale/expired claim, blocker, and re-entry into In Progress with controlled timestamps. Reload and enable reduced motion; verify the labels never claim measured agent runtime.

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Approve work from the board or table without opening each ticket. Make scope approval and acceptance of completed work separate, clearly named actions.

### Scope and approach

Provide Approve scope for unapproved planned work, and Accept into Done for tickets in Review. Show the result inline. Batch actions share the selection model from #17. Scope approval alone should not silently select, start, or complete a ticket.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A human can approve a ticket’s scope from its card/row; approved and inherited-scope states are visually distinguishable.
- [ ] A human can accept a Review ticket into Done directly; its summary and evidence remain accessible before accepting.
- [ ] Selected tickets can receive the same eligible approval action with a visible selection count; ineligible items are identified rather than silently changed.
- [ ] Agent requests cannot approve scope or accept work into Done, including through the new bulk path.
- [ ] Stale revisions and partial failures are shown per ticket; successful changes retain human attribution and do not overwrite unrelated fields.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with web/TicketCard.tsx, web/TableView.tsx, web/ProjectPage.tsx and src/store.ts authority/history. Related: #17. Keep the two meanings of approval explicit in copy and action availability.

### Human review / verification

Approve scope on a single item and selected items, then accept a reviewed item. Check that status is unchanged by scope approval, agent calls remain rejected, and a stale item produces a clear result.

- [ ] Reloading or returning to the saved view retains the order; concurrent reorder failures reconcile without losing tickets.

before.body:
## Intended outcome

Help a human review several agent submissions quickly with the handoff, current verification, changes and open questions visible together. Build on existing review controls rather than duplicating them.

## Acceptance criteria

Next/previous navigation preserves unsaved feedback; current versus historical evidence is explicit; accept/request-changes respects revisions and preserves discussion; unavailable PR/diff information is represented honestly; support keyboard and narrow screens.

## Scope

Recommendation from the local Kanban comparison. Awaiting human scope approval; no implementation started.

meta.title: Create a focused keyboard-friendly review queue

Queue evidence distinguishes missing diffs. Text editing retains native Option/Alt-arrow behavior. Merged on main 1797295 and installed in Control Room Dev and Juice Lab.
